 \le\|v\|^2-\gamma^2(1-q_{\rm eg})\|Jv\|^2\le\|v\|^2.
\end{equation}

\emph{One step.} Fix a worker, drop the index $i$, write $F_t=G(x_t)$,
and let $\mathbb E_t$ denote conditional expectation given the history before
the first batch of step $t$. The first batch gives $\mathbb E_te_t=0$ and
$\mathbb E_t\|e_t\|^2\le \alpha_{\rm rel}\|F_t\|^2$. Since $G$ is affine,
\[
 G(y_t)=F_t-\gamma J(F_t+e_t)=M_{{\rm eg},1}F_t-\gamma Je_t,
\]
and~\eqref{pv:H} yields
\begin{equation}\label{pv:corrector}
 \mathbb E_t\|G(y_t)\|^2
 =\|M_{{\rm eg},1}F_t\|^2+\gamma^2\mathbb E_t\|Je_t\|^2
 \le(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\|F_t\|^2.
\end{equation}
The second batch is centered given $y_t$, and its variance is at most
$\alpha_{\rm rel}\|G(y_t)\|^2$; hence
$\mathbb E_t\|\delta_t\|^2
\le \alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})
\|F_t\|^2$. Taking
the expectation given $z$ proves the last claim of the lemma.

\emph{Recursion for the operator.} By~\eqref{pv:algorithm},
\begin{equation}\label{pv:field-recursion}
 F_{t+1}=F_t-\gamma J\bigl(G(y_t)+\delta_t\bigr)
 =M_{\rm eg}F_t+\zeta_t,\qquad
 \zeta_t=\gamma^2J^2e_t-\gamma J\delta_t.
\end{equation}
We have $\mathbb E_t\zeta_t=0$. Because $\delta_t$ is centered given $e_t$, the
two terms of $\zeta_t$ are orthogonal in $L^2$, and
\begin{equation}\label{pv:field-variance}
 \mathbb E_t\|\zeta_t\|^2
 \le q_{\rm eg}^2\alpha_{\rm rel}\|F_t\|^2
 +q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel}
   (1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\|F_t\|^2
 =\vartheta_{\rm grow}\|F_t\|^2.
\end{equation}

\emph{Summation.} Unrolling~\eqref{pv:field-recursion} gives
$F_t=M_{\rm eg}^tG(z)+\sum_{j<t}M_{\rm eg}^{t-1-j}\zeta_j$.
The terms $\zeta_j$ are martingale differences, and
$M_{\rm eg}^tG(z)$ is fixed given $z$, so all cross terms vanish in
expectation. Using $\|M_{\rm eg}\|_{\rm op}\le1$
from~\eqref{pv:P} and~\eqref{pv:field-variance},
\[
 s_t=d_t+\sum_{j<t}\mathbb E\bigl[\|M_{\rm eg}^{t-1-j}\zeta_j\|^2\bigm|z\bigr]
 \le d_t+\vartheta_{\rm grow}\sum_{j<t}s_j.
\]
(The second moments are finite by induction on $t$, since every step is
affine in the previous iterate and the noise.) We claim that
\[
 s_t\le u_t:=d_t+\vartheta_{\rm grow}
       \sum_{j<t}(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{t-1-j}d_j .
\]
For $t=0$ this is $s_0=d_0$. If it holds for all $j<t$, then
$s_t\le d_t+\vartheta_{\rm grow}\sum_{j<t}u_j$, and
\[
 \sum_{j<t}u_j
 =\sum_{j<t}d_j\Bigl(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow}
       \sum_{l=j+1}^{t-1}(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{l-1-j}\Bigr)
 =\sum_{j<t}(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{t-1-j}d_j,
\]
which gives $s_t\le u_t$. The same identity with $t=T$ yields
\[
 \sum_{t<T}s_t\le\sum_{t<T}u_t
 =\sum_{j<T}(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{T-1-j}d_j
 \le(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{T-1}\sum_{j<T}d_j.
\]

\emph{The averaged iterate.} The noise is centered and the updates are
affine, so $\mathbb E[x_t^i-x_\star\mid z]=M_{\rm eg}^t(z-x_\star)$ for every $i$.
Since $J$ commutes with $M_{\rm eg}$,
$\mathbb E[G(\bar x_t)\mid z]
=JM_{\rm eg}^t(z-x_\star)=M_{\rm eg}^tG(z)$, and Jensen's
inequality gives $\mathbb E[\|G(\bar x_t)\|^2\mid z]\ge d_t$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{pv:block}
Assume SGC, $0<\gamma\le1/(4L)$, and
\begin{equation}\label{pv:condition}
 \frac{c_{\rm avg}(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{T-1}}{m}
 \le\frac{1-2q_{\rm eg}}2.
\end{equation}
Then the output of Definition~\ref{pv:definition} satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{pv:block-bound}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)\le\frac{3R_0^2}{\gamma NT}.
\end{equation}
For $\gamma=1/(4L)$ the bound is $12LR_0^2/(NT)$, and
condition~\eqref{pv:condition} reads
\begin{equation}\label{pv:explicit-condition}
 \alpha_{\rm rel}(35+\alpha_{\rm rel})
 \left(1+\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(18+\alpha_{\rm rel})}{256}\right)^{T-1}
 \le7m.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Within a round we may reveal, at each local step $t$, first the
predictor batches of all workers and then their corrector batches.
The responses are mutually independent across workers, so this order
does not change the joint law and respects every dependency.

\emph{The averaged trajectory.} Let bars denote averages over workers.
Since $G$ is affine, $G(\bar x)$ is the average of the $G(x^i)$, and
\[
 \bar y_t=\bar x_t-\gamma\bigl(G(\bar x_t)+\bar e_t\bigr),\qquad
 \bar x_{t+1}=\bar x_t-\gamma\bigl(G(\bar y_t)+\bar\delta_t\bigr).
\]
This is one extragradient step with errors $\bar e_t,\bar\delta_t$, so
identity~\eqref{nn:identity} and bound~\eqref{nn:pathwise-residual} of
Lemma~\ref{nn:identity-lemma}, with $F=G$, give for every
$u\in\mathbb R^d$
\begin{align}\label{pv:gap-identity}
 2\gamma\langle G(\bar y_t),\bar y_t-u\rangle
 \le{}&\|\bar x_t-u\|^2-\|\bar x_{t+1}-u\|^2
 +\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}
 -2\gamma\bigl\langle\bar\delta_t,\bar x_t-\gamma G(\bar y_t)-u\bigr\rangle,
\end{align}
where
\begin{equation}\label{pv:remainder}
 \overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}
 =-(1-2q_{\rm eg})\gamma^2\|G(\bar x_t)+\bar e_t\|^2
          +2\gamma^2\|\bar e_t\|^2+\gamma^2\|\bar\delta_t\|^2 .
\end{equation}

\emph{The remainder.} Condition on the round-start point $z$. The
errors of different workers are independent and centered, so
\[
 \mathbb E[\|\bar e_t\|^2\mid z]\le\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}s_t}m,\qquad
 \mathbb E[\|\bar\delta_t\|^2\mid z]
 \le\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}
 +q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})s_t}m,
\]
by Lemma~\ref{pv:field-lemma}. Since $\bar e_t$ is centered,
$\mathbb E[\|G(\bar x_t)+\bar e_t\|^2\mid z]
=\mathbb E[\|G(\bar x_t)\|^2\mid z]+\mathbb E[\|\bar e_t\|^2\mid z]$, and
Lemma~\ref{pv:field-lemma} gives
\[
 \frac{\mathbb E[\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}\mid z]}{\gamma^2}
 \le-(1-2q_{\rm eg})d_t
 +(1+2q_{\rm eg})\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}s_t}m
 +\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}
 +q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})s_t}m
 =-(1-2q_{\rm eg})d_t+\frac{c_{\rm avg}}{m}s_t.
\]
Summing over $t$ and using~\eqref{pv:field-energy}
and~\eqref{pv:condition},
\begin{equation}\label{pv:block-absorption}
 \mathbb E\Bigl[\sum_{t<T}\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}\Bigm|z\Bigr]
 \le\gamma^2\left(-(1-2q_{\rm eg})
 +\frac{c_{\rm avg}(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{T-1}}m\right)
 \sum_{t<T}d_t
 \le-\frac{(1-2q_{\rm eg})\gamma^2}2\sum_{t<T}d_t.
\end{equation}

\emph{Energy over all rounds.} Restore the round index $r$ and let
$\mathcal D_{\rm eg}=\sum_{r<N}\sum_{t<T}\mathbb E\|M_{\rm eg}^tG(z_r)\|^2$.
Take $u=x_\star$
in~\eqref{pv:gap-identity}. The left side is nonnegative by
monotonicity and $G(x_\star)=0$. The vector paired with $\bar\delta_t$ is
determined before the corrector batch, so the last term has zero mean.
Hence
$\mathbb E\|\bar x_{t+1}-x_\star\|^2\le\mathbb E\|\bar x_t-x_\star\|^2
+\mathbb E\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}$.
Since $\bar x_{r,0}=z_r$ and $\bar x_{r,T}=z_{r+1}$,
summing over $t$ and $r$ and using~\eqref{pv:block-absorption} gives
\begin{equation}\label{pv:global-energy}
 \mathbb E\|z_N-x_\star\|^2
 +\frac{(1-2q_{\rm eg})\gamma^2}2\,\mathcal D_{\rm eg}\le R_0^2.
\end{equation}

\emph{The corrector sum.} Ordered by $(r,t)$, the averaged correctors
$\bar\delta_{r,t}$ are martingale differences. By
Lemma~\ref{pv:field-lemma},
$\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})
\le c_{\rm avg}$, \eqref{pv:condition}
and~\eqref{pv:global-energy},
\begin{equation}\label{pv:martingale}
 \mathbb E\Bigl\|\sum_{r,t}\bar\delta_{r,t}\Bigr\|^2
 =\sum_{r,t}\mathbb E\|\bar\delta_{r,t}\|^2
 \le\frac{c_{\rm avg}(1+\vartheta_{\rm grow})^{T-1}}m\,
       \mathcal D_{\rm eg}
 \le\frac{1-2q_{\rm eg}}2\,\mathcal D_{\rm eg}
 \le\frac{R_0^2}{\gamma^2}.
\end{equation}

\emph{The gap.} Let $\|u-x_\star\|\le R_0$. Monotonicity gives
$\langle G(u),\bar y_t-u\rangle\le\langle G(\bar y_t),\bar y_t-u\rangle$.
Sum~\eqref{pv:gap-identity} over all $(r,t)$, drop
$-\|z_N-u\|^2$, use $\|x_0-u\|\le2R_0$, and write
$\bar x_{r,t}-\gamma G(\bar y_{r,t})-u
=(\bar x_{r,t}-\gamma G(\bar y_{r,t})-x_\star)+(x_\star-u)$. Since
$\widehat y$ is the average of the $\bar y_{r,t}$,
\begin{align}\label{pv:supremum}
 2\gamma NT\langle G(u),\widehat y-u\rangle
 \le{}&4R_0^2+\sum_{r,t}\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},r,t}
       +2\gamma R_0\Bigl\|\sum_{r,t}\bar\delta_{r,t}\Bigr\|\nonumber\\
 &-2\gamma\sum_{r,t}\bigl\langle\bar\delta_{r,t},
              \bar x_{r,t}-\gamma G(\bar y_{r,t})-x_\star\bigr\rangle.
\end{align}
The right side does not depend on $u$, so it also bounds
$2\gamma NT\,\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)$. In expectation, the second term is
nonpositive by~\eqref{pv:block-absorption}, the third is at most
$2\gamma R_0\cdot R_0/\gamma=2R_0^2$ by~\eqref{pv:martingale} and
Jensen's inequality, and the last has zero mean. Therefore
$2\gamma NT\,\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)\le6R_0^2$,
which is~\eqref{pv:block-bound}.

For $\gamma=1/(4L)$ we have $q_{\rm eg}=1/16$, $1-2q_{\rm eg}=7/8$,
$c_{\rm avg}=\alpha_{\rm rel}(35+\alpha_{\rm rel})/16$ and
$\vartheta_{\rm grow}=\alpha_{\rm rel}(18+\alpha_{\rm rel})/256$;
substituting these values
into~\eqref{pv:condition} gives~\eqref{pv:explicit-condition}.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{pv:comparison}
For all $m,K\ge1$ and $\rho\ge1$,
\begin{equation*}
 \beta\le1024\max\Bigl\{1,\frac K\rho,T_\star\Bigr\}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Write $K_{\rm eff}=K/\rho=\mathbb E Z_1$ and
$T_{\rm scale}=\max\{1,K_{\rm eff},T_\star\}$.
If $K=1$, then $\beta\le K=1$. If $m<1024$, then
$\beta\le\mathbb E\sum_iZ_i=mK_{\rm eff}\le1024K_{\rm eff}$. Assume from now on that $K\ge2$
and $m\ge1024$.

\emph{A horizon that satisfies the condition.} The function
$t\mapsto t\log(1+t/K_{\rm eff})$ increases from $0$ to $\infty$ on
$(0,\infty)$, so there is a unique $T_{\rm cont}>0$ with
\begin{equation*}
 T_{\rm cont}\log\Bigl(1+\frac {T_{\rm cont}}{K_{\rm eff}}\Bigr)
 =\frac14\log m.
\end{equation*}
Let $T=\lfloor\min\{K/2,T_{\rm cont}\}\rfloor$ and suppose $T\ge1$. Then
$K/(2T)\ge1$, so $b=\lfloor K/(2T)\rfloor\ge K/(4T)$ and
$\alpha_{\rm rel}\le\rho/b\le4T/K_{\rm eff}=4r_{\rm hor}$, where
$r_{\rm hor}=T/K_{\rm eff}$. Therefore
\[
 \frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(35+\alpha_{\rm rel})}{16}
 \le\frac{35}4r_{\rm hor}+r_{\rm hor}^2\le10(1+r_{\rm hor})^2,
 \qquad
 1+\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(18+\alpha_{\rm rel})}{256}
 \le1+\frac9{32}r_{\rm hor}+\frac{r_{\rm hor}^2}{16}
 \le(1+r_{\rm hor})^2.
\]
Since $T\le T_{\rm cont}$ and
$t\mapsto t\log(1+t/K_{\rm eff})$ is increasing,
$(1+r_{\rm hor})^{2T}=\exp\{2T\log(1+T/K_{\rm eff})\}\le\sqrt m$.
Hence
\begin{equation*}
 \frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(35+\alpha_{\rm rel})}{16}
 \left(1+\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(18+\alpha_{\rm rel})}{256}\right)^{T-1}
 \le10(1+r_{\rm hor})^{2T}\le10\sqrt m\le\frac7{16}m,
\end{equation*}
where the last step uses $m\ge1024$. This
is~\eqref{pv:explicit-condition}, so $T\le T_\star$. The inequality
$T\le T_\star$ also holds when $T=0$.

\emph{A tail bound for $\beta$.} The Chernoff bound for the binomial
law gives $\mathbb P\{Z_1\ge t\}\le(eK_{\rm eff}/t)^t$ for
$t\ge K_{\rm eff}$, and a union bound gives
$\mathbb P\{\max_iZ_i\ge t\}\le m(eK_{\rm eff}/t)^t$. Let
$t_0=4(K_{\rm eff}+T_{\rm cont}+1)$ and $c_0=\log4-1>0$.
For $t\ge t_0$ we have
$t\ge4(K_{\rm eff}+T_{\rm cont})$ and $t\ge4T_{\rm cont}$, so
\[
 \log\frac t{eK_{\rm eff}}
 \ge\log\frac{4(K_{\rm eff}+T_{\rm cont})}{eK_{\rm eff}}
 =\log\Bigl(1+\frac {T_{\rm cont}}{K_{\rm eff}}\Bigr)+c_0,
 \qquad
 t\log\Bigl(1+\frac {T_{\rm cont}}{K_{\rm eff}}\Bigr)
 \ge4T_{\rm cont}\log\Bigl(1+\frac {T_{\rm cont}}{K_{\rm eff}}\Bigr)
 =\log m .
\]
Hence $\mathbb P\{\max_iZ_i\ge t\}\le m\,e^{-\log m-c_0t}=e^{-c_0t}$, and
\begin{equation}\label{pv:tail-integration}
 \beta\le t_0+\int_{t_0}^\infty e^{-c_0t}\,dt
 \le t_0+\frac{e^{-4c_0}}{c_0}
 \le8(K_{\rm eff}+T_{\rm cont}+1).
\end{equation}

\emph{Conclusion.} If $T_{\rm cont}\le K/2$, then
$T=\lfloor T_{\rm cont}\rfloor$ and
$T_{\rm cont}<T+1\le T_\star+1\le2T_{\rm scale}$, so
\eqref{pv:tail-integration}
gives $\beta\le8(T_{\rm scale}+2T_{\rm scale}+T_{\rm scale})
=32T_{\rm scale}$. If $T_{\rm cont}>K/2$, then
$T=\lfloor K/2\rfloor\ge1$,
so $\lfloor K/2\rfloor\le T_\star$ and
$\beta\le K\le3\lfloor K/2\rfloor\le3T_{\rm scale}$. In all cases
$\beta\le1024T_{\rm scale}$.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
\emph{Upper bound.} The algorithm outputs the best of four
candidates, chosen by their parameter-based bounds: the initial point,
serial and common-query extragradient (Lemma~\ref{lem:relmm:upper}),
and, if $T_\star\ge1$, local extragradient with $T=T_\star$,
$b=\lfloor K/(2T_\star)\rfloor$ and $\gamma=1/(4L)$
(Lemma~\ref{pv:block}). Let $C_0\ge6$ be the constant of
Lemma~\ref{lem:relmm:upper} and
$T_{\rm scale}=\max\{1,K/\rho,T_\star\}$.

Suppose $mK/\rho>1$. The common-query bound is at most
$2C_0LR_0^2/N$, the serial bound is $C_0LR_0^2/(N\cdot K/\rho)$, and
the local bound is $12LR_0^2/(NT_\star)\le2C_0LR_0^2/(NT_\star)$.
Together with the initial point,
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat x)
 \le LR_0^2\min\Bigl\{1,\frac{2C_0}{NT_{\rm scale}}\Bigr\}
 \le LR_0^2\min\Bigl\{1,\frac{2048C_0}{N\beta}\Bigr\},
\]
where the last step is Lemma~\ref{pv:comparison}. This also covers
$K=1$ and $T_\star=0$, in which case
$T_{\rm scale}=\max\{1,K/\rho\}$.

Suppose $mK/\rho\le1$. Lemma~\ref{lem:clock:elementary} gives
$\beta\le mK/\rho$, and the common-query bound is at most
\[
 \frac{C_0LR_0^2}N\Bigl(1+\frac\rho{mK}\Bigr)
 \le\frac{2C_0LR_0^2}{N\cdot mK/\rho}
 \le\frac{2C_0LR_0^2}{N\beta}.
\]

In both cases
$\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat x)\le LR_0^2\min\{1,C_{\rm aff}/(N\beta)\}$,
where $C_{\rm aff}=2048C_0$. For $x>0$,
$\min\{1,C_{\rm aff}/x\}\le(C_{\rm aff}+1)/(1+x)$: if
$x\le C_{\rm aff}$ the left side is at most
$1\le(C_{\rm aff}+1)/(1+x)$, and if $x>C_{\rm aff}$ then
$C_{\rm aff}(1+x)\le(C_{\rm aff}+1)x$. Hence
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat x)\le\frac{(C_{\rm aff}+1)LR_0^2}{1+N\beta}
 \le\frac{64(C_{\rm aff}+1)LR_0^2}{1+ND_{\mathrm{info}}},
\]
by Theorem~\ref{thm:clock:asymptotic}. This holds in every dimension.

\emph{Lower bound.} Lemma~\ref{lem:relmm:masked} gives the matching
lower bound in dimension
$d_{\rm hard}\le1024mT_{\rm mask}^2\le1024m(KN)^2$,
with a single distribution of
instances that does not depend on the algorithm.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
\label{an:parallel-protocol}
For integers $b,T\ge1$ and a step size $\gamma>0$, every worker starts at
$x_0$ and performs $T$ steps of~\eqref{pv:algorithm} with batch size $b$,
without communication. At the end the workers send their running sums
and the method outputs
$\widehat y=\frac1{mT}\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{t<T}y_t^i$.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{an:parallel}
If $\alpha_{\rm rel}=(\rho-1)/b\le1/8$ and
$0<\gamma\le1/(4L)$, then the output of
Definition~\ref{an:parallel-protocol} satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{an:parallel-certificate}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)
 \le\frac{4R_0^2}{\gamma T}
       +\frac{5\gamma\sigma^2}{2mb}
       +\frac{\sqrt3\,\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mbT}}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for $\gamma=\min\{1/(4L),R_0\sqrt{mb}/(\sigma\sqrt T)\}$,
where the second entry is $+\infty$ if $\sigma=0$,
\begin{equation}\label{an:parallel-optimized}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)
 \le\frac{16LR_0^2}{T}+\frac{9\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mbT}}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
We have $q_{\rm eg}=\gamma^2L^2\le1/16$ and
$\alpha_{\rm rel}\le1/8$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{an:constants}
 \begin{aligned}
 1-2q_{\rm eg}&\ge\frac78,
 &c_{\rm avg}=\alpha_{\rm rel}(2+3q_{\rm eg}
   +q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})&\le\frac{281}{1024},
 &\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})
   &\le\frac{137}{1024},\\
 1+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel}&\le\frac{129}{128},
 &2+2q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel}&\le\frac{273}{128}.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
In particular $1-2q_{\rm eg}-c_{\rm avg}\ge1/2$ and
$2+2q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel}\le3$. All second moments are
finite by induction, since every step is affine in the previous iterate
and the noise; this justifies the expectations below.

\emph{One worker.} Let $F_t=G(x_t)$ and let $\mathbb E_t$ condition on the
history before step $t$. As in~\eqref{pv:corrector}, now with the
additional variance $\sigma_b^2$,
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E_t\|G(y_t)\|^2
 \le(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\|F_t\|^2
      +q_{\rm eg}\sigma_b^2,\qquad
 \mathbb E_t\|\delta_t\|^2
 \le\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})
      \|F_t\|^2+(1+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\sigma_b^2.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathcal R_{{\rm eg},t}$ be the remainder~\eqref{pv:remainder}
written for this worker.
Since $e_t$ is centered,
\begin{align*}
 \frac{\mathbb E_t\mathcal R_{{\rm eg},t}}{\gamma^2}
 & =-(1-2q_{\rm eg})\|F_t\|^2
   +(1+2q_{\rm eg})\mathbb E_t\|e_t\|^2+\mathbb E_t\|\delta_t\|^2\\
 & \le-(1-2q_{\rm eg}-c_{\rm avg})\|F_t\|^2
   +(2+2q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\sigma_b^2\\
 & \le-\frac12\|F_t\|^2+3\sigma_b^2.
\end{align*}
Apply~\eqref{pv:gap-identity} to this worker with $u=x_\star$; the left
side is nonnegative and the last term has zero mean. Summing over $t$,
\begin{equation}\label{an:parallel-local-energy}
 \sum_{t<T}\mathbb E\|G(x_t^i)\|^2
 \le\frac{2R_0^2}{\gamma^2}+6T\sigma_b^2
 \qquad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\end{equation}

\emph{The averaged trajectory.} Let bars denote averages over workers
and $V_{F,t}=\frac1m\sum_i\mathbb E\|G(x_t^i)\|^2$. Since $G$ is affine, the
averaged iterates follow one extragradient step with errors
$\bar e_t,\bar\delta_t$, so~\eqref{pv:gap-identity}
and~\eqref{pv:remainder} apply to them. The workers' errors are
independent and centered, hence
\[
 \mathbb E\|\bar e_t\|^2\le\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}V_{F,t}+\sigma_b^2}m,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E\|\bar\delta_t\|^2
 \le\frac{\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}
       +q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})V_{F,t}
       +(1+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\sigma_b^2}m,
\]
and, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{pv:block},
\[
 \mathbb E\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}
 \le-(1-2q_{\rm eg})\gamma^2\mathbb E\|G(\bar x_t)\|^2
 +\frac{\gamma^2}m\left(c_{\rm avg}V_{F,t}
 +(2+2q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\sigma_b^2\right).
\]
Drop the negative term and sum over $t$, using~\eqref{an:parallel-local-energy}
and~\eqref{an:constants} in the form $2c_{\rm avg}\le1$,
$6c_{\rm avg}+2+2q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel}\le5$,
$2\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})\le1/2$
and
$6\alpha_{\rm rel}(1+q_{\rm eg}+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel})
+1+q_{\rm eg}\alpha_{\rm rel}\le3$. The averaged correctors
are martingale differences, so
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{t<T}\mathbb E\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}
 &\le\frac{R_0^2}m+\frac{5\gamma^2T\sigma_b^2}m,
       \\
 \mathbb E\Bigl\|\sum_{t<T}\bar\delta_t\Bigr\|^2
 =\sum_{t<T}\mathbb E\|\bar\delta_t\|^2
 &\le\frac{R_0^2}{2m\gamma^2}+\frac{3T\sigma_b^2}m.
\end{align*}

\emph{The gap.} The argument leading to~\eqref{pv:supremum}, applied to
the single uninterrupted averaged trajectory, gives
\begin{align*}
 2\gamma T\,\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)
 &\le4R_0^2+\sum_{t<T}\mathbb E\overline{\mathcal R}_{{\rm eg},t}
       +2\gamma R_0\Bigl(\mathbb E\Bigl\|\sum_{t<T}\bar\delta_t\Bigr\|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}\\
 &\le4R_0^2+\frac{R_0^2}m+\frac{5\gamma^2T\sigma_b^2}m
       +2\gamma R_0\Bigl(\frac{R_0}{\gamma\sqrt{2m}}
       +\sigma_b\sqrt{\frac{3T}m}\Bigr)\\
 &\le(5+\sqrt2)R_0^2+\frac{5\gamma^2T\sigma_b^2}m
       +2\sqrt3\,\gamma R_0\sigma_b\sqrt{\frac Tm},
\end{align*}
where we used $\sqrt{x+y}\le\sqrt x+\sqrt y$ and $m\ge1$. Dividing by
$2\gamma T$, using $(5+\sqrt2)/2<4$ and $\sigma_b^2=\sigma^2/b$
proves~\eqref{an:parallel-certificate}.

For the given step size,
\[
 \frac1\gamma\le4L+\frac{\sigma_b\sqrt T}{R_0\sqrt m},\qquad
 \frac{\gamma\sigma_b^2}m\le\frac{\sigma_b R_0}{\sqrt{mT}}.
\]
Substituting into~\eqref{an:parallel-certificate} gives
$16LR_0^2/T$ plus
$(4+5/2+\sqrt3)\,\sigma_b R_0/\sqrt{mT}$, and
$4+5/2+\sqrt3<9$ proves~\eqref{an:parallel-optimized}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{an:mixed-explicit}
For every $m,K,N\in\mathbb N$ there is an algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} with
\begin{equation}\label{an:mixed-explicit-bound}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat x)
 \le\min\left\{LR_0^2,\
       \frac{512LR_0^2}{N}\min\Bigl\{\frac\rho K,1+\frac\rho{mK}\Bigr\}
       +\frac{18\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}\right\}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We combine two instances of Lemma~\ref{an:parallel} with the initial
point.

\emph{Independent trajectories.} Take
$b=\max\{1,\lceil8(\rho-1)\rceil\}$, so that
$\alpha_{\rm rel}=(\rho-1)/b\le1/8$ and
$b\le8\rho$, and $T=\lfloor KN/(2b)\rfloor$. Each worker runs its
trajectory across rounds, keeping an unfinished batch and its query
from one round to the next; it makes at most $K$ calls per round and
$2bT\le KN$ calls in total. If $T\ge1$, then $T\ge KN/(4b)$ and
$bT\ge KN/4$, and~\eqref{an:parallel-optimized} gives
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)
 \le\frac{64bLR_0^2}{KN}+\frac{18\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}
 \le\frac{512\rho LR_0^2}{KN}+\frac{18\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}.
\]
If $T=0$, then $KN<2b\le16\rho$, and the first term exceeds $LR_0^2$.

\emph{Common queries.} Let all workers query the same point and pool
their responses over
$r_{\rm cq}=\max\{1,\lceil8(\rho-1)/(mK)\rceil\}$ rounds per stage,
so that each stage averages $b_{\rm cq}=mKr_{\rm cq}$ responses and
$(\rho-1)/b_{\rm cq}\le1/8$. Perform
$T_{\rm cq}=\lfloor N/(2r_{\rm cq})\rfloor$ steps, and apply
Lemma~\ref{an:parallel} with one worker and batch size $b_{\rm cq}$.
If $T_{\rm cq}\ge1$, then $r_{\rm cq}T_{\rm cq}\ge N/4$ and
$r_{\rm cq}\le1+8\rho/(mK)\le8(1+\rho/(mK))$,
so
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat y)
 \le\frac{64r_{\rm cq}LR_0^2}{N}+\frac{18\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}
 \le\frac{512LR_0^2}{N}\Bigl(1+\frac\rho{mK}\Bigr)
       +\frac{18\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}.
\]
If $T_{\rm cq}=0$, then
$N<2r_{\rm cq}\le16(1+\rho/(mK))$, and the first term exceeds
$LR_0^2$.

The initial point satisfies $\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(x_0)\le LR_0^2$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:relmm:upper}). Outputting the candidate with the
smallest bound proves~\eqref{an:mixed-explicit-bound}.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{an:statistical}
Under~\eqref{an:noise}, in every dimension $d\ge2$,
\begin{equation*}
 \mathcal E_d^{\rm aff,mix}
 \ge\frac3{128}\min\left\{LR_0^2,\
                         \frac{\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}\right\}.
\end{equation*}
The hard instances are $L$-Lipschitz, have unique roots, and use a
Gaussian oracle whose variance equals $\sigma^2$ at every point.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
If $\sigma=0$ there is nothing to prove. Let $\sigma>0$,
$Q_{\rm tot}=mKN$, and
$\lambda=\min\{L,\sigma/(4R_0\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}})\}$. For
$\theta_{\rm test}\in\{-R_0,R_0\}$ and
$x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2$ define
\[
 G_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)
 =\bigl(\lambda(x_1-\theta_{\rm test}),\,Lx_2\bigr),\qquad
 \widehat G_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)
 =G_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)+(\sigma\zeta,0),
 \quad \zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
With $x_0=0$, the operator $G_{\theta_{\rm test}}$ is monotone and
$L$-Lipschitz, its unique root is
$x_{\star,\theta_{\rm test}}=(\theta_{\rm test},0)$, and
$\|x_0-x_{\star,\theta_{\rm test}}\|=R_0$. The oracle
satisfies~\eqref{an:noise}. For $d>2$, add coordinates on which the
operator is $Lx_j$ without noise.

\emph{Reduction to testing.} Give $\lambda$ to the algorithm, allow it
to communicate after every call, and let it make exactly $Q_{\rm tot}$
calls; this can only help it. Subtracting the known value $\lambda x_1$
from the first coordinate of each response leaves $Q_{\rm tot}$
independent $\mathcal N(-\lambda\theta_{\rm test},\sigma^2)$ observations,
and the other coordinates carry no information about $\theta_{\rm test}$.
Since $Q_{\rm tot}\lambda^2R_0^2/\sigma^2\le1/16$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-testing} shows that every test of the sign of
$\theta_{\rm test}$ based on the transcript errs with average probability
at least $3/8$. We use the test that declares the sign of $\widehat x_1$
(with either convention at $\widehat x_1=0$). When it errs,
$\widehat x_1$ and $\theta_{\rm test}$ lie on different sides of $0$, so
$|\widehat x_1-\theta_{\rm test}|\ge R_0$.

\emph{Gap on an error.} On this event put
$\Delta_{\rm test}=(R_0/2)
\operatorname{sign}(\widehat x_1-\theta_{\rm test})$ and
$u=x_{\star,\theta_{\rm test}}+(\Delta_{\rm test},0)$. Then
$\|u-x_{\star,\theta_{\rm test}}\|\le R_0$ and
$G_{\theta_{\rm test}}(u)=(\lambda\Delta_{\rm test},0)$. Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Gap}_{\star}^{\rm M}(\widehat x)
 \ge\langle G_{\theta_{\rm test}}(u),\widehat x-u\rangle
 =\lambda\Delta_{\rm test}
   (\widehat x_1-\theta_{\rm test}-\Delta_{\rm test})
 =\lambda\left(\frac{R_0}2|\widehat x_1-\theta_{\rm test}|
   -\frac{R_0^2}4\right)
 \ge\frac{\lambda R_0^2}4.
\]
The gap is nonnegative on the complementary event. Averaging over
$\theta_{\rm test}$,
\[
 \frac12\sum_{\theta_{\rm test}=\pm R_0}\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_\star^{\rm M}(\widehat x)
 \ge\frac38\cdot\frac{\lambda R_0^2}4
 =\frac{3\lambda R_0^2}{32}
 \ge\frac3{128}\min\left\{LR_0^2,
       \frac{\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}}\right\},
\]
and one of the two signs attains at least this average.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
\emph{Upper bound.} This is Corollary~\ref{an:mixed-explicit}, which
holds in every dimension.

\emph{Lower bound.} Let $G_{\rm hard}$ and $\widehat G_{\rm hard}$ be
the operator and the SGC oracle of Lemma~\ref{lem:relmm:masked}. Add one
coordinate with known operator $Lz_{\rm aux}$ and Gaussian noise:
\[
 G(z_{\rm hard},z_{\rm aux})
 =(G_{\rm hard}(z_{\rm hard}),Lz_{\rm aux}),\qquad
 \widehat G(z_{\rm hard},z_{\rm aux})
 =(\widehat G_{\rm hard}(z_{\rm hard}),Lz_{\rm aux}+\sigma\zeta),
 \qquad \zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1),
\]
with an independent $\zeta$ at every call. This operator is monotone and
$L$-Lipschitz and has a unique root at distance $R_0$ from the initial
point. Its conditional variance satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat G(z_{\rm hard},z_{\rm aux})\mid\mathcal F)
 \le(\rho-1)\|G_{\rm hard}(z_{\rm hard})\|^2+\sigma^2
 \le(\rho-1)\|G(z_{\rm hard},z_{\rm aux})\|^2+\sigma^2,
\]
so~\eqref{an:noise} holds, and its root variance equals $\sigma^2$. An
algorithm can generate the last coordinate of every response itself, so
the extension gives it no information, and comparators of the form
$(u,0)$ show that its gap is at least the gap of the original instance.
Hence~\eqref{pv:minimax-comparison} still holds.

Both this distribution and the one of Lemma~\ref{an:statistical} live in
dimension
\begin{equation*}
 d_{\rm mix}=\max\{d_{\rm hard}+1,2\}=O\bigl(m(KN)^2\bigr),
\end{equation*}
after padding with noiseless coordinates $Lx_j$. Let
$A_0=LR_0^2$, $A_{\rm info}=A_0/(1+ND_{\mathrm{info}})$ and
$R_{\rm stat}=\sigma R_0/\sqrt{mKN}$. The
equal mixture of the two distributions is a fixed distribution that
does not depend on the algorithm, and its expected loss is at least
\[
 \frac12\left(\frac{A_{\rm info}}{96}
       +\frac3{128}\min\{A_0,R_{\rm stat}\}\right)
 \ge\frac1{192}\bigl(A_{\rm info}+\min\{A_0,R_{\rm stat}\}\bigr)
 \ge\frac1{192}\min\{A_0,A_{\rm info}+R_{\rm stat}\}.
\]
Thus
\begin{equation}\label{an:combined-bound}
 \mathcal E_{d_{\rm mix}}^{\rm aff,mix}
 \ge\frac1{192}\min\left\{LR_0^2,\
       \frac{LR_0^2}{1+ND_{\mathrm{info}}}
       +\frac{\sigma R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}\right\}.
\end{equation}

\emph{Comparison.} Let $K_{\rm eff}=K/\rho$ and
$K_{\rm scale}=\max\{K_{\rm eff},\min\{1,mK_{\rm eff}\}\}$. Then
\[
 \frac1{K_{\rm scale}}
 =\min\Bigl\{\frac\rho K,\max\Bigl\{1,\frac\rho{mK}\Bigr\}\Bigr\}
 \le\min\Bigl\{\frac\rho K,1+\frac\rho{mK}\Bigr\}
 \le\frac2{K_{\rm scale}} .
\]
Moreover $D_{\mathrm{info}}\le(1+\log(2m)/\log2)K_{\rm scale}$: if
$mK_{\rm eff}\le1$, then
$K_{\rm scale}=mK_{\rm eff}$ and
$D_{\mathrm{info}}\le mK_{\rm eff}$ by definition; otherwise
$K_{\rm scale}\ge\max\{K_{\rm eff},1\}$ and
$D_{\mathrm{info}}\le K_{\rm eff}+\log(2m)/\log2
\le(1+\log(2m)/\log2)K_{\rm scale}$. The
upper bound of Corollary~\ref{an:mixed-explicit}, without its constants,
is, for a universal constant $C_{\rm cmp}>0$, bounded as follows. Define
\[
 R_{\rm alg}:=\frac{A_0}N
       \min\left\{\frac\rho K,1+\frac\rho{mK}\right\}+R_{\rm stat}.
\]
Then
\[
 \min\{A_0,R_{\rm alg}\}
 \le4\min\left\{A_0,\frac{A_0}{1+NK_{\rm scale}}+R_{\rm stat}\right\}
 \le C_{\rm cmp}\log(2m)
       \min\{A_0,A_{\rm info}+R_{\rm stat}\}.
\]
For the first inequality, if $NK_{\rm scale}\ge1$ then
$(A_0/N)\cdot2/K_{\rm scale}\le4A_0/(1+NK_{\rm scale})$, and if
$NK_{\rm scale}<1$ the
right side is at least $4\min\{A_0,A_0/2\}\ge A_0$. For the second,
$1+ND_{\mathrm{info}}
\le(1+\log(2m)/\log2)(1+NK_{\rm scale})$ and
$1+\log(2m)/\log2\le2\log(2m)/\log2$. Together
with~\eqref{an:combined-bound}, this proves the theorem.

\emph{The case $\rho=1$.} Then $D_{\mathrm{info}}=K$ and
$\min\{\rho/K,1+\rho/(mK)\}=1/K$. Since $KN\ge1$, we have
$KN\le1+KN\le2KN$, so the upper bound~\eqref{an:mixed-explicit-bound}
and the lower bound~\eqref{an:combined-bound} agree up to universal
constants, which proves~\eqref{eq:affine-uniform-specialization},
including $K=N=1$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{vi:affine-comparison}
For $r,\gamma>0$, the operator
\begin{equation}\label{vi:affine-chain}
 F_n(u,v)=\gamma\Bigl(D_n^\top v+\frac r{\sqrt n}e_1,\ -D_nu\Bigr)
\end{equation}
on $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n$ is monotone and $2\gamma$-Lipschitz, and its
root is $(0,-r\mathbf1/\sqrt n)$. On the product of two balls of radius
$r$ centered at $0$, the Minty gap and the primal--dual gap of
$\Phi_n(u,v)=\gamma(v^\top D_nu+ru_1/\sqrt n)$ coincide: for every
$(\widehat u,\widehat v)$ both equal
\begin{equation}\label{vi:affine-gap}
 \gamma\Bigl\{\frac r{\sqrt n}\widehat u_1+r\|D_n\widehat u\|
 +r\Bigl\|D_n^\top\widehat v+\frac r{\sqrt n}e_1\Bigr\|\Bigr\}
 \ \ge\ \frac{\gamma r}{\sqrt n}\Bigl|\widehat v_n+\frac r{\sqrt n}\Bigr|.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Write $F_n(z)=Az+h$ with $A(u,v)=\gamma(D_n^\top v,-D_nu)$ and
$h=\gamma(re_1/\sqrt n,0)$. The matrix $A$ is skew-symmetric, so $F_n$ is
monotone and $\|A\|=\gamma\|D_n\|\le2\gamma$. The root equation is
$D_n^\top v=-re_1/\sqrt n$ and $D_nu=0$, whose solution is $u=0$,
$v=-r\mathbf1/\sqrt n$.

\emph{Minty gap.} Since $\langle Aw,w\rangle=0$ and
$\langle Aw,\widehat z\rangle=-\langle w,A\widehat z\rangle$,
\[
 \langle F_n(w),\widehat z-w\rangle
 =\langle h,\widehat z\rangle+\langle w,-A\widehat z-h\rangle .
\]
Here $-A\widehat z-h=\gamma(-D_n^\top\widehat v-re_1/\sqrt n,\ D_n\widehat u)$,
and the supremum of $\langle w,\cdot\rangle$ over the product of balls is
$r$ times the sum of the norms of the two blocks. This gives the
expression in~\eqref{vi:affine-gap}.

\emph{Primal--dual gap.} Over $\|u\|,\|v\|\le r$,
\[
 \sup_v\Phi_n(\widehat u,v)-\inf_u\Phi_n(u,\widehat v)
 =\gamma\Bigl(r\|D_n\widehat u\|+\frac r{\sqrt n}\widehat u_1\Bigr)
 +\gamma r\Bigl\|D_n^\top\widehat v+\frac r{\sqrt n}e_1\Bigr\|,
\]
which is the same expression.

\emph{Lower bound.} By Cauchy--Schwarz,
$\|D_n\widehat u\|\ge|\mathbf1^\top D_n\widehat u|/\sqrt n
=|\widehat u_1|/\sqrt n$, so the first two terms have a nonnegative sum.
The coordinates of $D_n^\top\widehat v+re_1/\sqrt n$ sum to
$(D_n\mathbf1)^\top\widehat v+r/\sqrt n=\widehat v_n+r/\sqrt n$, so its
norm is at least $|\widehat v_n+r/\sqrt n|/\sqrt n$.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{vi:edge-lemma}
The function $E_\epsilon^\varsigma$ is $C^2$ and convex--concave. Its value
and gradient vanish on $\{|u|,|v|\le\epsilon\}$. Its second derivatives
satisfy $|\partial_{uu}E_\epsilon^\varsigma|,|\partial_{vv}E_\epsilon^\varsigma|\le512$
and $|\partial_{uv}E_\epsilon^\varsigma|\le82$, and every coordinate of
$\nabla E_\epsilon^\varsigma-\nabla(\varsigma uv)$ has absolute value at most
$274\epsilon$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Write $b,\zeta_{\rm edge},E$ for
$b_\epsilon,\zeta_\epsilon,E_\epsilon^\varsigma$.
By~\eqref{vi:psi-bounds}, $|\chi_{\rm edge}'|\le4$ and
$|\chi_{\rm edge}''|\le60$. From
\[
 b'(t)=\chi_{\rm edge}(t/\epsilon)
 +\frac t\epsilon\chi_{\rm edge}'(t/\epsilon),\qquad
 b''(t)=\frac1\epsilon\Bigl[2\chi_{\rm edge}'(t/\epsilon)
 +\frac t\epsilon\chi_{\rm edge}''(t/\epsilon)\Bigr]
\]
and $|t|\le2\epsilon$ on the support of $\chi_{\rm edge}(t/\epsilon)$ we get
\[
 |b|\le2\epsilon,\qquad |b'|\le1+2\cdot4=9,\qquad
 |b''|\le\frac{2\cdot4+2\cdot60}\epsilon=\frac{128}\epsilon .
\]
Since $b(t)=t$ for $|t|\le\epsilon$, the function $\zeta_{\rm edge}''$ is continuous,
even, nonnegative, bounded by $256$, and supported in
$\{\epsilon\le|t|\le2\epsilon\}$. Integrating from $0$ gives
$|\zeta_{\rm edge}'|\le256\epsilon$, and
$\zeta_{\rm edge}=\zeta_{\rm edge}'=0$ on $[-\epsilon,\epsilon]$. Direct
differentiation gives
\[
 \partial_{uu}E=\zeta_{\rm edge}''(u)-\varsigma b''(u)b(v),\qquad
 \partial_{vv}E=-\zeta_{\rm edge}''(v)-\varsigma b(u)b''(v),\qquad
 \partial_{uv}E=\varsigma\bigl[1-b'(u)b'(v)\bigr].
\]
Since $|b''(u)b(v)|\le2\epsilon|b''(u)|=\zeta_{\rm edge}''(u)$, we have
$\partial_{uu}E\ge0$, and similarly $\partial_{vv}E\le0$; hence $E$ is
convex--concave. The bounds give $|\partial_{uu}E|\le256+256=512$,
likewise for $\partial_{vv}E$, and $|\partial_{uv}E|\le1+81=82$. The
gradient error is
$\partial_uE-\varsigma v=-\varsigma b'(u)b(v)+\zeta_{\rm edge}'(u)$, of absolute value at
most $9\cdot2\epsilon+256\epsilon=274\epsilon$; the error
$\partial_vE-\varsigma u=-\varsigma b(u)b'(v)-\zeta_{\rm edge}'(v)$ obeys
the same bound. For $|u|,|v|\le\epsilon$, $b(u)=u$, $b(v)=v$ and
$\zeta_{\rm edge}=\zeta_{\rm edge}'=0$, so $E$ and $\nabla E$ vanish.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{vi:core-root}
The operator $G_\epsilon$ is monotone and $\ell$-Lipschitz with
$\ell=1200\lambda$, and
\begin{equation}\label{vi:uniform-core-error}
 \|G_\epsilon(z)-G_0(z)\|\le
 \Delta_{\rm op}:=548\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}
 \qquad(z\in\mathbb R^{d_{\rm ch}}).
\end{equation}
It has a root within distance $548n\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}$ of
$z_{\rm ref}$. If $0\le s<d_{\rm ch}$ and all coordinates of $z$ after position $s$ have absolute
value at most $\epsilon$, then $\Phi_\epsilon(z)$ and $G_\epsilon(z)$ depend
only on the first $s+1$ coordinates of $z$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
\emph{Monotonicity and Lipschitz constant.} The symmetric part of the
Jacobian of $G_\epsilon$ is
$\operatorname{diag}(\nabla^2_{uu}\Phi_\epsilon,-\nabla^2_{vv}\Phi_\epsilon)$,
which is positive semidefinite because every edge is convex--concave
(Lemma~\ref{vi:edge-lemma}). Every coordinate belongs to at most two
edges, so every row and every column of the Jacobian has absolute sum
at most $(2\cdot512+2\cdot82)\lambda=1188\lambda$. Hence the spectral norm
is at most $1188\lambda<\ell$.

\emph{Distance to the reference.} Each coordinate of $G_\epsilon-G_0$ is
$\lambda$ times the sum of at most two edge errors, each at most
$274\epsilon$ in absolute value. Hence every coordinate is at most
$548\lambda\epsilon$, which gives~\eqref{vi:uniform-core-error}.

\emph{A root.} The linear part of $G_0$ is
$A_{\rm ref}=\lambda\begin{psmallmatrix}0&D_n^\top\\-D_n&0\end{psmallmatrix}$,
and $D_n^{-1}$ is the upper triangular matrix of ones, so
$\|D_n^{-1}\|\le\|D_n^{-1}\|_F=\sqrt{n(n+1)/2}\le n$ and
$\|A_{\rm ref}^{-1}\|\le n/\lambda$. The continuous map
\[
 T(z)=z_{\rm ref}-A_{\rm ref}^{-1}\bigl(G_\epsilon(z)-G_0(z)\bigr)
\]
satisfies
$\|T(z)-z_{\rm ref}\|\le n\Delta_{\rm op}/\lambda
=548n\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}$, so by
Brouwer's theorem it has a fixed point $z$ in the ball of this radius
around $z_{\rm ref}$. Since $G_0(z)=A_{\rm ref}(z-z_{\rm ref})$, the fixed
point equation reads $G_0(z)=G_0(z)-G_\epsilon(z)$, that is,
$G_\epsilon(z)=0$.

\emph{Flatness.} Let all coordinates after position $s$ be at most
$\epsilon$. Every edge whose two coordinates are both after $s$
vanishes together with its gradient by Lemma~\ref{vi:edge-lemma}. The
remaining edges involve only the first $s+1$ coordinates.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{vi:operator-cutoff}
Let $G$ be continuously differentiable, monotone and $\ell$-Lipschitz,
with a root of norm at most $R_{\rm loc}>0$. Let
\[
 \theta(x)=\psi\Bigl(\frac{\|x\|-2R_{\rm loc}}{408R_{\rm loc}}\Bigr),\qquad
 V_{\rm loc}(x)=84\ell(\|x\|-R_{\rm loc})_+\frac x{\|x\|},\qquad
 \overline G=(1-\theta)G+V_{\rm loc},
\]
with $V_{\rm loc}(0)=0$. Then $\overline G$ is monotone and
$90\ell$-Lipschitz, it equals $G$ on $\{\|x\|\le R_{\rm loc}\}$ and the
known map $V_{\rm loc}$ on
$\{\|x\|\ge410R_{\rm loc}\}$, and it has the same root.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Write $t=\|x\|$. The map $V_{\rm loc}$ is the gradient of the convex function
$42\ell(t-R_{\rm loc})_+^2$, so it is monotone. For $t>R_{\rm loc}$ its Jacobian has the
eigenvalue $84\ell$ in the radial direction and $84\ell(1-R_{\rm loc}/t)$ in the
tangential directions.

\emph{The region $t\le2R_{\rm loc}$.} Here $\theta=0$ and
$\overline G=G+V_{\rm loc}$, which
is monotone and $(\ell+84\ell)$-Lipschitz.

\emph{The annulus $2R_{\rm loc}\le t\le410R_{\rm loc}$.}
By~\eqref{vi:psi-bounds},
$\|\nabla\theta\|\le4/(408R_{\rm loc})$, and since the root has norm at
most $R_{\rm loc}$,
$\|G(x)\|\le\ell(t+R_{\rm loc})\le411\ell R_{\rm loc}$. Hence
$\|G(x)\nabla\theta(x)^\top\|\le4\cdot411\ell/408<5\ell$. The Jacobian
\[
 \mathrm D\overline G=(1-\theta)\mathrm DG-G\nabla\theta^\top
 +\mathrm D V_{\rm loc}
\]
has symmetric part at least $(0-5\ell+42\ell)I\succeq0$, because
$\mathrm DG$ has positive semidefinite symmetric part and the tangential
eigenvalues of $\mathrm D V_{\rm loc}$ are at least
$84\ell(1-R_{\rm loc}/(2R_{\rm loc}))=42\ell$. Its
norm is at most $\ell+5\ell+84\ell=90\ell$.

\emph{The region $t\ge410R_{\rm loc}$.} Here $\theta=1$ and
$\overline G=V_{\rm loc}$.

The map $\overline G$ is continuous and piecewise continuously
differentiable, so integrating its Jacobian along segments gives global
monotonicity and the Lipschitz constant $90\ell$. For $t\le R_{\rm loc}$,
$\theta=0$ and $V_{\rm loc}=0$, so $\overline G=G$; in particular the root is
preserved.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{vi:product-cutoff}
Let $d_{\rm amb}\ge1$, and let $\Psi$ be $C^2$ and convex--concave on
$\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}\times\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}$,
with $\ell$-Lipschitz gradient, $\Psi(0)=0$ and
$\|\nabla\Psi(0)\|\le\ell R_{\rm loc}$. The function
\begin{equation}\label{vi:localized-game}
 \overline\Phi(u,v)=\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)\Psi(u,v)
 +P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)-P_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)
\end{equation}
is $C^2$ and convex--concave, and its gradient is $356\ell$-Lipschitz. If
$\Psi$ has a saddle point $z_\star$ with $\|z_\star\|<R_{\rm loc}$, then $z_\star$
is a saddle point of $\overline\Phi$ and
$|\overline\Phi(z_\star)|\le3\ell R_{\rm loc}^2/2$. Moreover, with
$r=R_{\rm loc}/2$,
\begin{equation}\label{vi:one-sided-values}
 \overline\Phi(u,v)\ge\Psi(u,v)\quad(\|v\|\le r),\qquad
 \overline\Phi(u,v)\le\Psi(u,v)\quad(\|u\|\le r).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Let $\chi(u,v)=\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)$; it vanishes
unless $\|u\|,\|v\|\le410R_{\rm loc}$, where
$\|(u,v)\|\le580R_{\rm loc}$.

\emph{Size of $\Psi$ on the support.} Integrating the Lipschitz
gradient from $0$,
\[
 \|\nabla\Psi(z)\|\le\ell R_{\rm loc}+\ell\|z\|
 \le581\ell R_{\rm loc},\qquad
 |\Psi(z)|\le\ell R_{\rm loc}\|z\|+\tfrac\ell2\|z\|^2
 \le169000\ell R_{\rm loc}^2 .
\]
The mask bounds give $\|\nabla\chi\|\le6/(408R_{\rm loc})$ and
$\|\nabla^2\chi\|\le76/(408R_{\rm loc})^2$, where the diagonal blocks contribute
at most $60$ and the mixed blocks at most $16$ in units of
$(408R_{\rm loc})^{-2}$. By the product rule,
\begin{equation}\label{vi:cutoff-hessian}
 \|\nabla^2(\chi\Psi)\|
 \le\ell\Bigl(1+\frac{2\cdot6\cdot581}{408}+\frac{76\cdot169000}{408^2}\Bigr)<100\ell .
\end{equation}

\emph{Convexity in $u$.} If $\|u\|\le2R_{\rm loc}$, then
$\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)=1$ and
$\nabla^2_{uu}(\chi\Psi)=\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)\nabla^2_{uu}\Psi\succeq0$,
while $\nabla^2P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)\succeq0$ because
$P_{R_{\rm loc}}$ is a nondecreasing convex function of the convex function
$\|u\|-R_{\rm loc}$. If $\|u\|\ge2R_{\rm loc}$, then
$\|u\|-R_{\rm loc}\ge R_{\rm loc}>R_{\rm loc}/100$, and the smallest
eigenvalue of $\nabla^2P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)$ is its tangential eigenvalue
\[
 256\ell\,\frac{q_{R_{\rm loc}/100}'(\|u\|-R_{\rm loc})}{\|u\|}
 =256\ell\Bigl(1-\frac{R_{\rm loc}+R_{\rm loc}/200}{\|u\|}\Bigr)
 \ge256\ell\Bigl(1-\frac{201}{400}\Bigr)=127.36\,\ell,
\]
which exceeds the bound $100\ell$ of~\eqref{vi:cutoff-hessian}.
Concavity in $v$ follows in the same way from $-P_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)$. The
Hessian of $P_{R_{\rm loc}}$ has norm at most $256\ell$, so the gradient
of $\overline\Phi$ is $(100+256)\ell$-Lipschitz. All pieces are $C^2$:
$P_{R_{\rm loc}}$ vanishes near the center of each ball, and the masks are
constant near $\|w\|=2R_{\rm loc}$ and $\|w\|=410R_{\rm loc}$.

\emph{The saddle point.} If $\|z_\star\|<R_{\rm loc}$, the masks equal one
and $P_{R_{\rm loc}}$, $\nabla P_{R_{\rm loc}}$ vanish in a neighbourhood
of $z_\star$, so
$\nabla\overline\Phi(z_\star)=\nabla\Psi(z_\star)=0$, and
$|\overline\Phi(z_\star)|=|\Psi(z_\star)|
\le\ell R_{\rm loc}^2+\ell R_{\rm loc}^2/2$.

\emph{One-sided comparison.} Let $\|v\|\le r$, so
$\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)=1$ and $P_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)=0$, and
$\overline\Phi-\Psi=P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)
-(1-\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(u))\Psi(u,v)$. If
$\|u\|\le2R_{\rm loc}$, this is $P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)\ge0$. If
$t=\|u\|\ge2R_{\rm loc}$, then
\[
 |\Psi(u,v)|\le\ell\Bigl(\frac{t^2}2
 +\frac{3R_{\rm loc}t}2+\frac{5R_{\rm loc}^2}8\Bigr)
 \le6\ell(t-R_{\rm loc})^2,
 \qquad
 P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)\ge126.72\,\ell(t-R_{\rm loc})^2,
\]
so $P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)\ge(1-\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(u))\Psi(u,v)$. This proves the first inequality;
the second follows by exchanging the roles of $u$ and $v$.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{vi:haar}
Let $R_{\rm cut},\epsilon>0$, and consider an algorithm whose queries and
output have norm at most $R_{\rm cut}$ on every transcript. If
\[
 d_{\rm amb}\ge d_{\rm ch}
 +\frac{2R_{\rm cut}^2}{\epsilon^2}\log(32mKNd_{\rm ch}),
\]
then, jointly over the frame, the bits and the algorithm's randomness,
the following event has probability at least $5/8$: $S_N\le k$, and all
queries and the output have hidden coordinates after position $k$ of
absolute value at most $\epsilon$. For two independent $n$-frames, used
for the two blocks of a saddle problem with $d_{\rm ch}=2n$ and the interleaved
order, the same holds if every query and output block has norm at most
$R_{\rm cut}$ and
$d_{\rm amb}\ge n+2R_{\rm cut}^2\epsilon^{-2}\log(32mKNd_{\rm ch})$.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Fix the bits and the algorithm's randomness; only the frame is random.

\emph{A fictitious oracle.} For a call of worker $i$ in round $r$ at slot
$j$, let
\[
 s=\min\Bigl\{d_{\rm ch},\
 \sum_{r'<r}\max_{i'}\sum_{j'=1}^KB_{{\rm mask},r',i',j'}
 +\sum_{j'<j}B_{{\rm mask},r,i,j'}\Bigr\}.
\]
Let $c'=\min\{d_{\rm ch},s+1\}$, let $w^{(c')}$ keep the first $c'$ hidden
coordinates of the query and set the others to $0$, and let $\pi_{c'}$ keep
the first $c'$ components of a vector of $\mathbb R^{d_{\rm ch}}$. The
fictitious oracle returns $0$ if $B_{{\rm mask},r,i,j}=0$, and otherwise
\[
 \frac1p\,U_{\le c'}\,\pi_{c'}G\bigl(w^{(c')}\bigr),
 \qquad U_{\le c'}=(U_1,\ldots,U_{c'}).
\]
The projection $\pi_{c'}$ is needed because an edge with one large
coordinate has a nonzero output in its other coordinate, so
$G(w^{(c')})$ itself may have a nonzero component $c'+1$. With it, an
informative response depends on the frame only through
$U_1,\ldots,U_{c'}$. By induction over calls, every query of the
fictitious transcript depends on the frame only through
$U_1,\ldots,U_s$: an informative response adds at most one column, and at
a communication the workers share their prefixes, which are nested, so
the longest one is kept. Hence the fictitious output depends only on the
first $\min\{d_{\rm ch},S_N\}$ columns.

\emph{One hidden coordinate.} Let $x$ be a fictitious query or the
output, with $\|x\|\le R_{\rm cut}$, and let $U_i$ be a column not yet used,
$i>s$. Conditionally on $U_1,\ldots,U_s$, the column $U_i$ is uniform on
the unit sphere of the orthogonal complement of these columns, of
dimension $d_{\rm amb}-s\ge d_{\rm amb}-d_{\rm ch}$. For a uniform unit
vector $\vartheta$ in dimension $n'$ and a fixed $y$ with
$\|y\|\le R_{\rm cut}$,
$\mathbb E\langle\vartheta,y\rangle^{2j}\le(2j-1)!!\,R_{\rm cut}^{2j}/n'^j$ and the odd
moments vanish, so
\[
 \mathbb E e^{t\langle\vartheta,y\rangle}
 \le\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{t^{2j}(2j-1)!!\,R_{\rm cut}^{2j}}{(2j)!\,n'^j}
 =\sum_{j\ge0}\frac1{j!}\Bigl(\frac{t^2R_{\rm cut}^2}{2n'}\Bigr)^j
 =e^{t^2R_{\rm cut}^2/(2n')} .
\]
The Chernoff bound and the assumption on $d_{\rm amb}$ give
\[
 \mathbb P\bigl\{|\langle U_i,x\rangle|>\epsilon\bigm|U_1,\ldots,U_s\bigr\}
 \le2e^{-(d_{\rm amb}-d_{\rm ch})\epsilon^2/(2R_{\rm cut}^2)}
 \le\frac1{16mKNd_{\rm ch}}.
\]
For two frames, condition on both prefixes and apply the same bound in
the block of each query, whose remaining dimension is at least
$d_{\rm amb}-n$.

\emph{Union bound.} For every fictitious query, with its prefix length
$s$ at the time of the call, consider all hidden coordinates $i>s$; for the
fictitious output consider all $i>\min\{d_{\rm ch},S_N\}$. Since the bits are fixed,
these index sets are deterministic, and the vector is determined by the
columns of its prefix, so the previous bound applies to each pair. There
are at most $(mKN+1)d_{\rm ch}\le2mKNd_{\rm ch}$ pairs, hence define
$\Omega_{\rm good}$ as the event that all these coordinates are at most
$\epsilon$ in absolute value; it has probability
at least $7/8$. Together with~\eqref{vi:clock-event}, the event
$\Omega_{\rm good}\cap\{S_N\le k\}$ has probability at least
$7/8-1/4=5/8$. On it,
the final prefix has length at most $k$, so the output has all hidden
coordinates after position $k$ bounded by $\epsilon$.

\emph{The true transcript.} On $\Omega_{\rm good}$, every query has hidden
coordinates after its prefix $s$ bounded by $\epsilon$. Then all edges with
both coordinates after $s$ vanish, including the edge between $s+1$ and
$s+2$, so $G(U^\top x)$ is supported on the first $c'$ coordinates and
coincides with $\pi_{c'}G(w^{(c')})$. Hence the true response equals the
fictitious one at every informative call, and both are $0$ otherwise. By
induction the true and fictitious transcripts coincide. Unused calls
can be padded by ignored queries, so the bound covers every algorithm
with at most $K$ calls per worker and round.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{vi:uvi-lower}
Let $m,K,N\ge1$, $\rho\ge1$, $L,D>0$, $p=1/\rho$, $k$ as in
Section~\ref{vi:haar-subsection}, $n=k+1$, and
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 d_{\rm ch}=2n,\quad r=\frac D4,\quad
 R_{\rm loc}=2r,\quad R_{\rm cut}=410R_{\rm loc},\\
 \lambda=\frac L{120000},\quad\ell=1200\lambda=\frac L{100},\quad
 \epsilon=\frac r{2000000\,n\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
If the ambient dimension satisfies
$d_{\rm amb}\ge d_{\rm ch}
+2R_{\rm cut}^2\epsilon^{-2}\log(32mKNd_{\rm ch})$, then every algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} on $\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}$ has an instance with a
monotone $L$-Lipschitz operator, a root in $B(0,D)$ and an
oracle satisfying SGC with equality, such that
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}^{\rm M}_{B(0,D)}(\widehat z)
 \ge\frac{LD^2}{122880000\,(1+ND_{\mathrm{info}})}.
\end{equation*}
Every realization of the oracle is a monotone, $\rho L$-Lipschitz
operator with the same root, and the bound holds even if the bit
$B_{\rm mask}$ is revealed with every response.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
\emph{The instance.} Take the chain~\eqref{vi:robust-chain} with these
parameters. By Lemma~\ref{vi:core-root} it has a root $z_\epsilon$ with
$\|z_\epsilon-z_{\rm ref}\|\le548n\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}
=548r/2000000<r/4$, and
$\|z_{\rm ref}\|=a_{\rm ch}\sqrt n=r$, so
$\|z_\epsilon\|\le5r/4<R_{\rm loc}$. For a frame
$U$, let $G_U(x)=UG_\epsilon(U^\top x)$, which is monotone and
$\ell$-Lipschitz, and let $F_U=(1-\theta)G_U+V_{\rm loc}$ be its localization from
Lemma~\ref{vi:operator-cutoff}. Then $F_U$ is monotone and
$90\ell\le L$-Lipschitz, and $Uz_\epsilon$ is a root with
$\|Uz_\epsilon\|<R_{\rm loc}\le D$.

\emph{Interior outputs.} Let $\|x\|<R_{\rm cut}$ and let the hidden coordinates
$U^\top x=(\widehat u,\widehat v)$ after position $k=n-1$ be at most
$\epsilon$; in particular $|\widehat v_n|\le\epsilon$. Test on
$Z_r=\{U(u,v):\|u\|,\|v\|\le r\}$, which lies in
$B(0,\sqrt2r)\subseteq B(0,R_{\rm loc})$, where
$F_U=G_U$. For
$w=U(u,v)\in Z_r$,
$\langle F_U(w),x-w\rangle=\langle G_\epsilon(u,v),U^\top x-(u,v)\rangle$.
By Lemma~\ref{vi:affine-comparison} with $\gamma=\lambda$ and
$\epsilon\le r/(4\sqrt n)$, the reference operator $G_0$ gives
\[
 \sup_{(u,v)}\langle G_0(u,v),U^\top x-(u,v)\rangle
 \ge\frac{\lambda r}{\sqrt n}\Bigl(\frac r{\sqrt n}-\epsilon\Bigr)
 \ge\frac{3\lambda r^2}{4n}.
\]
By~\eqref{vi:uniform-core-error}, replacing $G_0$ by $G_\epsilon$ changes
each tested inner product by at most
\[
 \Delta_{\rm op}\bigl(\|U^\top x\|+\sqrt2r\bigr)
 \le548\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}\,(820r+\sqrt2r)
 \le\frac{548\cdot822}{2000000}\cdot\frac{\lambda r^2}n<\frac{\lambda r^2}{4n}.
\]
Hence $\operatorname{Gap}^{\rm M}_{B(0,D)}(x)\ge\lambda r^2/(2n)$.

\emph{Exterior outputs.} Let $\|x\|\ge R_{\rm cut}$,
$u_{\rm rad}=x/\|x\|$, and test at
$w=2R_{\rm loc}u_{\rm rad}$, with $\|w\|=D$. There $\theta(w)=0$,
$V_{\rm loc}(w)=84\ell R_{\rm loc}u_{\rm rad}$, and
$\|G_U(w)\|\le\ell\|U^\top w-z_\epsilon\|
\le\ell(2R_{\rm loc}+R_{\rm loc})=3\ell R_{\rm loc}$. Since
$x-w=(\|x\|-2R_{\rm loc})u_{\rm rad}$,
\[
 \langle F_U(w),x-w\rangle
 \ge(84-3)\ell R_{\rm loc}(\|x\|-2R_{\rm loc})
 \ge81\cdot408\,\ell R_{\rm loc}^2\ge\frac{\lambda r^2}{2n}.
\]

\emph{Oracle and simulation.} At every call the oracle draws an independent bit
$B_{\rm mask}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)$ and returns
$B_{\rm mask}F_U/p$ and $B_{\rm mask}$. It is unbiased,
$\mathbb E\|B_{\rm mask}F_U/p\|^2=\rho\|F_U\|^2$,
and every realization is a nonnegative multiple of $F_U$. We simulate
the algorithm by one that sees only the hidden chain: its oracle returns
$B_{\rm mask}G_U/p$ and $B_{\rm mask}$. At a query with
$\|x\|<R_{\rm cut}$ the
simulator makes the same query and returns
$(1-\theta(x))\cdot B_{\rm mask}G_U(x)/p
+B_{\rm mask}V_{\rm loc}(x)/p$; at a query
with $\|x\|\ge R_{\rm cut}$ it queries $0$, uses only the bit and returns
$B_{\rm mask}V_{\rm loc}(x)/p$. Its output is the original output if this has norm
below $R_{\rm cut}$ and $0$ otherwise. All its queries and its output have
norm at most $R_{\rm cut}$, so Lemma~\ref{vi:haar} applies to it; on the event of the
lemma, the output of the original algorithm is either interior with
small hidden coordinates or exterior.

\emph{Conclusion.} The gap is nonnegative, because the test set contains
the root. By the remark after Lemma~\ref{vi:haar}, some fixed frame gives
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}^{\rm M}_{B(0,D)}(\widehat z)\ge\frac{\lambda r^2}{4n}
 =\frac{LD^2}{7680000\,n}\ge\frac{LD^2}{30720000\,(1+N\beta_p)},
\]
since $n=k+1\le4N\beta_p+1\le4(1+N\beta_p)$. Finally
$1+N\beta_p\le4(1+ND_{\mathrm{info}})$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:clock:asymptotic}.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{vi:sp-lower}
Let $k,n,d_{\rm ch}$ be as in Theorem~\ref{vi:uvi-lower}, and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{\rm loc}&=\frac D{2\sqrt2},&
 r&=\frac{R_{\rm loc}}2,&
 \ell&=\frac L{400},&
 \lambda&=\frac L{480000},\\
 \epsilon&=\frac r{2000000\,n\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}},&
 d_{\rm amb}&\ge n+\frac{2(410R_{\rm loc})^2}{\epsilon^2}
 \log(32mKNd_{\rm ch}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Every algorithm of Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} on
$\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}\times\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}$ has a $C^2$
convex--concave instance with
$L$-Lipschitz saddle operator and an oracle satisfying SGC with
equality, such that, for
$\mathcal Z_{\rm test}=B(0,2R_{\rm loc})
\times B(0,2R_{\rm loc})\subseteq B(0,D)$,
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{\mathcal Z_{\rm test}}^{\rm M}(\widehat z)\ \text{ and }\
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{\mathcal Z_{\rm test}}^{\rm PD}(\widehat z)
 \ \ge\ \frac{LD^2}{983040000\,(1+ND_{\mathrm{info}})}.
\end{equation*}
The same instance works for both gaps. Every sample function is
convex--concave with a $\rho L$-Lipschitz saddle operator and the same
saddle point, and the bound holds even if sample values and the bit
$B_{\rm mask}$ are revealed.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
\emph{The instance.} For independent $n$-frames $U,V$ in
$\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}$, let
$\Psi(u,v)=\Phi_\epsilon(U^\top u,V^\top v)$ and
$\Psi_0(u,v)=\Phi_0(U^\top u,V^\top v)$, and let $\overline\Phi$
be~\eqref{vi:localized-game}. Since $\ell=1200\lambda$, Lemma~\ref{vi:core-root} shows that $\Psi$
has $\ell$-Lipschitz gradient; moreover $\Psi(0)=0$ and
$\|\nabla\Psi(0)\|=\lambda a_{\rm ch}\le\ell R_{\rm loc}$, because every edge has zero
gradient at the origin. Its saddle point has norm below
$R_{\rm loc}$ by Lemma~\ref{vi:core-root}. Lemma~\ref{vi:product-cutoff} shows that
$\overline\Phi$ is $C^2$ and convex--concave, that its saddle operator
$\overline F$ is $356\ell\le L$-Lipschitz, and that the saddle point
$z_\star=(u_\star,v_\star)$ is preserved and lies in $\mathcal Z_{\rm test}$.

\emph{Interior outputs.} Let both output blocks have norm below
$410R_{\rm loc}$
and all hidden coordinates
$(\widetilde u,\widetilde v)=(U^\top\widehat u,V^\top\widehat v)$ after
position $k$ be at most $\epsilon$; in particular
$|\widetilde v_n|\le\epsilon$. On the product of hidden balls of radius $r$
(a subset of $\mathcal Z_{\rm test}$ on which $\overline\Phi=\Psi$),
Lemma~\ref{vi:affine-comparison} bounds both gaps of $\Psi_0$ below by
$\lambda r^2/n-\lambda r\epsilon/\sqrt n$. For the Minty gap, replacing
the operator of $\Psi_0$ by that of $\Psi$ changes each tested inner
product by at most
\[
 \Delta_{\rm op}\sqrt2\,(410R_{\rm loc}+r)<1200\,r\Delta_{\rm op}
 =\frac{657600}{2000000}\cdot\frac{\lambda r^2}n .
\]
For the primal--dual gap, apply~\eqref{vi:one-sided-values}: it suffices
to compare $\Psi$ with $\Psi_0$, and since $\Psi-\Psi_0$ vanishes at
the origin and has gradient norm at most $\Delta_{\rm op}$, the two value errors sum
to at most
\[
 2(410R_{\rm loc}+r)\Delta_{\rm op}
 =\frac{899816}{2000000}\cdot\frac{\lambda r^2}n .
\]
The term $\lambda r\epsilon/\sqrt n$ is at most
$\lambda r^2/(2000000\,n)$. In both cases the total loss is below
$\lambda r^2/(2n)$, so both gaps are at least $\lambda r^2/(2n)$.

\emph{Exterior outputs.} Suppose
$\|\widehat u\|\ge410R_{\rm loc}$. Testing at
$u_\star$ and $v_\star$ gives
\[
 \operatorname{Gap}^{\rm PD}_{\mathcal Z_{\rm test}}(\widehat z)
 \ge\overline\Phi(\widehat u,v_\star)-\overline\Phi(u_\star,\widehat v)
 \ge P_{R_{\rm loc}}(\widehat u)-|\overline\Phi(z_\star)|
 \ge256\ell\Bigl(\frac{(409R_{\rm loc})^2}2
 -\frac{409R_{\rm loc}^2}{200}\Bigr)-\frac{3\ell R_{\rm loc}^2}2,
\]
which exceeds $\lambda r^2/(2n)$ by a large margin; the case
$\|\widehat v\|\ge410R_{\rm loc}$ is symmetric. For the Minty gap, test at
$u_{\rm test}=2R_{\rm loc}\widehat u/\|\widehat u\|$ and
$v_{\rm test}=2R_{\rm loc}\widehat v/\|\widehat v\|$ (a zero
block is tested at $0$). There the masks equal one with zero gradients,
every nonzero radial block of $\overline F$ has norm
$256\ell(R_{\rm loc}-R_{\rm loc}/200)=254.72\,\ell R_{\rm loc}$, and the
localized core operator has norm at most
$\ell(\|(u_{\rm test},v_{\rm test})\|+R_{\rm loc})\le4\ell R_{\rm loc}$.
With $R_{\rm sum}=\|\widehat u\|+\|\widehat v\|
\ge410R_{\rm loc}$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\langle\overline F(u_{\rm test},v_{\rm test}),
 \widehat z-(u_{\rm test},v_{\rm test})\rangle\\
 &\quad\ge\bigl(254.72\,\ell R_{\rm loc}R_{\rm sum}
 -1018.88\,\ell R_{\rm loc}^2\bigr)
 -4\ell R_{\rm loc}(R_{\rm sum}+3R_{\rm loc})\\
 &\quad\ge101469\,\ell R_{\rm loc}^2>\frac{\lambda r^2}{2n}.
 \end{aligned}
\]

\emph{Oracle and simulation.} At every call the oracle draws an independent
$B_{\rm mask}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)$ and returns the value and the
saddle operator of $B_{\rm mask}\overline\Phi/p$, together with
$B_{\rm mask}$. A simulator with access to $B_{\rm mask}\Psi/p$ reproduces a
response at an interior query from one response at the same query, by the
product rule. At an exterior query at least one mask vanishes with its
derivatives, so the response is a known function of the query and the
bit, and the simulator queries $0$ to obtain the bit. All queries of the
simulator have blocks of norm at most $410R_{\rm loc}$, and its output is the
original output if interior and $0$ otherwise. The two-frame version of
Lemma~\ref{vi:haar} applies, since $\Psi$ has the flatness property for
values and gradients.

\emph{Conclusion.} Both gaps are nonnegative, because $\mathcal Z_{\rm test}$
contains the saddle point. Some fixed pair of frames gives,
simultaneously for both gaps,
\[
 \min\left\{
  \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{\mathcal Z_{\rm test}}^{\rm M}(\widehat z),
  \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{\mathcal Z_{\rm test}}^{\rm PD}(\widehat z)
 \right\}
 \ge\frac{\lambda r^2}{4n}
 \ge\frac{LD^2}{245760000\,(1+N\beta_p)},
\]
using $r^2=D^2/32$ and $n\le4(1+N\beta_p)$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:clock:asymptotic} gives $1+N\beta_p\le4(1+ND_{\mathrm{info}})$.
Each sample function $B_{\rm mask}\overline\Phi/p$ is convex--concave, has
the same saddle point, and has a $\rho L$-Lipschitz saddle operator.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{vi:strong-core}
The vector $w$ with $w_i=cq_{\rm geo}^{i-1}$,
$i=1,\ldots,d_{\rm ch}$, is the root
of~\eqref{vi:strong-affine}, and $\|w\|=R_0/2$. Let
$\phi_\epsilon(t)=q_\epsilon(|t|-\epsilon)$ with $q_\delta$
from~\eqref{vi:smooth-hinge}, and
\begin{equation*}
 \Psi_\epsilon(u,v)=\lambda\Bigl[-\frac c{q_{\rm geo}}u_1
 +\sum_{i=1}^nE_\epsilon^{+1}(u_i,v_i)
 +\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}E_\epsilon^{-1}(u_{i+1},v_i)
 -q_{\rm geo}\phi_\epsilon(v_n)\Bigr].
\end{equation*}
Its saddle operator $G_{\mu,\epsilon}$ is monotone and $\ell$-Lipschitz, has the
flatness property of Lemma~\ref{vi:core-root}, and satisfies
\[
 \|G_{\mu,\epsilon}-(F_0-\mu I)\|
 \le550\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}},\qquad
 \Psi_\epsilon(0)=0,\qquad
 G_{\mu,\epsilon}(0)=-\frac{\lambda c}{q_{\rm geo}}e_1 .
\]
The operator $F_\epsilon=\mu I+G_{\mu,\epsilon}$ has a unique root
$z_{\mu,\epsilon}$,
and
\begin{equation}\label{vi:strong-root-shift}
 \|z_{\mu,\epsilon}-w\|\le\frac{550\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}}{\mu}
 \le\frac{550}{10000}R_0q_{\rm geo}^k<\frac{R_0}{16},\qquad
 \|z_{\mu,\epsilon}\|\le\frac{9R_0}{16}<R_{\rm loc}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
\emph{The root of the reference.} Using
$\lambda q_{\rm geo}^2+\mu q_{\rm geo}-\lambda=0$,
the first row of $F_0(w)$ is
$\mu c+\lambda cq_{\rm geo}-\lambda c/q_{\rm geo}
=(c/q_{\rm geo})(\lambda q_{\rm geo}^2+\mu q_{\rm geo}-\lambda)=0$,
every interior row is
$-\lambda w_{i-1}+\mu w_i+\lambda w_{i+1}
=cq_{\rm geo}^{i-2}(-\lambda+\mu q_{\rm geo}
+\lambda q_{\rm geo}^2)=0$, and the last row is
$-\lambda w_{d_{\rm ch}-1}+(\mu+\lambda q_{\rm geo})w_{d_{\rm ch}}=0$
for the same reason. Moreover
$\|w\|^2=c^2\sum_{i<d_{\rm ch}}q_{\rm geo}^{2i}
=c^2(1-q_{\rm geo}^{2d_{\rm ch}})/(1-q_{\rm geo}^2)=R_0^2/4$.

\emph{The terminal term.} The function $\phi_\epsilon$ is even, convex and
$C^2$, it vanishes on $[-\epsilon,\epsilon]$, $0\le\phi_\epsilon''\le1$, and
$\phi_\epsilon'(t)=\operatorname{sign}(t)(|t|-\epsilon)^2/(2\epsilon)$ for
$\epsilon<|t|<2\epsilon$ and $\operatorname{sign}(t)(|t|-3\epsilon/2)$ for
$|t|\ge2\epsilon$. Hence $|\phi_\epsilon'(t)-t|\le3\epsilon/2$ for all $t$.
The term $-q_{\rm geo}\phi_\epsilon(v_n)$ is concave in $v$ and flat near $0$.

\emph{The operator $G_{\mu,\epsilon}$.} As in Lemma~\ref{vi:core-root}, the
Jacobian has row and column sums at most
$(2\cdot512+2\cdot82+1)\lambda=1189\lambda<\ell$, its symmetric part is
positive semidefinite, and the flatness property holds. The edges
contribute at most $548\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}$ to
$\|G_{\mu,\epsilon}-(F_0-\mu I)\|$ and the terminal at most
$3\lambda q_{\rm geo}\epsilon/2
\le2\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}$. The values at $0$ follow
from the definitions.

\emph{The root.} The operator $F_\epsilon$ is $\mu$-strongly monotone and
$(\mu+\ell)$-Lipschitz, so for $\eta=\mu/(\mu+\ell)^2$ the map
$T(z)=z-\eta F_\epsilon(z)$ satisfies
\[
 \|T(z)-T(y)\|^2\le\bigl(1-2\eta\mu+\eta^2(\mu+\ell)^2\bigr)\|z-y\|^2
 =\Bigl(1-\frac{\mu^2}{(\mu+\ell)^2}\Bigr)\|z-y\|^2 ,
\]
and Banach's fixed point theorem gives a unique root $z_{\mu,\epsilon}$. Since
$F_0(w)=0$, $\|F_\epsilon(w)\|
=\|G_{\mu,\epsilon}(w)-(F_0-\mu I)(w)\|\le
550\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}$, and strong monotonicity gives
$\mu\|z_{\mu,\epsilon}-w\|^2
\le\langle F_\epsilon(w),w-z_{\mu,\epsilon}\rangle\le
\|F_\epsilon(w)\|\,\|z_{\mu,\epsilon}-w\|$. Substituting $\epsilon$,
\[
 \frac{550\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}}\mu
 =\frac{550}{10000}\cdot\frac{\lambda}{\mu+\lambda}R_0q_{\rm geo}^k
 \le\frac{550}{10000}R_0q_{\rm geo}^k,
\]
and $\|z_{\mu,\epsilon}\|\le R_0/2+R_0/16$.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{vi:strong-lower}
For the parameters~\eqref{vi:strong-params} and
$d_{\rm amb}\ge n+2(410R_{\rm loc})^2\epsilon^{-2}
\log(32mKNd_{\rm ch})$, every algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} on
$\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}\times\mathbb R^{d_{\rm amb}}$ has a $C^2$,
$\mu$-strongly convex--concave instance with $L$-Lipschitz saddle
operator, a root $z_\star$ with $\|z_\star\|\le R_0$, and an oracle
satisfying SGC with equality, such that
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\ge\frac{R_0^2q_{\rm geo}^{2k}}{50}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
\emph{The instance.} For independent $n$-frames $U,V$ let
$\Psi(u,v)=\Psi_\epsilon(U^\top u,V^\top v)$ and
\begin{equation*}
 \overline\Phi(u,v)=\frac\mu2(\|u\|^2-\|v\|^2)
 +\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)\chi_{R_{\rm loc}}(v)\Psi(u,v)
 +P_{R_{\rm loc}}(u)-P_{R_{\rm loc}}(v).
\end{equation*}
Since $\|\nabla\Psi(0)\|=\lambda c/q_{\rm geo}
\le\ell R_{\rm loc}$, the part of
Lemma~\ref{vi:product-cutoff} that does not use a saddle point applies:
the localized residual is $C^2$, convex--concave, and has
$356\ell$-Lipschitz gradient. Adding the quadratic makes $\overline\Phi$
$\mu$-strongly convex--concave, and its saddle operator $\overline F$ is
$(\mu+356\ell)$-Lipschitz, where
$\mu+356\ell=\mu+\frac{356}{400}(L-\mu)\le L$. The point
$z_\star=(Uu_{\mu,\epsilon},Vv_{\mu,\epsilon})$, where
$z_{\mu,\epsilon}=(u_{\mu,\epsilon},v_{\mu,\epsilon})$,
has norm at most $9R_0/16<R_{\rm loc}$, where the masks equal one and
$P_{R_{\rm loc}}$
vanishes; there $\overline F(z_\star)=0$, so $z_\star$ is the unique
saddle point.

\emph{Interior outputs.} Let both output blocks have norm below
$410R_{\rm loc}$
and the hidden coordinates after position $k$ be at most $\epsilon$.
Projecting onto the frames,
\[
 \|\widehat z-z_\star\|
 \ge\|w_{>k}\|-\|z_{\mu,\epsilon}-w\|-\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}},
 \qquad w_{>k}=(w_{k+1},\ldots,w_{d_{\rm ch}}).
\]
Since $d_{\rm ch}-k=k+2\ge d_{\rm ch}/2$, we have
$q_{\rm geo}^{4(d_{\rm ch}-k)}\le q_{\rm geo}^{2d_{\rm ch}}$, hence
$1-q_{\rm geo}^{2d_{\rm ch}}
\le(1-q_{\rm geo}^{2(d_{\rm ch}-k)})(1+q_{\rm geo}^{2(d_{\rm ch}-k)})
\le2(1-q_{\rm geo}^{2(d_{\rm ch}-k)})$ and
\[
 \|w_{>k}\|^2=\frac{R_0^2}4\,q_{\rm geo}^{2k}\,
 \frac{1-q_{\rm geo}^{2(d_{\rm ch}-k)}}{1-q_{\rm geo}^{2d_{\rm ch}}}
 \ge\frac{R_0^2}8\,q_{\rm geo}^{2k}.
\]
By~\eqref{vi:strong-root-shift} and the choice of $\epsilon$,
$\|z_{\mu,\epsilon}-w\|+\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}
\le(551/10000)R_0q_{\rm geo}^k$. Since
$1/(2\sqrt2)>1/3$ and $1/3-551/10000>1/5$,
\begin{equation}\label{vi:strong-good-event}
 \|\widehat z-z_\star\|\ge\frac{R_0q_{\rm geo}^k}5 .
\end{equation}

\emph{Exterior outputs.} If a block has norm at least
$410R_{\rm loc}\ge410R_0$, then
$\|\widehat z-z_\star\|\ge410R_0-9R_0/16>R_0q_{\rm geo}^k/5$.

\emph{Oracle and simulation.} The oracle returns the value and saddle
operator of $B_{\rm mask}\overline\Phi/p$ and the bit $B_{\rm mask}$, with
an independent $B_{\rm mask}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)$; it is unbiased and
$\mathbb E\|B_{\rm mask}\overline F/p\|^2=\rho\|\overline F\|^2$. As in the proof
of Theorem~\ref{vi:sp-lower}, a simulator with access to
$B_{\rm mask}\Psi/p$
answers every interior query with one call at the same point and every
exterior query with one call at $0$; the term $\mu z$ is known. Its
queries and output have blocks of norm at most $410R_{\rm loc}$, and $\Psi$ has
the flatness property, so the two-frame version of Lemma~\ref{vi:haar}
applies. Some fixed pair of frames gives~\eqref{vi:strong-good-event}
probability at least $1/2$, hence
$\mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
\ge\frac12(R_0q_{\rm geo}^k/5)^2=R_0^2q_{\rm geo}^{2k}/50$.
Every sample function $B_{\rm mask}\overline\Phi/p$ is convex--concave
and has the same saddle point.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{vi:strong-exponent}
Let $\kappa=L/\mu\ge2$. In the setting of Theorem~\ref{vi:strong-lower},
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 \ge\frac{R_0^2}{50}\exp\Bigl[-\frac{15372800\,N}{\kappa}D_{\mathrm{info}}\Bigr].
\]
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
With $x=\mu/(2\lambda)$ we have
$1/q_{\rm geo}=x+\sqrt{x^2+1}$, so
$\log(1/q_{\rm geo})=\operatorname{arsinh}(x)\le x$ and
$q_{\rm geo}^{2k}\ge e^{-k\mu/\lambda}$.
Since $k\le4N\beta_p$ and $\lambda=(L-\mu)/480400$,
\[
 \frac{k\mu}\lambda\le\frac{1921600\,N\beta_p}{\kappa-1}
 \le\frac{3843200\,N\beta_p}{\kappa},
\]
where we used $1/(\kappa-1)\le2/\kappa$ for $\kappa\ge2$. Finally
$\beta_p\le4D_{\mathrm{info}}$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:clock:asymptotic}, and
Theorem~\ref{vi:strong-lower} gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:smr-schedules}
Run the serial or the common-query schedule
of~\eqref{vi:all-budget-schedules} with the step sizes of
Proposition~\ref{nn:strong-distance} for $N\ge1$ rounds from a point $x$,
and return $x$ if the schedule makes no complete step. The output
$\widehat z$ satisfies, respectively,
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 &\le96\Bigl[\|x-z_\star\|^2e^{-3NK_{\rm ser}/(640\kappa)}
      +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2KN}\Bigr],\\
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 &\le96\Bigl[\|x-z_\star\|^2e^{-3NK_{\rm cq}/(640\kappa)}
      +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mKN}\Bigr].
\end{align*}
The bounds also hold conditionally on a random starting point $x$.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Consider the serial schedule with batch size $b\le4\rho$ and
$T_{\rm sd}=\lfloor KN/(2b)\rfloor$ steps. If $KN\ge4b$, this is the
first case in the proof of Proposition~\ref{nn:strong-distance}. If
$KN<4b$, then $NK_{\rm ser}/\kappa<16\mu/L\le16$, so
$\|x-z_\star\|^2\le e^{3/40}\|x-z_\star\|^2
 e^{-3NK_{\rm ser}/(640\kappa)}$. If moreover
$T_{\rm sd}=0$, the output is $x$. If $T_{\rm sd}\ge1$,
\eqref{nn:strong-trajectory} gives the bias $\|x-z_\star\|^2$ at most and
the variance $\frac{1932}{81}\cdot\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2bT_{\rm sd}}$, and
$bT_{\rm sd}\ge b>KN/4$. In all cases the first bound holds. The
common-query schedule is treated in the same way with
$s_{\rm cq}\le5/K_{\rm cq}$ rounds per stage: if $N<4s_{\rm cq}$, then
$NK_{\rm cq}<20$, and if $T_{\rm cq}\ge1$, then
$mKs_{\rm cq}T_{\rm cq}\ge mKs_{\rm cq}>mKN/4$. The step sizes depend only on the
horizon and known parameters, which gives the conditional version.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:strong-mixed-hybrid}
For all integers $m,K,N\ge1$ there is an algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main}. Set $c_{\rm hyb}:=1/640$ and
$C_{\rm hyb}:=3\cdot96^2$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:smr-hybrid}
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\le C_{\rm hyb}\min\Bigl\{R_0^2,\quad
 R_0^2e^{-c_{\rm hyb}N(K_{\rm ser}+K_{\rm cq})/\kappa}
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mKN}
   \bigl[1+m\,e^{-c_{\rm hyb}NK_{\rm cq}/\kappa}\bigr]\Bigr\}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
The bound $R_0^2$ is attained by $z_0$; the algorithm returns $z_0$ if
this is the smaller bound.

\emph{One round.} For $N=1$ we run the serial schedule. Since
$K_{\rm cq}\le1\le\kappa$, we have
$e^{-c_{\rm hyb}K_{\rm cq}/\kappa}\ge e^{-c_{\rm hyb}}$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:smr-schedules} and $3/640\ge c_{\rm hyb}$ give
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 \le96\Bigl[R_0^2e^{-c_{\rm hyb}K_{\rm ser}/\kappa}
      +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2K}\Bigr]
 \le96e^{c_{\rm hyb}}\Bigl[
 R_0^2e^{-c_{\rm hyb}(K_{\rm ser}+K_{\rm cq})/\kappa}
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mK}\,m\,
   e^{-c_{\rm hyb}K_{\rm cq}/\kappa}\Bigr],
\]
which is~\eqref{eq:smr-hybrid}.

\emph{Two phases.} Let $N\ge2$, $N_s=\lfloor N/2\rfloor$ and
$N_c=N-N_s$; both are at least $N/3$. Run the serial schedule from $z_0$
for $N_s$ rounds and let $z_{\rm mid}$ be its output; it is broadcast at the end
of round $N_s$. Then run the common-query schedule from $z_{\rm mid}$ for $N_c$
rounds. Each phase uses at most $K$ calls per worker and round, and the
two phases use $N$ rounds. By Lemma~\ref{lem:smr-schedules},
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\|z_{\rm mid}-z_\star\|^2
 &\le96\Bigl[R_0^2e^{-3N_sK_{\rm ser}/(640\kappa)}
      +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2KN_s}\Bigr],
 \label{eq:smr-first-phase}\\
 \mathbb E\bigl[\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\bigm|z_{\rm mid}\bigr]
 &\le96\Bigl[\|z_{\rm mid}-z_\star\|^2e^{-3N_cK_{\rm cq}/(640\kappa)}
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mKN_c}\Bigr].
 \label{eq:smr-second-phase}
\end{align}
Taking the expectation of~\eqref{eq:smr-second-phase} and
inserting~\eqref{eq:smr-first-phase},
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 \le96^2R_0^2e^{-3(N_sK_{\rm ser}+N_cK_{\rm cq})/(640\kappa)}
 +\frac{96^2\sigma^2}{\mu^2KN_s}
   e^{-3N_cK_{\rm cq}/(640\kappa)}
 +\frac{96\sigma^2}{\mu^2mKN_c}.
\]
With $N_s,N_c\ge N/3$, the exponents are at least
$N(K_{\rm ser}+K_{\rm cq})/(640\kappa)$ and
$NK_{\rm cq}/(640\kappa)$, and $1/(KN_s)\le3m/(mKN)$,
$1/(mKN_c)\le3/(mKN)$. This gives~\eqref{eq:smr-hybrid}.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:smr-statistical}
In every dimension $d\ge2$, every algorithm of Definition~\ref{def:ic-main}
has an instance with a $\mu$-strongly monotone $L$-Lipschitz operator,
$\|z_0-z_\star\|\le R_0$, and an oracle with variance $\sigma^2$ at every point,
so that Assumption~\ref{ass:mixed} holds for every $\rho\ge1$, such that
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 \ge\frac{3}{128}\min\Bigl\{R_0^2,\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mKN}\Bigr\}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
For $\sigma=0$ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise let $Q_{\rm tot}=mKN$,
$r_{\rm test}=\min\{R_0,\sigma/(4\mu\sqrt {Q_{\rm tot}})\}$ and
$\theta_{\rm test}\in\{-r_{\rm test},r_{\rm test}\}$, and
consider on $\mathbb R^2$, with $z_0=0$,
\[
 F_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)
 =\bigl(\mu(x_1-\theta_{\rm test}),Lx_2\bigr),\qquad
 \widehat F_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)
 =F_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)+(\sigma\zeta,0),\qquad
 \zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
This operator is $\mu$-strongly monotone and $L$-Lipschitz, its root
$(\theta_{\rm test},0)$ satisfies $\|z_0-z_\star\|\le R_0$, and the oracle satisfies
Assumption~\ref{ass:mixed} for every $\rho\ge1$. Subtracting the known
value $\mu x_1$ from the first coordinate of every response leaves
$Q_{\rm tot}$ observations from
$\mathcal N(-\mu\theta_{\rm test},\sigma^2)$. Since
$Q_{\rm tot}\mu^2r_{\rm test}^2/\sigma^2\le1/16$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-testing} shows that the sign of $\widehat z_1$
differs from the sign of $\theta_{\rm test}$ with average probability
at least $3/8$, and then
$\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\ge r_{\rm test}^2$.
Hence one of the two signs gives
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\ge\frac38r_{\rm test}^2
 \ge\frac{3R_0^2}{128}\min\Bigl\{1,\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2R_0^2mKN}\Bigr\}.
\]
Padding with coordinates on which
the operator is $Lx_j$ embeds this example in every dimension.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:strong-mixed-accuracy}
Suppose $\kappa\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon_{\rm rel}<1/200$. Then
\begin{equation*}
 N^*_{\rm dist}(\varepsilon)=\Omega\!\left(\max\Bigl\{1,\
 \frac{\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})}{D_{\mathrm{info}}},\
 \frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mK\varepsilon}\Bigr\}\right),
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:smr-round-upper}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_{\rm ser}
   &:=\frac{\kappa}{K_{\rm ser}}\log\frac1{\varepsilon_{\rm rel}}
      +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2K\varepsilon},\\
 \mathcal T_{\rm pool}
   &:=\frac{\kappa}{K_{\rm cq}}\log\frac1{\varepsilon_{\rm rel}}
      +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mK\varepsilon},\\
 \mathcal T_{\rm hyb}
   &:=\frac{\kappa}{K_{\rm ser}+K_{\rm cq}}
      \log\frac1{\varepsilon_{\rm rel}}
      +\frac{\kappa\log(2m)}{K_{\rm cq}}
      +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mK\varepsilon},\\
 N^*_{\rm dist}(\varepsilon)
   &=O\!\left(1+\min\{\mathcal T_{\rm ser},\mathcal T_{\rm pool},
                        \mathcal T_{\rm hyb}\}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
\emph{Optimization lower bound.} By Corollary~\ref{vi:strong-exponent},
every algorithm has an instance with
$\mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\ge\frac{R_0^2}{50}\exp[-15372800ND_{\mathrm{info}}/\kappa]$.
Accuracy $\varepsilon$ therefore requires
\[
 N\ge\frac{\kappa\log(1/(50\varepsilon_{\rm rel}))}
          {15372800D_{\mathrm{info}}},
 \qquad
 \log\frac1{50\varepsilon_{\rm rel}}
 \ge\Bigl(1-\frac{\log50}{\log200}\Bigr)
      \log\frac1{\varepsilon_{\rm rel}},
\]
where the second inequality uses $\varepsilon_{\rm rel}<1/200$.

\emph{Statistical lower bound.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:smr-statistical} and
$\varepsilon_{\rm rel}<3/128$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ requires
$N\ge3\sigma^2/(128\mu^2mK\varepsilon)$.

\emph{Upper bound.} We give three choices of $N$ for which an algorithm
reaches accuracy $\varepsilon$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:smr-schedules} with
$x=z_0$, the serial schedule does so if
\[
 N\ge\frac{640\kappa}{3K_{\rm ser}}
      \log\frac{192}{\varepsilon_{\rm rel}}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 N\ge\frac{192\sigma^2}{\mu^2K\varepsilon},
\]
since then each of the two terms is at most $\varepsilon/2$; the
common-query schedule does so under the same conditions with
$K_{\rm ser}$ and $K$ replaced by $K_{\rm cq}$ and $mK$.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:strong-mixed-hybrid}, the two-phase algorithm does so if
\[
 N\ge\frac{640\kappa}{K_{\rm ser}+K_{\rm cq}}
      \log\frac{3C_{\rm hyb}}{\varepsilon_{\rm rel}},\qquad
 N\ge\frac{640\kappa\log m}{K_{\rm cq}},\qquad
 N\ge\frac{6C_{\rm hyb}\sigma^2}{\mu^2mK\varepsilon},
\]
because then
$C_{\rm hyb}R_0^2e^{-N(K_{\rm ser}+K_{\rm cq})/(640\kappa)}
\le\varepsilon/3$,
$m\,e^{-NK_{\rm cq}/(640\kappa)}\le1$, and the statistical term is at most
$2C_{\rm hyb}\sigma^2/(\mu^2mKN)\le\varepsilon/3$.
For $\varepsilon_{\rm rel}<1/200$, there is a universal constant
$C_{\log}>0$ such that
$\log(3C_{\rm hyb}/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})
\le C_{\log}\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})$, and the
smallest integer satisfying each set of conditions exceeds its largest
right-hand side by at most one. This proves~\eqref{eq:smr-round-upper}.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{nn:statistical-lower}
Every algorithm of Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} has an affine monotone
instance with $L$-Lipschitz operator, root at distance $D$ from
$z_0=0$, and an oracle with variance $\sigma^2$ at every point (so
Assumption~\ref{ass:mixed} holds for every $\rho\ge1$), such that
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{B(0,D)}^{\rm M}(\widehat z)
 \ge\frac3{128}\min\left\{LD^2,\
                   \frac{\sigma D}{\sqrt{mKN}}\right\}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
For $\sigma=0$ there is nothing to prove. Let $Q_{\rm tot}=mKN$,
$\lambda=\min\{L,\sigma/(4D\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}})\}$,
$\theta_{\rm test}\in\{-D,D\}$, and on
$\mathbb R^2$ (padded by coordinates with operator $Lx_j$)
\[
 F_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)
 =\bigl(\lambda(x_1-\theta_{\rm test}),Lx_2\bigr),\qquad
 g_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)=F_{\theta_{\rm test}}(x)+(\sigma\zeta,0),
 \quad \zeta\sim\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The root is $(\theta_{\rm test},0)$. Subtracting the known value
$\lambda x_1$ from
the first coordinate of every response leaves $Q_{\rm tot}$ observations
from $\mathcal N(-\lambda\theta_{\rm test},\sigma^2)$. Since
$Q_{\rm tot}\lambda^2D^2/\sigma^2\le1/16$,
Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-testing} shows that the decision
``$\theta_{\rm test}=D$ if $\widehat z_1\ge0$,
$\theta_{\rm test}=-D$ otherwise'' errs with average probability at least
$3/8$. On an error, test at
$u=(\theta_{\rm test}/2,0)\in B(0,D)$:
\[
 \langle F_{\theta_{\rm test}}(u),\widehat z-u\rangle
 =-\frac{\lambda\theta_{\rm test}}2
   \Bigl(\widehat z_1-\frac{\theta_{\rm test}}2\Bigr)
 =\frac{\lambda D}2\Bigl(\frac D2+|\widehat z_1|\Bigr)
 \ge\frac{\lambda D^2}4,
\]
because $\widehat z_1$ and $\theta_{\rm test}$ have opposite signs. The gap is
nonnegative otherwise, so the average over the two signs is at least
$3\lambda D^2/32$, and
$\lambda D^2=\min\{LD^2,\sigma D/(4\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}})\}
\ge\frac14\min\{LD^2,\sigma D/\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}\}$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{gm:edge}
For $0<\epsilon\le a_{\rm ch}/274$ and $\varsigma\in\{-1,1\}$, the function
\begin{equation*}
 \widehat E_{\epsilon,a_{\rm ch}}^{\varsigma}(u,v)
 =\varsigma\bigl[s_{a_{\rm ch}}(u)s_{a_{\rm ch}}(v)-b_\epsilon(u)b_\epsilon(v)\bigr]
 +\zeta_\epsilon(u)-\zeta_\epsilon(v)+q_{a_{\rm ch}}(u)-q_{a_{\rm ch}}(v)
\end{equation*}
is $C^2$ and convex--concave, and its value and gradient vanish on
$\{|u|,|v|\le\epsilon\}$. Both partial derivatives are at most $6a_{\rm ch}$ in
absolute value, so the gradient has norm at most $9a_{\rm ch}$. The diagonal
second derivatives are at most $522$ and the mixed one at most $82$ in
absolute value. On $[-2a_{\rm ch},2a_{\rm ch}]^2$,
$\widehat E_{\epsilon,a_{\rm ch}}^\varsigma$ equals $E_\epsilon^\varsigma$.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Since $\psi(1-s)=1-\psi(s)$, $\int_0^1(1-\psi)=1/2$, hence
$|s_{a_{\rm ch}}|\le2a_{\rm ch}+a_{\rm ch}/2=5a_{\rm ch}/2$.
By~\eqref{vi:psi-bounds}, $|s_{a_{\rm ch}}'|=\omega_{a_{\rm ch}}\le1$
and $|s_{a_{\rm ch}}''|\le15/(8a_{\rm ch})$. On each half-line
$s_{a_{\rm ch}}'$ decreases monotonically from $1$ to $0$, so
$\int_0^\infty|s_{a_{\rm ch}}''|=1$ and
$|q_{a_{\rm ch}}'|\le5a_{\rm ch}/2$; also $q_{a_{\rm ch}}''\le75/16$.
Lemma~\ref{vi:edge-lemma} and its
proof give $|b_\epsilon|\le2\epsilon$, $|b_\epsilon'|\le9$,
$|\zeta_\epsilon'|\le256\epsilon$ and
$0\le \zeta_\epsilon''=2\epsilon|b_\epsilon''|\le256$.

Write $\widehat E$ for $\widehat E_{\epsilon,a_{\rm ch}}^\varsigma$. Then
\[
 \partial_{uu}\widehat E=\varsigma\bigl[s_{a_{\rm ch}}''(u)s_{a_{\rm ch}}(v)-b_\epsilon''(u)b_\epsilon(v)\bigr]
 +\zeta_\epsilon''(u)+q_{a_{\rm ch}}''(u)\ge0,
\]
because $|s_{a_{\rm ch}}''(u)s_{a_{\rm ch}}(v)|
\le\frac{5a_{\rm ch}}2|s_{a_{\rm ch}}''(u)|=q_{a_{\rm ch}}''(u)$ and
$|b_\epsilon''(u)b_\epsilon(v)|\le2\epsilon|b_\epsilon''(u)|=\zeta_\epsilon''(u)$;
likewise $\partial_{vv}\widehat E\le0$. These bounds also give
$|\partial_{uu}\widehat E|\le2(256+75/16)<522$. The mixed derivative is
$\varsigma[s_{a_{\rm ch}}'(u)s_{a_{\rm ch}}'(v)-b_\epsilon'(u)b_\epsilon'(v)]$, at most $1+81$ in
absolute value. The first derivative
$\partial_u\widehat E
=\varsigma[s_{a_{\rm ch}}'(u)s_{a_{\rm ch}}(v)-b_\epsilon'(u)b_\epsilon(v)]
+\zeta_\epsilon'(u)+q_{a_{\rm ch}}'(u)$ is at most
$5a_{\rm ch}/2+18\epsilon+256\epsilon+5a_{\rm ch}/2\le6a_{\rm ch}$,
and similarly for $\partial_v\widehat E$; hence the gradient norm is at
