most $6\sqrt2a_{\rm ch}<9a_{\rm ch}$. For
$|u|,|v|\le\epsilon\le2a_{\rm ch}$ we have
$s_{a_{\rm ch}}=b_\epsilon=\mathrm{id}$ and $\zeta_\epsilon,q_{a_{\rm ch}}$
vanish with their derivatives, so $\widehat E$ and $\nabla\widehat E$ vanish.
On $[-2a_{\rm ch},2a_{\rm ch}]^2$, $s_{a_{\rm ch}}=\mathrm{id}$ and
$q_{a_{\rm ch}}=0$.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{gm:chain}
Let $\epsilon=a_{\rm ch}/(2000000\,n\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}})$. The operator $\widehat G$ is monotone
and $\ell$-Lipschitz with $\ell=1300\lambda$, and
\begin{equation*}
 \widehat G(w)=\lambda a_{\rm ch}e_1+\sum_{j=1}^{d_{\rm ch}-1}E_j(w),
\end{equation*}
where $E_j$ depends only on coordinates $j,j+1$,
$\|E_j\|\le9\lambda a_{\rm ch}$,
and $E_j$ vanishes when both coordinates are at most $\epsilon$ in absolute
value. Moreover $\widehat G$ has a root within distance
$548n\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}<a_{\rm ch}/4$ of
$z_{\rm ref}=(0,-a_{\rm ch}\mathbf1)$.
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Monotonicity, the decomposition and the bounds on $E_j$ follow from
Lemma~\ref{gm:edge}. Each coordinate belongs to at most two edges, so
the rows and columns of the Jacobian have absolute sums at most
$(2\cdot522+2\cdot82)\lambda=1208\lambda<\ell$. On the ball of radius
$548n\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}<a_{\rm ch}/4$ around
$z_{\rm ref}$, all coordinates have absolute value below $2a_{\rm ch}$,
so $\widehat G$ coincides with $G_\epsilon$ of~\eqref{vi:robust-chain}
there, and $\|\widehat G-G_0\|\le548\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}$
by Lemma~\ref{vi:core-root}. The Brouwer argument in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{vi:core-root} gives a root in this ball.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{gm:cube}
Let $r=D/4$ and $k=n-1$. If $\|x\|<R_{\rm cut}$ and all hidden coordinates of
$U^\top x$ after position $k$ are at most $\epsilon$ in absolute value, or
if $\|x\|\ge R_{\rm cut}$, then
\begin{equation*}
 \operatorname{Gap}^{\rm M}_{B(0,D)}(x)\ge\frac{\lambda r^2}{2n}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
\emph{Interior points.} Test on the hidden cube
$\{U(u,v):|u_i|,|v_i|\le a_{\rm ch}\}$, whose points have norm at most
$\sqrt2r<R_{\rm loc}$, so $F_U=G_U$ there. Write
$U^\top x=(\widehat u,\widehat v)$. The support function of the cube of
half-width $a_{\rm ch}$ is $a_{\rm ch}\|\cdot\|_1$, so,
as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{vi:affine-comparison}, the reference
operator $G_0$ gives
\[
 \sup_{(u,v)\in[-a_{\rm ch},a_{\rm ch}]^{d_{\rm ch}}}
 \langle G_0(u,v),U^\top x-(u,v)\rangle
 =\lambda\bigl[a_{\rm ch}\widehat u_1+a_{\rm ch}\|D_n\widehat u\|_1
 +a_{\rm ch}\|D_n^\top\widehat v+a_{\rm ch}e_1\|_1\bigr]
 \ge\lambda a_{\rm ch}(a_{\rm ch}-\epsilon).
\]
Indeed $\|D_n\widehat u\|_1\ge|\mathbf1^\top D_n\widehat u|=|\widehat u_1|$,
and the coordinates of $D_n^\top\widehat v+a_{\rm ch}e_1$ sum to
$a_{\rm ch}+\widehat v_n$,
where $|\widehat v_n|\le\epsilon$ because $\widehat v_n$ is the last
coordinate. On the cube $\widehat G=G_\epsilon$, so
by~\eqref{vi:uniform-core-error} replacing $G_0$ by $\widehat G$ changes
each tested inner product by at most
\[
 548\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}\,(R_{\rm cut}+\sqrt2r)
 \le\frac{548\cdot822}{2000000}\cdot
 \frac{\lambda r^2}{n\sqrt n}<\frac{\lambda r^2}{4n}.
\]
Since $\lambda a_{\rm ch}(a_{\rm ch}-\epsilon)
=\frac{\lambda r^2}n(1-\epsilon/a_{\rm ch})$ and
$\epsilon/a_{\rm ch}<10^{-6}$, the gap is at least $\lambda r^2/(2n)$.

\emph{Exterior points.} The argument of Theorem~\ref{vi:uvi-lower} with
the test point $2R_{\rm loc}x/\|x\|$ gives a gap of at least
$81\cdot408\,\ell R_{\rm loc}^2\ge\lambda r^2/(2n)$.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{gm:hiding}
Let $S_N$ be as in Section~\ref{vi:haar-subsection}, with the bits
$B_{\rm mask}$ of
the oracle, and let $k\ge0$ be an integer with $\mathbb P\{S_N\le k\}\ge3/4$;
for instance $k=\min\{KN,\lfloor4N\beta_p\rfloor\}$. If
\begin{equation}\label{gm:dimension}
 d_{\rm amb}\ge d_{\rm ch}
 +\frac{2R_{\rm cut}^2}{\epsilon^2}\log(32mKNd_{\rm ch}),
\end{equation}
then for every algorithm of Definition~\ref{def:ic-main}, with probability
at least $5/8$ over the frame, the bits and the algorithm's randomness,
the output either has norm at least $R_{\rm cut}$ or has all hidden coordinates
after position $k$ at most $\epsilon$ in absolute value.
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
We follow the proof of Lemma~\ref{vi:haar}; only the fictitious oracle
changes. Fix the bits and the algorithm's randomness, and let $c$ be
the number of granted columns before a call, as there. For a query $x$
with $\|x\|<R_{\rm cut}$ write $w=U^\top x$, and let $w^{(j)}$ keep the first $j$
coordinates of $w$ and set the others to zero.

Let $\pi_j$ keep the first $j$ components of a vector of
$\mathbb R^{d_{\rm ch}}$ and
$U_{\le j}=(U_1,\ldots,U_j)$. The known radial term $V(x)$ and the known
factor $\chi(x)$ are kept outside the projections below.

\emph{Failure.} The fictitious response is
$V(x)+\chi(x)U_{\le c}\,\pi_c(\widehat G-E_{\rm bd})(w^{(c)})$, which uses $c$
columns. Suppose all coordinates of $w$ after $c$ are at most $\epsilon$.
Then $s(w)=s(w^{(c)})=:s\le c$, and in
$\widehat G-E_s^{\rm bd}$ the edges $E_j$ with
$j>s$ vanish, the edges with $j<s$ involve and are supported on
coordinates up to $s$, and the edge $E_s$ (or the term
$\lambda a_{\rm ch}e_1$ if $s=0$) is removed. Hence
$(\widehat G-E_{\rm bd})(w)$ depends only on the first
$s\le c$ coordinates and is supported on them, so it equals
$\pi_c(\widehat G-E_{\rm bd})(w^{(c)})$, and the fictitious response equals the
true one.

\emph{Success.} Grant the column $c+1$ (if $c<d_{\rm ch}$), let
$c'=\min\{d_{\rm ch},c+1\}$,
and let the fictitious response be
\[
 V(x)+\chi(x)\,U_{\le c'}\,\pi_{c'}\bigl[\widehat G(w^{(c')})
 +(p^{-1}-1)E_{s(w^{(c)})}^{\rm bd}(w^{(c')})\bigr],
\]
where $E_s^{\rm bd}$ is the edge selected by $s$. It uses $c'$ columns; without
$\pi_{c'}$ it would not, since the edge $E_{c+1}$ evaluated at $w^{(c')}$
has a nonzero component $c+2$ when $|w_{c+1}|>\epsilon$. Under the same
assumption as above, the edges $E_j$ with $j\ge c+1$ have both coordinates
at most $\epsilon$ and vanish for $w$ and for $w^{(c')}$, the other edges
and $E_s^{\rm bd}$ with $s\le c$ involve and are supported on the first $c+1$
coordinates, and $s(w)=s(w^{(c)})$. Hence the true response is supported
on the first $c'$ coordinates and equals the fictitious one.

\emph{Exterior queries.} For $\|x\|\ge R_{\rm cut}$ the response is the known
vector $V(x)$; the simulator queries $0$ to use the bit, and its output
is $0$ whenever the true output has norm at least $R_{\rm cut}$.

All queries and outputs of the fictitious transcript have norm at most
$R_{\rm cut}$, and the number of granted columns at the end is at most
$\min\{d_{\rm ch},S_N\}$. The concentration and union-bound steps of
Lemma~\ref{vi:haar} apply without change: with probability at least $7/8$,
every fictitious query has all hidden coordinates after its own granted
prefix $c$ bounded by $\epsilon$, and the fictitious output has all hidden
coordinates after the final prefix bounded by $\epsilon$. On this event
the true and fictitious transcripts coincide by induction over calls.
Intersecting with $\{S_N\le k\}$, on which the final prefix has length at
most $k$, gives probability at least $5/8$.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
\label{gm:lower}\label{gm:frontier}
Let $0<p\le1$, $\sigma>0$, and
\begin{equation*}
 k=\min\{KN,\lfloor4N\beta_p\rfloor\},\quad n=k+1,\quad d_{\rm ch}=2n,\quad
 r=\frac D4,\quad a_{\rm ch}=\frac r{\sqrt n},\quad
 \lambda=\min\Bigl\{\frac L{120000},\ \frac{\sigma\sqrt{pn}}{9r}\Bigr\}.
\end{equation*}
In every dimension satisfying~\eqref{gm:dimension}, every algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} has an instance with monotone
$L$-Lipschitz operator, root in $B(0,D)$, and an oracle with
variance at most $\sigma^2$ at every point, such that
\begin{equation}\label{gm:lower-bound}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}^{\rm M}_{B(0,D)}(\widehat z)
 \ge c\min\left\{\frac{LD^2}{1+N\beta_p},\
 \frac{\sigma D\sqrt p}{\sqrt{1+N\beta_p}}\right\}
\end{equation}
with a universal $c>0$. In particular Assumption~\ref{ass:mixed} holds
for every $\rho\ge1$.
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
The operator $F_U$ is $90\cdot1300\lambda\le L$-Lipschitz, its root has
norm below $R_{\rm loc}<D$, and by~\eqref{gm:variance} and the choice of $\lambda$
the variance is at most $81\lambda^2r^2/(np)\le\sigma^2$.
Lemmas~\ref{gm:hiding} and~\ref{gm:cube} give an event of probability at
least $5/8$ on which the gap is at least $\lambda r^2/(2n)$. The gap is
nonnegative, so, as after Lemma~\ref{vi:haar}, a fixed frame gives
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}^{\rm M}_{B(0,D)}(\widehat z)\ge\frac{\lambda r^2}{4n}
 =\min\Bigl\{\frac{LD^2}{7680000\,n},\ \frac{\sigma D\sqrt p}{144\sqrt n}\Bigr\}.
\]
Since $n\le1+4N\beta_p\le4(1+N\beta_p)$, this
gives~\eqref{gm:lower-bound}.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{gm:local-obstruction}
In the dimension of Theorem~\ref{gm:lower} with $p=1/K$, every algorithm
has an instance with
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}^{\rm M}_{B(0,D)}(\widehat z)
 =\Omega\!\left(\min\left\{\frac{LD^2}{Nh},\ \frac{\sigma D}{\sqrt{KNh}}\right\}\right).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:clock:elementary} gives
$\beta_{1/K}\le(e-1)+\log m$. Hence $\beta_{1/K}=O(h)$ and
$1+N\beta_{1/K}=O(Nh)$, and Theorem~\ref{gm:lower} with $p=1/K$ gives
the claim.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{gm:equivalence}\label{gm:minimax}
Let
\[
 \mathcal U=\min\Bigl\{L,\ \frac{\rho L}{KN}+\frac{\sigma}{D\sqrt{KN}},\
 \frac LN\Bigl(1+\frac\rho{mK}\Bigr)+\frac{\sigma}{D\sqrt{mKN}}\Bigr\}.
\]
In every dimension
$\mathfrak R_{d_{\rm amb}}(\rho,\sigma)=O(D^2\,\mathcal U)$, and in
a sufficiently large dimension
\begin{equation}\label{gm:equivalent-lower}
 \mathfrak R_{d_{\rm amb}}(\rho,\sigma)
 =\Omega\!\left(\frac{D^2\,\mathcal U}{\log(2m)}\right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
\emph{Upper bound.} This is~\eqref{nn:ic-upper}, since
$1+\rho/(mK)$ and $1/\min\{1,mK/\rho\}$ differ by at most a factor two.

\emph{Lower bounds available.} Write $\alpha=K/\rho$ and, after division
by $D^2$,
\[
 x_1=\frac{\rho L}{KN},\quad y_1=\frac{\sigma}{D\sqrt{KN}},\quad
 x_0=\frac LN,\quad x_m=\Bigl(1+\frac1{m\alpha}\Bigr)x_0,\quad
 y_m=\frac{y_1}{\sqrt m},
\]
so that $\mathcal U=\min\{L,x_1+y_1,x_m+y_m\}$. Operators satisfying SGC
satisfy Assumption~\ref{ass:mixed}, so Theorem~\ref{vi:uvi-lower} gives
the lower bound $c\,r_{\rm info}$ with
$r_{\rm info}=L/(1+ND_{\mathrm{info}})$.
Proposition~\ref{nn:statistical-lower} gives $c\min\{L,y_m\}$ and
Corollary~\ref{gm:local-obstruction} gives
$c\min\{x_0/h,y_1/\sqrt h\}\ge c'\min\{x_0,y_1\}/h$, using $h\ge\log2$.
For each algorithm we use the instance with the largest of these bounds,
after padding all instances to a common dimension with coordinates on
which the operator is $Lx_j$.

\emph{Case $K\ge2\rho$.} Then $\alpha\ge2$, $x_1\le x_0/2\le L$ and
$x_0\le x_m\le\frac32x_0$. Since
$D_{\mathrm{info}}\le\alpha+h/\log2\le(1+1/\log2)h\alpha$, we get
$r_{\rm info}=\Omega(\min\{L,x_1/h\})$. Since $x_1/h\le L$, this gives
$r_{\rm info}=\Omega(x_1/h)$. If $y_1\le x_0$, then
$\mathcal U\le x_1+\min\{y_1,x_0\}$. If $y_1>x_0$, then
$\mathcal U\le\min\{L,\frac32x_0+y_m\}\le\frac32\min\{y_1,x_0\}+\min\{L,y_m\}$.
In both cases
$\mathcal U\le3\max\{x_1,\min\{L,y_m\},\min\{y_1,x_0\}\}$, and the maximum
of the three lower bounds is at least $c\,\mathcal U/h$.

\emph{Case $K<2\rho$.} Let $w=\min\{1,m\alpha\}$; then
$\max\{\alpha,w\}\le2w$. Lemma~\ref{lem:clock:constructive} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:clock:asymptotic} give $D_{\mathrm{info}}=O(hw)$, so
$r_{\rm info}=\Omega(\min\{L,L/(Nw)\}/h)$, and
\[
 \max\bigl\{r_{\rm info},\min\{L,y_m\}\bigr\}
 =\Omega\!\left(\frac1h\min\Bigl\{L,\frac L{Nw}+y_m\Bigr\}\right).
\]
Since $x_m\le2L/(Nw)$, $\mathcal U\le\min\{L,x_m+y_m\}\le
2\min\{L,L/(Nw)+y_m\}$, which proves~\eqref{gm:equivalent-lower}.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{sf:root}
The operator $\mu I+\widehat G$ has a unique root $w_\star=(u_\star,v_\star)$,
and
\begin{equation*}
 \|w_\star\|<1.072\,r,\qquad
 (v_\star)_i<-0.928\,a_{\rm ch}\quad(1\le i\le n).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Let $A=\lambda\begin{psmallmatrix}0&D_n^\top\\-D_n&0\end{psmallmatrix}$, so
that $G_0(w)=A(w-z_{\rm ref})$. Since $D_n^{-1}$ is the upper triangular
matrix of ones, $\|A^{-1}\|\le n/\lambda$ and also
$\|A^{-1}\|_{\infty}\le n/\lambda$ (maximal absolute row sum), so
$\|\mu A^{-1}\|\le1/16$ in both norms. The root of $\mu I+G_0$ is
$z_\mu=(I+\mu A^{-1})^{-1}z_{\rm ref}$, and the Neumann series gives
\begin{equation*}
 \|z_\mu-z_{\rm ref}\|\le\frac{1/16}{1-1/16}\|z_{\rm ref}\|=\frac r{15},\qquad
 \|z_\mu-z_{\rm ref}\|_\infty\le\frac{a_{\rm ch}}{15}.
\end{equation*}
All coordinates of $z_\mu$ are below $2a_{\rm ch}$ in absolute value,
so~\eqref{sf:local-error} holds at $z_\mu$. The operator $\mu I+\widehat G$
is $\mu$-strongly monotone and $(\mu+\ell)$-Lipschitz, so, as in the proof
of Lemma~\ref{vi:strong-core}, it has a unique root $w_\star$ and
\begin{equation*}
 \|w_\star-z_\mu\|\le\frac{\|(\mu I+\widehat G)(z_\mu)\|}\mu
 =\frac{\|(\widehat G-G_0)(z_\mu)\|}\mu
 \le\frac{548\lambda\epsilon\sqrt{d_{\rm ch}}}\mu
 =0.004384\,a_{\rm ch}.
\end{equation*}
Hence $\|w_\star\|\le(1+\frac1{15})r+0.004384a_{\rm ch}<1.072r$ and
$(v_\star)_i\le-a_{\rm ch}+\frac{a_{\rm ch}}{15}
+0.004384a_{\rm ch}<-0.928a_{\rm ch}$.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{sf:hiding}
Suppose $Nh\le n/64$. Let $p=n/(128KN)$ if $KN\ge n/128$ and $p=1$
otherwise, and let $k=\lfloor n/4\rfloor$. If
\begin{equation}\label{sf:dimension}
 d_{\rm amb}\ge d_{\rm ch}
 +\frac{2R_{\rm cut}^2}{\epsilon^2}\log(32mKNd_{\rm ch})
 =2n+10758400000000000000\,n^4\log(64mKNn),
\end{equation}
then for every algorithm there is a fixed frame $U$ such that, with
probability at least $1/2$ over the bits and the algorithm's randomness,
the output either has norm at least $R_{\rm cut}$ or has all hidden coordinates
after position $k$ at most $\epsilon$.
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
If $p=n/(128KN)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:clock:elementary} gives
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E S_N=N\beta_p\le N\bigl((e-1)Kp+\log m\bigr)
 \le\frac{(e-1)n}{128}+\frac n{64}<\frac n{32},
\end{equation*}
and since $S_N>k$ implies $S_N>n/4$, Markov's inequality gives
$\mathbb P\{S_N\le k\}>7/8$. If $p=1$, then $S_N\le KN<n/128\le k$ (this case
requires $n>128$). Subtracting the known term $\mu x$ from every response
reduces the oracle to~\eqref{gm:oracle}, so Lemma~\ref{gm:hiding} applies
with this $k$; together with $\mathbb P\{S_N\le k\}\ge7/8$, its
event has probability at least $3/4$, and some fixed frame gives
probability at least $1/2$. Finally
$R_{\rm cut}=820a_{\rm ch}\sqrt n$ and
$\epsilon=a_{\rm ch}/(2000000\,n\sqrt{2n})$ give
$2R_{\rm cut}^2/\epsilon^2
=2\cdot820^2\cdot(2\cdot10^6)^2\cdot2\,n^4$, which
is~\eqref{sf:dimension}.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{sf:short-lower}
Let $\sigma>0$ and
\begin{equation}\label{sf:length}
 n=\Bigl\lfloor\frac{\kappa-1}{1872000}\Bigr\rfloor .
\end{equation}
If $n\ge1$ and $Nh\le n/64$, then in the dimension~\eqref{sf:dimension}
every algorithm has an instance with $\mu$-strongly monotone
$L$-Lipschitz operator, $\|z_0-z_\star\|\le R_0$, and an oracle with
variance at most $\sigma^2$, such that
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 \ge\min\left\{\frac{R_0^2}{80},\
       \frac{\sigma^2}{13271040\,\mu^2KN}\right\}.
\end{equation*}
If $KN<n/128$, the oracle is exact and the bound is $R_0^2/80$, also for
$\sigma=0$.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
By~\eqref{sf:lipschitz} and~\eqref{sf:length}, the Lipschitz constant is at
most $\mu\kappa=L$. If $KN\ge n/128$, let
\begin{equation*}
 p=\frac n{128KN},\qquad
 a_{\rm ch}=\min\Bigl\{\frac{R_0}{4\sqrt n},\
 \frac{\sigma\sqrt p}{9\lambda}\Bigr\},
\end{equation*}
so that the variance~\eqref{sf:variance} is at most $\sigma^2$; if
$KN<n/128$, let $p=1$ and $a_{\rm ch}=R_0/(4\sqrt n)$. In both cases
$\|z_\star\|<1.072\,a_{\rm ch}\sqrt n<R_0$.

Consider the event of Lemma~\ref{sf:hiding}. If the output has norm
below $R_{\rm cut}$, its hidden coordinates after $k=\lfloor n/4\rfloor$
are at most $\epsilon<0.001a_{\rm ch}$. The coordinate $v_i$ has position $2i$, so at least
$n-k/2\ge n/2$ of the $v$-coordinates lie after $k$, and each differs from
$(v_\star)_i<-0.928a_{\rm ch}$ by more than $0.9a_{\rm ch}$. Hence
$\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\ge\frac n2(0.9a_{\rm ch})^2
=0.405\,na_{\rm ch}^2$. If the output has norm at least $R_{\rm cut}$, then
$\|\widehat z-z_\star\|\ge R_{\rm cut}-1.072r>818r$, which is larger. Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2
 \ge\frac12\cdot0.405\,na_{\rm ch}^2\ge\frac{na_{\rm ch}^2}5 .
\]
For $a_{\rm ch}=R_0/(4\sqrt n)$ this is $R_0^2/80$. For
$a_{\rm ch}=\sigma\sqrt p/(9\lambda)=\sigma\sqrt p/(144n\mu)$ it is
$\sigma^2p/(103680\,\mu^2n)=\sigma^2/(13271040\,\mu^2KN)$.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{sf:rate-lower}
Let $\kappa\ge2$ and $T_{\rm ch}=1872000$. In a sufficiently large
dimension, every algorithm of Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} has, for each
of the three quantities
\begin{equation*}
 \begin{gathered}
 \frac{R_0^2}{50}e^{-15372800ND_{\mathrm{info}}/\kappa},\qquad
 \frac3{128}\min\Bigl\{R_0^2,\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mKN}\Bigr\},\\
 \mathbf 1\Bigl\{N\log(2m)\le\frac{\kappa}{256T_{\rm ch}}\Bigr\}
 \min\Bigl\{\frac{R_0^2}{80},\frac{\sigma^2}{13271040\,\mu^2KN}\Bigr\},
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation*}
an instance with a $\mu$-strongly monotone $L$-Lipschitz operator,
$\|z_0-z_\star\|\le R_0$, and an oracle satisfying
Assumption~\ref{ass:mixed}, on which $\mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2$ is at
least this quantity.
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
The first quantity is Corollary~\ref{vi:strong-exponent}; its oracle
satisfies SGC and therefore Assumption~\ref{ass:mixed} for every
$\sigma\ge0$. The second is Lemma~\ref{lem:smr-statistical}. The third is
zero for $\sigma=0$. For $\sigma>0$ let $h=\log(2m)$ and suppose
$Nh\le\kappa/(256T_{\rm ch})$. Since $N\ge1$ and $h\ge\log2$, this gives
$\kappa\ge256T_{\rm ch}\log2>2T_{\rm ch}+1$, so
$n=\lfloor(\kappa-1)/T_{\rm ch}\rfloor\ge(\kappa-1)/T_{\rm ch}-1
\ge\kappa/(4T_{\rm ch})\ge1$ and $Nh\le n/64$; Theorem~\ref{sf:short-lower}
gives the bound. Coordinates on which the operator is $\mu x_j$ embed all
instances in a common dimension.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{sf:accuracy-lower}
For $\kappa\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon_{\rm rel}<1/200$,
\begin{equation}\label{sf:accuracy-bridge}
 N^*_{\rm dist}(\varepsilon)=\Omega\!\left(\min\Bigl\{\frac\kappa h,\ s_1\Bigr\}\right),
\end{equation}
and, together with Corollary~\ref{cor:strong-mixed-accuracy},
\begin{equation}\label{sf:accuracy-full-lower}
 N^*_{\rm dist}(\varepsilon)=\Omega\!\Biggl(1
 +\frac{\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})}{D_{\mathrm{info}}}
 +\min\Bigl\{s_1,\ \frac\kappa h+s_m\Bigr\}\Biggr).
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Let $T=1872000$ and $n=\lfloor(\kappa-1)/T\rfloor$. Suppose
$N<\min\{n/(64h),\,s_1/13271040\}$. Then $n\ge1$ and $Nh\le n/64$, and
Theorem~\ref{sf:short-lower} gives an instance with
$\mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2>\varepsilon$, because $R_0^2/80>\varepsilon$ and
$\sigma^2/(13271040\mu^2KN)>\varepsilon$. Hence
$N^*_{\rm dist}(\varepsilon)\ge\min\{n/(64h),s_1/13271040\}$. If
$\kappa\ge2T+1$, then $n\ge(\kappa-1)/T-1\ge\kappa/(4T)$, which
gives~\eqref{sf:accuracy-bridge}. If $2\le\kappa<2T+1$, then
$\kappa/h\le(2T+1)/\log2$, and~\eqref{sf:accuracy-bridge} follows from
$N^*_{\rm dist}(\varepsilon)\ge1$.

Corollary~\ref{cor:strong-mixed-accuracy} gives the lower bounds $1$,
$\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})/D_{\mathrm{info}}$ and $s_m$.
Since $s_m\le s_1$,
\[
 \min\Bigl\{s_1,\frac\kappa h+s_m\Bigr\}
 \le s_m+\min\Bigl\{s_1,\frac\kappa h\Bigr\}
 \le2\max\Bigl\{s_m,\min\Bigl\{s_1,\frac\kappa h\Bigr\}\Bigr\},
\]
so the sum in~\eqref{sf:accuracy-full-lower} is at most four times the
largest of the four lower bounds.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- corollary-11: body_md -->
\label{sf:accuracy-match}
For $\kappa\ge2$ and $0<\varepsilon_{\rm rel}<1/200$, the lower
bound~\eqref{sf:accuracy-full-lower} and the upper bound
\begin{equation}\label{sf:accuracy-full-upper}
 N^*_{\rm dist}(\varepsilon)=O\!\Biggl(1
 +\frac{\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})}
 {\max\{K/\rho,\min\{1,mK/\rho\}\}}
 +\min\bigl\{s_1,\ \kappa h+s_m\bigr\}\Biggr)
\end{equation}
differ by at most a factor $C\log^2(2m)$ with a universal $C$.
<!-- end corollary-11 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Let $\alpha=K/\rho$, $w=\min\{1,m\alpha\}$ and $\Delta=\max\{\alpha,w\}$.

\emph{Upper bound.} If $\alpha\le w$, then $\Delta=w$, and the
common-query entry of~\eqref{eq:smr-round-upper} gives
$1+\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})/w+s_m$, which is at most the right side
of~\eqref{sf:accuracy-full-upper} because $s_m\le s_1$ and
$s_m\le\kappa h+s_m$. If $\alpha>w$, then $w=1<\alpha=\Delta$, and the
serial and two-phase entries give
$1+\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})/\alpha+s_1$ and
$1+\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon_{\rm rel})/(\alpha+1)+\kappa h+s_m$;
their minimum is at most
the right side of~\eqref{sf:accuracy-full-upper}.

\emph{Comparison.} If $\alpha\ge1$, then $\Delta\ge\alpha$ and
$D_{\mathrm{info}}\le\alpha+h/\log2\le C_1h\Delta$. If $\alpha<1$, then
$\Delta=w$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:clock:constructive} with
Theorem~\ref{thm:clock:asymptotic} gives $D_{\mathrm{info}}\le C_1h\Delta$. Hence
the second terms of the two bounds differ by at most a factor $C_1h$.
For the third terms, $\kappa h+s_m\le\max\{1,h^2\}(\kappa/h+s_m)$ and
$\max\{1,h^2\}\le h^2/\log^22$, so
$\min\{s_1,\kappa h+s_m\}\le(h^2/\log^22)\min\{s_1,\kappa/h+s_m\}$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{gs:gronwall}
For all $x,y\in\mathbb R^d$,
\[
 \|F(y)-F(x)\|\le(L_0+L_1\|F(x)\|)\,e^{L_1\|y-x\|}\,\|y-x\| .
\]
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Let $u=(y-x)/\|y-x\|$ and $\varphi_{\rm seg}(t)=\|F(x+tu)\|$. Then
$\varphi_{\rm seg}$ is absolutely continuous and
$\varphi_{\rm seg}'(t)\le\|\mathrm DF(x+tu)\|_{\rm op}\le L_0+L_1\varphi_{\rm seg}(t)$
almost everywhere, so $L_0+L_1\varphi_{\rm seg}(t)\le(L_0+L_1\varphi_{\rm seg}(0))e^{L_1t}$ (for $L_1=0$
directly, for $L_1>0$ by Gr\"onwall's inequality). Integrating
$\|\mathrm DF(x+tu)u\|\le(L_0+L_1\varphi_{\rm seg}(0))e^{L_1t}$ over $t\in[0,\|y-x\|]$
gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{gs:seg-residual}
Let $C$ be closed and convex, $x,u\in C$, $\eta>0$, and
\[
 y=\Pi_C\bigl(x-\eta(F(x)+e)\bigr),\qquad
 x^+=\Pi_C\bigl(x-\eta(F(y)+h)\bigr).
\]
If $\|F(y)-F(x)\|\le L_{\rm seg}\|y-x\|$, then
\begin{equation}\label{gs:projected-pathwise}
 \|x^+-u\|^2\le\|x-u\|^2-2\eta\langle F(y),y-u\rangle
 -(1-3\eta^2L_{\rm seg}^2)\|x-y\|^2
 +3\eta^2\bigl(\|e\|^2+\|h\|^2\bigr)-2\eta\langle h,y-u\rangle .
\end{equation}
If moreover $C=B(c,2r)$, $\|c-z_\star\|\le r$,
$\eta\|F(x)\|\le3r$, and $y^0=\Pi_C(x-\eta F(x))$, then
\begin{equation}\label{gs:projection-margin}
 \|x-y^0\|\ge\frac{\eta\|F(x)\|}8 .
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
The optimality conditions of the two projections,
$\langle x-\eta(F(y)+h)-x^+,u-x^+\rangle\le0$ and
$\langle x-\eta(F(x)+e)-y,x^+-y\rangle\le0$, give the standard bound
\[
 \|x^+-u\|^2\le\|x-u\|^2-2\eta\langle F(y)+h,y-u\rangle
 -\|x-y\|^2-\|y-x^+\|^2
 +2\eta\langle F(y)-F(x)+h-e,\,y-x^+\rangle .
\]
By $2\langle a,b\rangle\le\|a\|^2+\|b\|^2$ the last term is at most
$\eta^2\|F(y)-F(x)+h-e\|^2+\|y-x^+\|^2$, and
$\|F(y)-F(x)+h-e\|^2\le3(L_{\rm seg}^2\|y-x\|^2+\|h\|^2+\|e\|^2)$. This
proves~\eqref{gs:projected-pathwise}.

For~\eqref{gs:projection-margin} let $M_x=\|F(x)\|$ and
$\Delta_0=\|x-y^0\|$.
If $M_x=0$ there is nothing to prove, and if $\Delta_0\ge r/2$ the claim
follows from $\eta M_x\le3r$. Otherwise let
$u=z_\star-rF(x)/M_x$, which lies in
$C$. Monotonicity and $F(z_\star)=0$ give
$\langle F(x),x-z_\star\rangle\ge0$, hence
\[
 \langle F(x),y^0-u\rangle
 =\langle F(x),y^0-x\rangle+\langle F(x),x-z_\star\rangle+rM_x
 \ge M_x(r-\Delta_0)\ge\frac{M_xr}2 .
\]
The optimality condition of $y^0$ gives
$\eta\langle F(x),y^0-u\rangle\le\langle x-y^0,y^0-u\rangle\le4r\Delta_0$,
since $C$ has diameter $4r$. Hence $\eta M_xr/2\le4r\Delta_0$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{grv:robust}
Fix a query $x$ determined by the history $\mathcal F$, a reference
magnitude $F_{\rm ref}>0$, a tolerance $\delta_{\rm rob}>0$, and a
failure probability $0<\tau_{\rm fail}<1$. Let
\begin{equation}\label{grv:robust-budget}
 n=\max\Bigl\{1,\Bigl\lceil\frac{256}{\delta_{\rm rob}^2}
       \Bigl(\rho-1+\frac{\sigma^2}{F_{\rm ref}^2}\Bigr)\Bigr\rceil\Bigr\},
 \qquad k=\max\{1,\lceil8\log(1/\tau_{\rm fail})\rceil\},\qquad b=nk .
\end{equation}
The geometric median $\widehat F_x$ of $k$ block means, each of $n$ independent
responses at $x$, satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb P\bigl\{\|\widehat F_x-F(x)\|>
 \delta_{\rm rob}\max\{\|F(x)\|,F_{\rm ref}\}\bigm|\mathcal F\bigr\}
 \le\tau_{\rm fail} .
\end{equation*}
If $\rho=1$ and $\sigma=0$, one exact response is used instead ($b=1$). The
median is the minimum-norm minimizer of the sum of distances, which is
measurable and lies in the convex hull of the block means.
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Let $M_x=\|F(x)\|$ and $M_{\rm rob}=\max\{M_x,F_{\rm ref}\}$. A block
mean $h_j$ has conditional variance at most
$((\rho-1)M_x^2+\sigma^2)/n$, so Chebyshev's inequality and
the choice of $n$ give
\[
 \mathbb P\Bigl\{\|h_j-F(x)\|>
       \frac{\delta_{\rm rob}M_{\rm rob}}4\Bigm|\text{earlier blocks}\Bigr\}
 \le\frac{16\bigl((\rho-1)M_x^2+\sigma^2\bigr)}
          {n\delta_{\rm rob}^2M_{\rm rob}^2}
 \le\frac{16}{n\delta_{\rm rob}^2}
       \Bigl(\rho-1+\frac{\sigma^2}{F_{\rm ref}^2}\Bigr)\le\frac1{16}.
\]

\emph{Medians.} Suppose that at least a fraction $1-\vartheta$ of points
$x_1,\ldots,x_k$ lie within $r_{\rm med}$ of a point $v$, and let
$z_{\rm med}$ be a geometric
median. For such a good point,
$\|x_i-z_{\rm med}\|-\|x_i-v\|\ge\|z_{\rm med}-v\|-2r_{\rm med}$,
and for every other point
$\|x_i-z_{\rm med}\|-\|x_i-v\|\ge-\|z_{\rm med}-v\|$.
Since $z_{\rm med}$ minimizes the sum of
distances, summing gives
\begin{equation}\label{grv:median-distance}
 (1-2\vartheta)\|z_{\rm med}-v\|\le2(1-\vartheta)r_{\rm med} .
\end{equation}

\emph{Counting bad blocks.} Let $I_j$ indicate
$\|h_j-F(x)\|>\delta_{\rm rob}M_{\rm rob}/4$. Then
$\mathbb E[4^{I_j}\mid\text{earlier blocks}]\le1+3/16$,
so $\mathbb E4^{\sum_jI_j}\le(19/16)^k$ and, by Markov's inequality,
\[
 \mathbb P\Bigl\{\sum_jI_j\ge\frac k4\Bigr\}\le\Bigl(\frac{19}{16}\cdot4^{-1/4}\Bigr)^k
 \le e^{-k/8}\le\tau_{\rm fail} .
\]
Otherwise $\vartheta<1/4$, and~\eqref{grv:median-distance} with
$r_{\rm med}=\delta_{\rm rob}M_{\rm rob}/4$ gives
\[
 \|\widehat F_x-F(x)\|
 \le\frac{2\cdot3/4}{1/2}\cdot\frac{\delta_{\rm rob}M_{\rm rob}}4
 =\frac{3\delta_{\rm rob}M_{\rm rob}}4.
\]
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{grv:adaptive-stage}
Conditionally on any history at the start of the stage with
$\|c-z_\star\|\le r$, the output $z_{\rm out}(c,r)=x_{T_r}$ satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\|z_{\rm out}(c,r)-z_\star\|^2\le\frac{r^2}{1024},
 \qquad
 \mathbb P\Bigl\{\|z_{\rm out}(c,r)-z_\star\|>\frac r8\Bigr\}\le\frac1{16}.
\end{equation*}
All queries and the output lie in $\mathcal B(c,r)$ on every history.
For a universal constant $C_{\rm stage}>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{grv:adaptive-stage-work}
 T_r\le C_{\rm stage}S_r,\qquad
 b_r\le C_{\rm stage}\Bigl(\rho+\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2r^2S_r}\Bigr)\log(64S_r),\qquad
 b_rT_r\le C_{\rm stage}\Bigl(\rho S_r+\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2r^2}\Bigr)\log(64S_r).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
Fix an iteration and condition on the history before it. Drop the index
$r$ by writing
\[
 S=S_r,\quad M=M_r,\quad \ell=\ell_r,\quad F_{\rm ref}=F_r,
 \quad \tau_{\rm fail}=\tau_{{\rm fail},r},\quad
 n=n_r,\quad b=b_r.
\]
Also write $M_x=\|F(x)\|$,
$\widehat M_x=\|\widehat F_x\|$,
$e_x=\widehat F_x-F(x)$,
$E_x=\|x-z_\star\|^2\le9r^2$,
$R_y=\|y-z_\star\|$, and $\Delta_{xy}=\|x-y\|$.

\emph{A good estimate controls the step.} Consider the event
$\{\|e_x\|\le\delta_{\rm rob}\max\{M_x,F_{\rm ref}\}\}$, which fails
with probability at most $\tau_{\rm fail}$ (Lemma~\ref{grv:robust}). On it,
$(1-\delta_{\rm rob})M_x\le\widehat M_x+\delta_{\rm rob}F_{\rm ref}$,
and since $\ell F_{\rm ref}\le M$, we have
$(1-\delta_{\rm rob})(M+\ell M_x)\le M+\ell\widehat M_x$. Hence
\begin{equation*}
 \eta(L_0+L_1M_x)\le\eta(M+\ell M_x)
      \le\frac1{64(1-\delta_{\rm rob})},\qquad
 \Delta_{xy}\le\eta\widehat M_x\le\frac1{64\ell},\qquad
 \eta M_x<\frac1{32\ell}\le\frac r{32}.
\end{equation*}
By Lemma~\ref{gs:gronwall}, $F$ is $L_{xy}$-Lipschitz on the segment
$[x,y]$ with $L_{xy}=(L_0+L_1M_x)e^{L_1\Delta_{xy}}$, and
$L_1\Delta_{xy}\le\ell\Delta_{xy}\le1/64$ gives
$\eta L_{xy}\le e^{1/64}/(64(1-\delta_{\rm rob}))<1/16$. Therefore
$\|F(y)\|\le M_x+\widehat M_x/16
\le\frac{17}{16}M_x+\frac{\|e_x\|}{16}$ and
$\|F(y)\|^2\le3M_x^2+\delta_{\rm rob}^2F_{\rm ref}^2/128$.

\emph{The step is not too short.} Since $\eta M_x<r/32$,
Lemma~\ref{gs:seg-residual} gives $\|x-y^0\|\ge\eta M_x/8$ for
$y^0=\Pi_{\mathcal B(c,r)}(x-\eta F(x))$. Since
$\|y-y^0\|\le\eta\|e_x\|$ and
$(s-t)^2\ge s^2/2-t^2$,
\begin{equation}\label{grv:adaptive-displacement}
 \Delta_{xy}^2\ge\frac{\eta^2M_x^2}{128}-\eta^2\|e_x\|^2 .
\end{equation}

\emph{The corrector.} Let $e_y=\widehat h-F(y)$. The batch size $b\ge n$ gives
$(\rho-1)/b\le\delta_{\rm rob}^2/256$ and
$\sigma^2/b\le\delta_{\rm rob}^2F_{\rm ref}^2/256$, so
\begin{equation}\label{grv:adaptive-corrector}
 \mathbb E[e_y\mid\widehat F_x,\mathcal F]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E[\|e_y\|^2\mid\widehat F_x,\mathcal F]
 \le\frac{\rho-1}b\|F(y)\|^2+\frac{\sigma^2}b
 \le\frac{\delta_{\rm rob}^2}{64}(M_x^2+F_{\rm ref}^2).
\end{equation}

\emph{One iteration on the good event.} Apply~\eqref{gs:projected-pathwise}
with $u=z_\star$ and $L_{\rm seg}=L_{xy}$; the last term has zero conditional mean,
$1-3\eta^2L_{xy}^2\ge3/4$, and
$\|e_x\|^2\le\delta_{\rm rob}^2(M_x^2+F_{\rm ref}^2)$.
By~\eqref{grv:adaptive-displacement} and~\eqref{grv:adaptive-corrector}, the
terms other than $-2\eta\langle F(y),y-z_\star\rangle$ contribute at most
\[
 \eta^2\Bigl[-\frac{3M_x^2}{512}
 +\Bigl(\frac34+3\Bigr)\delta_{\rm rob}^2(M_x^2+F_{\rm ref}^2)
 +\frac3{64}\delta_{\rm rob}^2(M_x^2+F_{\rm ref}^2)\Bigr]
 \le-\frac{\eta^2M_x^2}{256}
      +4\delta_{\rm rob}^2\eta^2F_{\rm ref}^2,
\]
because $\delta_{\rm rob}=2^{-20}$. With
$\langle F(y),y-z_\star\rangle\ge\mu R_y^2$,
\begin{equation}\label{grv:adaptive-good-drift}
 \mathbb E[\|x^+-z_\star\|^2\mid\widehat F_x,\mathcal F]
 \le E_x-2\eta\mu R_y^2-\frac{\eta^2M_x^2}{256}
      +4\delta_{\rm rob}^2\eta^2F_{\rm ref}^2 .
\end{equation}

\emph{Contraction.} Let $\theta_{\rm ctr}=\theta_r$. If
$\ell M_x>M$, then $M_x>F_{\rm ref}$,
$\widehat M_x\le(1+\delta_{\rm rob})M_x$ and
$\eta M_x\ge1/(192\ell)$; since
$S\ge(1+L_1r)^2=\ell^2r^2$ and $E_x\le9r^2$,
\[
 \frac{\eta^2M_x^2}{256}\ge\frac1{256\cdot192^2\ell^2}
 \ge\frac {E_x}{9\cdot256\cdot192^2S}\ge\theta_{\rm ctr}E_x,
\]
because $9\cdot256\cdot192^2<2^{32}$. If $\ell M_x\le M$, then
$\ell\widehat M_x\le(1+\delta_{\rm rob})M$, so
$\eta\mu\ge\mu/(192M)=1/(192S)\ge\theta_{\rm ctr}$;
moreover
$E_x\le2R_y^2+2\Delta_{xy}^2
\le2R_y^2+8\eta^2M_x^2+4\delta_{\rm rob}^2\eta^2F_{\rm ref}^2$, and
since $8\theta_{\rm ctr}\le1/256$, the two negative terms
of~\eqref{grv:adaptive-good-drift} are at least
$\theta_{\rm ctr}E_x
-4\theta_{\rm ctr}\delta_{\rm rob}^2\eta^2F_{\rm ref}^2$. In both cases
\[
 \mathbb E[\|x^+-z_\star\|^2\mid\widehat F_x,\mathcal F]
 \le(1-\theta_{\rm ctr})E_x
      +5\delta_{\rm rob}^2\eta^2F_{\rm ref}^2
 \le(1-\theta_{\rm ctr})E_x+\frac{\theta_{\rm ctr} r^2}{4096},
\]
using
$\eta^2F_{\rm ref}^2\le F_{\rm ref}^2/(4096M^2)=r^2/(4096S)$ and
$5\delta_{\rm rob}^2\le2^{-32}$.

\emph{Failures and iteration.} On the event that the estimate fails,
$\|x^+-z_\star\|^2\le9r^2$. Hence
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E[\|x^+-z_\star\|^2\mid\mathcal F]
 \le(1-\theta_{\rm ctr})E_x
      +\frac{\theta_{\rm ctr}r^2}{4096}+9r^2\tau_{\rm fail} .
\end{equation*}
Iterating from $\|x_0-z_\star\|^2\le r^2$ and using
$(1-\theta_{\rm ctr})^{T_r}\le e^{-\theta_{\rm ctr}T_r}\le1/4096$
and $9\tau_{\rm fail}/\theta_{\rm ctr}=1/4096$,
\[
 \mathbb E\|x_{T_r}-z_\star\|^2\le\frac{r^2}{4096}+\frac{r^2}{4096}+\frac{r^2}{4096}
 \le\frac{r^2}{1024},
\]
and Markov's inequality gives the probability bound.

\emph{Work.} $T_r\le2^{32}S\log4096+1$ and
$\log(1/\tau_{{\rm fail},r})
=\log(9\cdot4096\cdot2^{32}S)\le C_{\rm stage}\log(64S)$; substituting
$F_r^2=\mu^2r^2S$ into~\eqref{grv:robust-budget}
gives~\eqref{grv:adaptive-stage-work}.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{grv:restarted}
In every dimension, $\mathbb E\|c_J-z_\star\|^2\le\varepsilon$. The method uses
$2k_{\rm rep}\sum_{j<J}b_jT_j$ calls. For a universal constant
$C_{\rm rst}>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{grv:restart-sums}
 \sum_{j<J}T_j\le C_{\rm rst}A_{\rm rst},\qquad
 \sum_{j<J}b_jT_j\le C_{\rm rst}\ell_0
 \Bigl(\rho A_{\rm rst}+\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2\varepsilon}\Bigr).
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
\emph{Accuracy.} Suppose $\|c_j-z_\star\|\le r_j$. Each copy ends within
$r_j/8$ of $z_\star$ with probability at least $15/16$, independently given
$c_j$. As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{grv:robust}, fewer than a quarter of the
copies fail with probability at least $1-e^{-k_{\rm rep}/8}$, and then
\eqref{grv:median-distance} gives $\|c_{j+1}-z_\star\|\le3r_j/8\le r_{j+1}$.
By the choice of $k_{\rm rep}$, each stage fails with probability at most
$\varepsilon/(50JR_0^2)$, so all stages succeed except with probability at most
$\varepsilon/(50R_0^2)$. On every history the copies stay in
$B(c_j,2r_j)$, hence so does their median, and
$\|c_J-z_\star\|\le R_0+2\sum_jr_j<5R_0$. The choice of $J$ gives
$\varepsilon/8<r_J^2\le\varepsilon/2$. Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E\|c_J-z_\star\|^2\le r_J^2+25R_0^2\cdot\frac\varepsilon{50R_0^2}\le\varepsilon .
\]

\emph{Work.} Since $\kappa_0\ge1$, $S_j\le(1+L_1r_j)^2+\kappa_0\le3\kappa_0+2L_1^2r_j^2$,
so $\sum_{j<J}S_j\le3\kappa_0J+\frac83a_0^2\le3A_{\rm rst}$, and
$\sum_{j<J}r_j^{-2}=(r_J^{-2}-R_0^{-2})/3<8/(3\varepsilon)$. Since
$S_j\le S_0$, \eqref{grv:adaptive-stage-work} gives~\eqref{grv:restart-sums}.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{ghs:upper}
For $j_{\rm sw}\in\{0,\ldots,J\}$, run stages $j<j_{\rm sw}$ on one
worker and stages $j\ge j_{\rm sw}$
with common queries. Then $\mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\le\varepsilon$, with
\begin{equation}\label{ghs:exact-budget}
 \Bigl\lceil\frac{2k_{\rm rep}}K\sum_{j<j_{\rm sw}}b_jT_j\Bigr\rceil
 +2k_{\rm rep}\sum_{j_{\rm sw}\le j<J}T_j
      \Bigl\lceil\frac{b_j}{mK}\Bigr\rceil
\end{equation}
rounds. Choosing $j_{\rm sw}$ to minimize~\eqref{ghs:exact-budget}, the number of
rounds is at most
\begin{equation}\label{ghs:rate}
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde O\Bigl(&1
 +\min\Bigl\{\frac\rho K,1+\frac\rho{mK}\Bigr\}
       \Bigl[a_0^2+\kappa_0\log\frac{2R_0^2}{\varepsilon}\Bigr]\\
 &+\min\Bigl\{\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2K\varepsilon},\
 \kappa_0+\frac{\sigma L_1}{\mu\sqrt K}
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\mu^2mK\varepsilon}\Bigr\}\Bigr)
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where the tilde hides only logarithmic factors in $2+a_0$, $2+\kappa_0$ and
$2R_0^2/\varepsilon$.
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
\emph{Accuracy and budget.} The way responses are distributed over workers
changes neither the stage algorithm nor the conditional moments, so
Theorem~\ref{grv:restarted} applies. The serial part needs
$\lceil(2k_{\rm rep}/K)\sum_{j<j_{\rm sw}}b_jT_j\rceil$ rounds, its last round
communicates $c_{j_{\rm sw}}$, and each pooled iteration needs
$2\lceil b_j/(mK)\rceil$ rounds; this is~\eqref{ghs:exact-budget}.

\emph{Cost per stage.} Let $\vartheta_1=\rho/K$,
$\vartheta_m=1+\rho/(mK)$, $U_j=L_1^2r_j^2+\kappa_0$ and
$V_j=\sigma^2/(\mu^2r_j^2)$, so that $S_j\le3U_j$. By
\eqref{grv:adaptive-stage-work} and $\lceil t\rceil\le1+t$,
for a universal constant $C_{\rm comm}>0$,
\eqref{ghs:exact-budget} is at most $C_{\rm comm}k_{\rm rep}\ell_0$ times
\begin{equation}\label{ghs:stage-cost}
 1+\vartheta_1\sum_{j<j_{\rm sw}}U_j
 +\vartheta_m\sum_{j_{\rm sw}\le j<J}U_j
 +\frac1K\sum_{j<j_{\rm sw}}V_j
 +\frac1{mK}\sum_{j_{\rm sw}\le j<J}V_j .
\end{equation}
We use $\sum_{j<J}U_j\le\frac43a_0^2+\kappa_0J$,
$\sum_{j_{\rm sw}\le j<J}U_j
\le\frac43L_1^2r_{j_{\rm sw}}^2+\kappa_0J$,
$\sum_{j<j_{\rm sw}}V_j
\le\sigma^2/(3\mu^2r_{j_{\rm sw}}^2)$ and
$\sum_{j<J}V_j\le8\sigma^2/(3\mu^2\varepsilon)$.

\emph{The case $\vartheta_1\ge\vartheta_m$.} Take $j_{\rm sw}=0$:
\eqref{ghs:stage-cost} is at most
$1+\vartheta_m\sum_jU_j+8\sigma^2/(3\mu^2mK\varepsilon)$, which is bounded
by~\eqref{ghs:rate}.

\emph{The case $\vartheta_1<\vartheta_m$.} Then $0<\vartheta_m-\vartheta_1\le1$
and~\eqref{ghs:stage-cost} is at most
\[
 1+\vartheta_1\sum_{j<J}U_j+\sum_{j_{\rm sw}\le j<J}U_j
 +\frac1K\sum_{j<j_{\rm sw}}V_j+\frac1{mK}\sum_{j<J}V_j .
\]
With $j_{\rm sw}=J$ the third term vanishes, and this gives the first entry of the
minimum in~\eqref{ghs:rate}. For the second entry, note that
$\sum_{j_{\rm sw}\le j<J}U_j\le\kappa_0J+\Lambda_{j_{\rm sw}}$ with
$\Lambda_{j_{\rm sw}}=\frac43L_1^2r_{j_{\rm sw}}^2$ for
$j_{\rm sw}<J$ and $\Lambda_J=0$, so it suffices to choose $j_{\rm sw}$ with
\[
 \Lambda_{j_{\rm sw}}+\frac1K\sum_{j<j_{\rm sw}}V_j
 \le\frac{8\sigma L_1}{3\mu\sqrt K}.
\]
If $L_1=0$, take $j_{\rm sw}=0$; if $\sigma=0$, take $j_{\rm sw}=J$.
Otherwise let $r_{\rm bal}^2=\sigma/(\mu L_1\sqrt K)$.
If $r_J^2<r_{\rm bal}^2<R_0^2$, take the unique
$j_{\rm sw}\in\{1,\ldots,J\}$ with
$r_{j_{\rm sw}}^2\le r_{\rm bal}^2<4r_{j_{\rm sw}}^2$; then the left side is at most
$\frac43L_1^2r_{\rm bal}^2
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{3\mu^2Kr_{j_{\rm sw}}^2}
\le\frac43L_1^2r_{\rm bal}^2
 +\frac{4\sigma^2}{3\mu^2Kr_{\rm bal}^2}
=\frac{8\sigma L_1}{3\mu\sqrt K}$.
If $r_{\rm bal}^2\ge R_0^2$, take $j_{\rm sw}=0$: the left side is
$\frac43L_1^2R_0^2\le\frac43L_1^2r_{\rm bal}^2
=\frac{4\sigma L_1}{3\mu\sqrt K}$. If
$r_{\rm bal}^2\le r_J^2$, take $j_{\rm sw}=J$: the left side is at most
$\frac{\sigma^2}{3\mu^2Kr_J^2}
\le\frac{\sigma^2}{3\mu^2Kr_{\rm bal}^2}
=\frac{\sigma L_1}{3\mu\sqrt K}$.
In all cases we obtain the second entry, with $\kappa_0J$ in place of
$\kappa_0$.

Finally $J$, $k_{\rm rep}$ and $\ell_0$ are logarithmic in $2R_0^2/\varepsilon$,
$2+a_0$ and $2+\kappa_0$, which gives~\eqref{ghs:rate}.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- corollary-12: body_md -->
\label{gs:rate-sgc}
Let $\sigma=0$, $\vartheta=\min\{\rho/K,1+\rho/(mK)\}$, let $C_{\rm comm}$ be
the constant in the proof of Theorem~\ref{ghs:upper}, and
$C_{\rm rate}=51C_{\rm comm}$. For every $N\ge1$ there is a number of stages
$J$ for which the method of Theorem~\ref{ghs:upper} uses at most $N$
rounds and
\begin{equation}\label{gs:rate-sgc-bound}
 \mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\le8R_0^2\cdot4^{-x},\qquad
 x=\min\Bigl\{\frac{N}{2C_{\rm rate}\ell_0(1+\vartheta a_0^2)},\
 \sqrt{\frac{N}{2C_{\rm rate}\ell_0\vartheta\kappa_0}}\Bigr\}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-12 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
For an integer $J\ge1$ take the target $\varepsilon_J=2R_0^2\cdot4^{-J}$; then
the method has $J$ stages and
$k_{\rm rep}=\lceil8\log(25J\cdot4^J)\rceil
\le8\log25+8(J-1)+8J\log4+1\le38J$.
With $\sigma=0$ the terms with $V_j$ in~\eqref{ghs:stage-cost} vanish, and the
choice $j_{\rm sw}=0$ if $\vartheta_1\ge\vartheta_m$ and $j_{\rm sw}=J$
otherwise, as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{ghs:upper}, bounds the number of
rounds by
\[
 C_{\rm comm}k_{\rm rep}\ell_0\Bigl[1+\vartheta\Bigl(\tfrac43a_0^2+\kappa_0J\Bigr)\Bigr]
 \le C_{\rm rate}\ell_0\bigl[J(1+\vartheta a_0^2)+\vartheta\kappa_0J^2\bigr].
\]
Let $J=\lfloor x\rfloor$. If $J\ge1$, each of the two parts of the right
side is at most $N/2$, so the method uses at most $N$ rounds, and
Theorem~\ref{grv:restarted} gives
$\mathbb E\|\widehat z-z_\star\|^2\le\varepsilon_J=2R_0^2\cdot4^{-J}\le8R_0^2\cdot4^{-x}$.
If $J=0$, the method returns $z_0$, and
$\|z_0-z_\star\|^2\le R_0^2\le8R_0^2\cdot4^{-x}$ because $x<1$.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:composite:variance}\label{lem:samples:variance}
\label{prop:composite-potential-main}
\label{interp:samples-subsection}
For every query $x$, conditionally on the history before the call,
\begin{equation*}
 \operatorname{Var}(\nabla f_\xi(x))
 \le4L_{\max}\min\{D_f(x,x_\star),D_f(x_\star,x)\}+2\sigma_\star^2.
\end{equation*}
Under interpolation, $4L_{\max}$ can be replaced by $2L_{\max}$ and the
last term vanishes.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
For a convex function with $L_{\max}$-Lipschitz gradient,
$\|\nabla f_\xi(x)-\nabla f_\xi(y)\|^2\le2L_{\max}D_{f_\xi}(x,y)$ for
both orders of $x$ and $y$. Moreover $\mathbb E D_{f_\xi}(x,y)=D_f(x,y)$: with
$e=x-y$,
$D_{f_\xi}(x,y)=\int_0^1\langle\nabla f_\xi(y+te)-\nabla f_\xi(y),e\rangle\,dt$,
the integrand is at most $L_{\max}t\|e\|^2$ in absolute value, and
Fubini's theorem and unbiasedness of $\nabla f_\xi$ apply. The variance
is at most the second moment about $\nabla f(x_\star)$, so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\nabla f_\xi(x))
 \le\mathbb E\|\nabla f_\xi(x)-\nabla f(x_\star)\|^2
 \le2\mathbb E\|\nabla f_\xi(x)-\nabla f_\xi(x_\star)\|^2
 +2\mathbb E\|\nabla f_\xi(x_\star)-\nabla f(x_\star)\|^2,
\]
and the last expectation is $\sigma_\star^2$
by~\eqref{eq:composite-root-variance-main}. Under interpolation
$\nabla f_\xi(x_\star)=\nabla f(x_\star)$ almost surely, and the factor two
is not needed. Each call uses an independent sample, which gives the
conditional statement.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
\label{thm:interp-main}\label{interp:accelerated}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:interp-main}, in every dimension,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(z_T)
 &\le\frac{10\Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2}{T(T+1)}\label{interp:main}\\
 &\le640\Bigl[R_0^2\Bigl(\frac{L_f}{T^2}+\frac{L_H}T
       +\frac{4L_{\max}}{bT}\Bigr)
       +\frac{\sqrt2\,\sigma_\star R_0}{\sqrt{bT}}\Bigr].\notag
\end{align}
The method uses $bT$ stochastic gradients and $2T-1$ evaluations of $H$.
Under interpolation, $4L_{\max}$ may be replaced by $2L_{\max}$.
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
If $\Gamma_{\rm amp}=0$, then $L_f=L_H=0$, so $\nabla f$ and $H$ are constant with zero
sum, and $\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}\equiv0$. Let $\Gamma_{\rm amp}>0$ and put
\[
 \delta_t=g_t-\nabla f(y_t),\qquad d_t=r_t-w_t,\qquad
 \omega_t=\frac2{t(t+1)} .
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:composite:variance} and independence within a batch,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[\delta_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E[\|\delta_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le a_\phi\phi(y_t)+\sigma_{\star,b}^2,
 \label{interp:variance}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal F_{t-1}$ is the history before the batch of step $t$. All
iterates have finite second moments by induction.

\emph{Step 1: the function part.} Since $z_t-y_t=-\alpha_td_t$ and
$z_t=(1-\alpha_t)z_{t-1}+\alpha_tw_t$, smoothness and convexity of $f$
give, for every $u$,
\begin{align*}
 f(z_t)&\le f(y_t)+\langle\nabla f(y_t),z_t-y_t\rangle
 +\frac{L_f\alpha_t^2}2\|d_t\|^2\notag\\
 &=(1-\alpha_t)\bigl[f(y_t)+\langle\nabla f(y_t),z_{t-1}-y_t\rangle\bigr]
 +\alpha_t\bigl[f(y_t)+\langle\nabla f(y_t),w_t-y_t\rangle\bigr]
 +\frac{L_f\alpha_t^2}2\|d_t\|^2\notag\\
 &\le(1-\alpha_t)f(z_{t-1})+\alpha_t\bigl[f(u)+\langle\nabla f(y_t),w_t-u\rangle\bigr]
 +\frac{L_f\alpha_t^2}2\|d_t\|^2 .
\end{align*}
Moreover
$\langle H(u),z_t-u\rangle-(1-\alpha_t)\langle H(u),z_{t-1}-u\rangle
=\alpha_t\langle H(u),w_t-u\rangle\le\alpha_t\langle H(w_t),w_t-u\rangle$
by monotonicity. Adding,
\[
 \mathcal M(z_t,u)-(1-\alpha_t)\mathcal M(z_{t-1},u)
 \le\alpha_t\langle H(w_t)+g_t,w_t-u\rangle
 -\alpha_t\langle\delta_t,w_t-u\rangle+\frac{L_f\alpha_t^2}2\|d_t\|^2 .
\]

\emph{Step 2: the extragradient part.} Expanding the squares in the
updates of $w_t$ and $r_{t+1}$,
\begin{align*}
 \eta_t\langle H(w_t)+g_t,w_t-u\rangle
 &=\frac{\|r_t-u\|^2-\|r_{t+1}-u\|^2}2
  -\frac{\|d_t\|^2}2-\frac{\|w_t-r_{t+1}\|^2}2\notag\\
 &\quad+\eta_t\langle H(w_t)-H(r_t),w_t-r_{t+1}\rangle,
\end{align*}
and Young's inequality bounds the last term by
$\frac12\eta_t^2L_H^2\|d_t\|^2+\frac12\|w_t-r_{t+1}\|^2$. For the noise,
\[
 -\langle\delta_t,w_t-u\rangle
 =\langle\delta_t,u-r_t\rangle+\langle\delta_t,d_t\rangle,\qquad
 \langle\delta_t,d_t\rangle\le2\eta_t\|\delta_t\|^2+\frac{\|d_t\|^2}{8\eta_t}.
\]

\emph{Step 3: one step.} Combining the last three displays, the
coefficient of $\|d_t\|^2$ is
$\frac{\alpha_t}{\eta_t}\bigl(-\frac38+\frac12(\eta_t^2L_H^2+L_f\alpha_t\eta_t)\bigr)$.
By~\eqref{interp:parameters}, $\eta_t^2L_H^2\le(TL_H/\Gamma_{\rm amp})^2\le1/4096$ and
$L_f\alpha_t\eta_t\le2L_f/\Gamma_{\rm amp}\le1/32$, so this coefficient is at most
$-\alpha_t/(4\eta_t)$, and for every $u$
\begin{align}\label{interp:onestep}
 \mathcal M(z_t,u)&\le(1-\alpha_t)\mathcal M(z_{t-1},u)
 +\frac{\alpha_t}{2\eta_t}\bigl(\|r_t-u\|^2-\|r_{t+1}-u\|^2\bigr)\notag\\
 &\quad-\frac{\alpha_t}{4\eta_t}\|d_t\|^2
       +2\alpha_t\eta_t\|\delta_t\|^2
       +\alpha_t\langle\delta_t,u-r_t\rangle.
\end{align}

\emph{Step 4: summation.} We have $\alpha_t/\omega_t=t$, $t/\eta_t=\Gamma_{\rm amp}$,
$(1-\alpha_t)/\omega_t=1/\omega_{t-1}$ for $t\ge2$, and $\alpha_1=1$.
Dividing~\eqref{interp:onestep} by $\omega_t$ and summing,
\begin{align}\label{interp:weighted}
 \frac{\mathcal M(z_t,u)}{\omega_t}
 +\frac{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}4\sum_{j\le t}\|d_j\|^2
 &\le\frac{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}2\bigl(\|x_0-u\|^2-\|r_{t+1}-u\|^2\bigr)
 +\frac2{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}\sum_{j\le t}j^2\|\delta_j\|^2
 +\sum_{j\le t}j\langle\delta_j,u-r_j\rangle .
\end{align}

\emph{Step 5: the noise is controlled by the gap at the root.} Since
$\phi$ is nonnegative and $L_f$-smooth, $\|\nabla\phi(z)\|^2\le2L_f\phi(z)$,
and therefore
$\phi(y)\le\phi(z)+\|\nabla\phi(z)\|\|y-z\|+\frac{L_f}2\|y-z\|^2
\le2\phi(z)+L_f\|y-z\|^2$. With $y_t-z_t=\alpha_td_t$,
\begin{equation}\label{interp:newaggregate}
 \phi(y_t)\le2\phi(z_t)+L_f\alpha_t^2\|d_t\|^2 .
\end{equation}
Let $V_t=\mathbb E\|\delta_t\|^2$, $p_t=\mathbb E\phi(z_t)/\omega_t$ and let the
accumulated step energy be
$\mathsf E_t^{\rm step}=\sum_{j\le t}\mathbb E\|d_j\|^2$. By~\eqref{interp:variance}
and~\eqref{interp:newaggregate},
\begin{equation}\label{interp:varianceused}
 V_t\le2a_\phi\omega_tp_t+a_\phi L_f\alpha_t^2\mathbb E\|d_t\|^2+\sigma_{\star,b}^2 .
\end{equation}
Take $u=x_\star$ in~\eqref{interp:weighted}: then
$\mathcal M(z_t,x_\star)=\phi(z_t)$ and the last sum has zero mean. Using
$j^2\omega_j\le2$, $j^2\alpha_j^2\le4$ and $\sum_{j\le t}j^2\le T^3$,
\begin{equation*}
 p_t+\frac{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}4\mathsf E_t^{\rm step}
 \le\frac{\Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2}2+\frac{8a_\phi}{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}\sum_{j\le t}p_j
 +\frac{8a_\phi L_f}{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}\mathsf E_t^{\rm step}
 +\frac{2\sigma_{\star,b}^2T^3}{\Gamma_{\rm amp}} .
\end{equation*}
By~\eqref{interp:parameters}, $a_\phi T\le \Gamma_{\rm amp}/64$,
$L_f\le \Gamma_{\rm amp}/64$ and
$\sigma_{\star,b}^2T^3\le \Gamma_{\rm amp}^2R_0^2/4096$; in particular
$8a_\phi L_f\le8\Gamma_{\rm amp}^2/64^2\le \Gamma_{\rm amp}^2/8$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{interp:closure}
 p_t+\frac{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}8\mathsf E_t^{\rm step}
 \le\Bigl(\frac12+\frac1{2048}\Bigr)\Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2
 +\frac{8a_\phi}{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}\sum_{j\le t}p_j .
\end{equation}
Let $p_{\max}=\max_{t\le T}p_t$. Since $8a_\phi T/\Gamma_{\rm amp}\le1/8$,
\eqref{interp:closure} at a maximizing index gives
$p_{\max}\le(\frac12+\frac1{2048})\Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2+\frac18p_{\max}$, so
$p_{\max}\le \Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2$, and then~\eqref{interp:closure} with $t=T$ gives
$\mathsf E_T^{\rm step}\le8R_0^2$. Consequently, by~\eqref{interp:varianceused},
\begin{align*}
 \mathsf V_{\rm wt}:=\sum_{t\le T}t^2V_t
 &\le4a_\phi T\Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2
 +4a_\phi L_f\mathsf E_T^{\rm step}+\sigma_{\star,b}^2T^3\notag\\
 &\le \Gamma_{\rm amp}^2R_0^2\Bigl(\frac4{64}+\frac{32}{4096}+\frac1{4096}\Bigr)
 \le \Gamma_{\rm amp}^2R_0^2 .
\end{align*}

\emph{Step 6: the gap.} Let $\|u-x_\star\|\le R_0$, so that
$\|x_0-u\|\le2R_0$. Write
$\sum_tt\langle\delta_t,u-r_t\rangle
=\langle\sum_tt\delta_t,u-x_\star\rangle+\sum_tt\langle\delta_t,x_\star-r_t\rangle$.
The second sum has zero mean, and the supremum of the first over $u$ is
$R_0\|\sum_tt\delta_t\|$, whose expectation is at most
$R_0\sqrt{\mathsf V_{\rm wt}}$ by
orthogonality of martingale differences. Taking the supremum
in~\eqref{interp:weighted} at $t=T$ and then the expectation,
\[
 \frac{\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(z_T)}{\omega_T}
 \le2\Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2
 +\frac{2\mathsf V_{\rm wt}}{\Gamma_{\rm amp}}
 +R_0\sqrt{\mathsf V_{\rm wt}}\le5\Gamma_{\rm amp}R_0^2,
\]
which is~\eqref{interp:main}. The second line follows from
$T(T+1)\ge T^2$ and the definition of $\Gamma_{\rm amp}$.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:composite-schedules-main}
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:interp-main}, an algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)=O\!\left(R_0^2
 \min\left\{\begin{aligned}
 &L_f+L_H,\\[-2pt]
 &\frac{L_f}{(KN)^2}+\frac{L_H+L_{\max}}{KN}
       +\frac{\sigma_\star}{R_0\sqrt{KN}}
 \end{aligned}\right\}\right)
 \label{eq:comm-upper-main}
\end{equation}
and, if $K\ge3$, also
$\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)=O\!\left(R_0^2\bigl(\frac{L_f}{N^2}
+\frac{L_H}N+\frac{L_{\max}}{mKN}+\frac{\sigma_\star}{R_0\sqrt{mKN}}\bigr)\right)$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
\emph{Initial point.} Let $\widetilde H(u)=H(u)-H(x_\star)$. Since
$\nabla f(x_\star)+H(x_\star)=0$,
$\mathcal M(x_0,u)=\phi(x_0)-\phi(u)+\langle\widetilde H(u),x_0-u\rangle$.
For $\|u-x_\star\|\le R_0$, monotonicity gives
$\langle\widetilde H(u),x_\star-u\rangle\le0$, hence
$\langle\widetilde H(u),x_0-u\rangle\le\langle\widetilde H(u),x_0-x_\star\rangle
\le L_HR_0^2$, and $\phi(x_0)\le L_fR_0^2/2$, $\phi(u)\ge0$. Thus
$\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(x_0)\le(L_f/2+L_H)R_0^2$.

\emph{Serial schedule.} One worker runs~\eqref{interp:algorithm} with $b=1$
and $T=\lfloor KN/3\rfloor$. Each step uses one gradient and at most two
evaluations of $H$, so the $3T\le KN$ calls can be split into rounds of
$K$ calls, the worker keeping its state across round boundaries. If
$KN\ge3$, then $T\ge KN/6$ and Theorem~\ref{thm:interp-main} gives the
second entry of~\eqref{eq:comm-upper-main}. If $KN<3$, the initial point
gives $(L_f/2+L_H)R_0^2$, which is at most twice the second entry.

\emph{Synchronized schedule.} Let $K\ge3$, $T=N$ and $b=m(K-2)\ge mK/3$.
At the start of round $t\ge2$ every worker knows
$r_{t-1},w_{t-1},z_{t-1},g_{t-1}$. It evaluates $H(w_{t-1})$ and computes
$r_t=r_{t-1}-\eta_{t-1}(H(w_{t-1})+g_{t-1})$, then evaluates $H(r_t)$,
computes $y_t$, and spends its remaining $K-2$ calls on independent
gradients at $y_t$. Averaging these gradients over the workers at the
end of the round gives $g_t$ with an independent batch of size $m(K-2)$, after
which all workers compute $w_t$ and $z_t$. In round $1$ only $H(r_1)$ is
needed. This reproduces~\eqref{interp:algorithm} with at most $K$ calls
per worker and round, and Theorem~\ref{thm:interp-main} gives the third
bound, since $4L_{\max}/(bN)\le12L_{\max}/(mKN)$ and
$\sigma_\star/\sqrt{bN}\le\sqrt3\,\sigma_\star/\sqrt{mKN}$.

The algorithm returns the candidate with the smallest bound.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{interp:separation}
There is a distribution of nonnegative convex $1$-smooth functions
$f_\xi$ on $\mathbb R$, all minimized at $0$, whose mean $f=\mathbb E f_\xi$ has
the unique minimizer $0$, such that no finite $\rho$ satisfies
$\mathbb E|f_\xi'(x)|^2\le\rho|f'(x)|^2$ for all $x$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
Let $U$ be uniform on $[0,1]$ and
\[
 f_U(x)=\tfrac12\min\{x,0\}^2+\tfrac12\max\{x-U,0\}^2,\qquad
 f_U'(x)=\min\{x,0\}+\max\{x-U,0\}.
\]
The derivative is continuous, nondecreasing and piecewise affine with
slopes $0$ and $1$, so every $f_U$ is convex, $1$-smooth, nonnegative,
and zero at $0$. For $0<x<1$,
\begin{equation*}
 f'(x)=\mathbb E f_U'(x)=\int_0^x(x-u)\,du=\frac{x^2}2,\qquad
 \mathbb E f_U'(x)^2=\int_0^x(x-u)^2\,du=\frac{x^3}3,
\end{equation*}
while $f'(x)=x$ for $x<0$ and $f'(x)=x-1/2$ for $x\ge1$. Hence $0$ is the
unique zero of $f'$. On $(0,1)$,
$\mathbb E f_U'(x)^2/f'(x)^2=4/(3x)\to\infty$ as $x\downarrow0$.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\label{comp-local:near}\label{thm:composite-local-resolvent}
If $N\ge D_{\rm loc}$, there is an algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} with output $\widehat x\in\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$ and
\begin{equation}\label{comp-local:near-bound}
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)\le16R_0^2\Bigl[{}
 &\frac{32D_{\rm loc}^2L_f}{N^2}
 +\frac{16D_{\rm loc}L_{\max}}{mKN}\\
 &+\frac{64J_{\rm loc}L_H}{KN}
 +\frac{2\sqrt{2D_{\rm loc}}\,\sigma_\star}{R_0\sqrt{mKN}}\Bigr].
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
\emph{Parameters.} Let $T=\lfloor N/D_{\rm loc}\rfloor\ge1$,
$B_{\rm loc}=K(D_{\rm loc}-1)$, so that
$64J_{\rm loc}\le B_{\rm loc}\le64J_{\rm loc}+K$, and
\begin{equation*}
 \vartheta_{\rm loc}=\frac{32J_{\rm loc}}{B_{\rm loc}}\le\frac12,\qquad
 \Gamma_{\rm loc}=8L_f+\frac{16L_{\max}T}b
 +\frac{2\sigma_\star T^{3/2}}{R_0\sqrt b}+\vartheta_{\rm loc}L_HT .
\end{equation*}
If $L_f=L_{\max}=L_H=0$, the operator $G$ is constant and has a root, so
$G\equiv0$ and we return $x_0$. Otherwise $\Gamma_{\rm loc}>0$.

\emph{The method.} Set $z_0=r_1=x_0$ and, for $t=1,\ldots,T$,
\begin{equation*}
 \alpha_t=\frac2{t+1},\quad\eta_t=\frac t{\Gamma_{\rm loc}},\quad
 y_t=(1-\alpha_t)z_{t-1}+\alpha_tr_t,\quad
 z_t=(1-\alpha_t)z_{t-1}+\alpha_tw_t,\quad r_{t+1}=w_t .
\end{equation*}
In the first round of window $t$, every worker makes $K$ independent gradient
calls at $y_t$, and one worker receives their average $c_t$. In the
remaining $D_{\rm loc}-1$ rounds this worker approximately solves the VI on
$\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$ with the operator
\begin{equation}\label{comp-local:inner-operator}
 A_t(w)=\frac{w-r_t}{\eta_t}+c_t+H(w),
\end{equation}
which is $(1/\eta_t)$-strongly monotone and $(1/\eta_t+L_H)$-Lipschitz, by
\[
 q_t=\Bigl\lceil8J_{\rm loc}
       \Bigl(1+\frac{L_Ht}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}\Bigr)\Bigr\rceil
\]
steps of projected extragradient from $r_t$ with step
$1/(4(1/\eta_t+L_H))$. Its last point is $w_t$, broadcast at the end of the
window. All iterates lie in $\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$.

\emph{Budget.} Since
$L_Ht/\Gamma_{\rm loc}\le L_HT/\Gamma_{\rm loc}\le1/\vartheta_{\rm loc}$
and $16J_{\rm loc}/\vartheta_{\rm loc}=B_{\rm loc}/2$, the local solve uses
$2q_t\le16J_{\rm loc}+16J_{\rm loc}/\vartheta_{\rm loc}+2
\le B_{\rm loc}$ evaluations of $H$,
which fit into the $D_{\rm loc}-1$ rounds. Since $TD_{\rm loc}\le N$, the
whole method uses at most $N$ rounds and at most $K$ calls per worker and
round.

\emph{Gradient noise.} Let $\delta_t=c_t-\nabla f(y_t)$ and let
$\mathcal F_{t-1}$ be the history before the batch at $y_t$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:composite:variance} with $D_f(x_\star,y_t)$,
\begin{equation}\label{comp-local:variance}
 \mathbb E[\delta_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E[\|\delta_t\|^2\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le\frac{4L_{\max}}bD_f(x_\star,y_t)
 +\frac{2\sigma_\star^2}b .
\end{equation}

\emph{Accuracy of the local solve.} Let $w_t^\star$ be the solution of the
VI with $A_t$ on $\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$; it depends continuously on $c_t$.
By~\eqref{comp-local:peg}, with $\gamma\mu=1/(4(1+\eta_tL_H))$ and
$\eta_tL_H=L_Ht/\Gamma_{\rm loc}$,
\begin{equation*}
 \|w_t-w_t^\star\|\le4R_0\exp\Bigl(-\frac{q_t}{8(1+L_Ht/\Gamma_{\rm loc})}\Bigr)
 \le4R_0e^{-J_{\rm loc}}.
\end{equation*}
Let $R_t=\max_{v\in\mathcal X_{\rm loc}}\langle A_t(w_t),w_t-v\rangle\ge0$. Since
$g_\star+H(x_\star)=0$,
\[
 A_t(w)=\frac{w-r_t}{\eta_t}+(c_t-g_\star)
 +\bigl(H(w)-H(x_\star)\bigr),
\]
and pathwise
$\|c_t-g_\star\|
\le\|\frac1b\sum_j(\nabla f_{\xi_j}(y_t)-\nabla f_{\xi_j}(x_\star))\|
+\|\frac1b\sum_j\nabla f_{\xi_j}(x_\star)-g_\star\|$, where the first
term is
at most $3L_{\max}R_0$ and the second has expectation at most
$\sigma_\star/\sqrt b$. Hence
\[
 \mathbb E\sup_{w\in\mathcal X_{\rm loc}}\|A_t(w)\|
 \le\Bigl(\frac4{\eta_t}+3L_{\max}+3L_H\Bigr)R_0+\frac{\sigma_\star}{\sqrt b},
\]
and~\eqref{comp-local:residual-distance} with $L_A=1/\eta_t+L_H$ gives
\[
 \mathbb E R_t\le4R_0e^{-J_{\rm loc}}
 \Bigl[\Bigl(\frac8{\eta_t}+7L_H+3L_{\max}\Bigr)R_0
 +\frac{\sigma_\star}{\sqrt b}\Bigr]
 \le4\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2e^{-J_{\rm loc}}
 \Bigl[8+\frac7{\vartheta_{\rm loc}T}
 +\frac{3b}{16T}+\frac1{2T^{3/2}}\Bigr],
\]
using $1/\eta_t=\Gamma_{\rm loc}/t\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}$,
$L_H\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}/(\vartheta_{\rm loc}T)$,
$L_{\max}\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}b/(16T)$ and
$\sigma_\star\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0\sqrt b/(2T^{3/2})$. Since
$1/\vartheta_{\rm loc}=B_{\rm loc}/(32J_{\rm loc})\le2+K/32$,
the bracket is at most
$32+6b+14K$, and the
choice of $J_{\rm loc}$ gives
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E R_t\le\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2}{16N^2}
 \le\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2}{T^2}.
\end{equation*}

\emph{One outer step.} Let $h_t=w_t-r_t$ and $u\in\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$. As in
Step~1 of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:interp-main}, but keeping the
Bregman term from convexity,
\[
 \mathcal M(z_t,u)-(1-\alpha_t)\mathcal M(z_{t-1},u)
 \le\alpha_t\langle\nabla f(y_t)+H(w_t),w_t-u\rangle
 +\frac{L_f\alpha_t^2}2\|h_t\|^2-\alpha_tD_f(u,y_t).
\]
By~\eqref{comp-local:inner-operator},
$\nabla f(y_t)+H(w_t)=A_t(w_t)-h_t/\eta_t-\delta_t$. Here
$\langle A_t(w_t),w_t-u\rangle\le R_t$;
$-\langle h_t,w_t-u\rangle=\frac12(\|r_t-u\|^2-\|w_t-u\|^2-\|h_t\|^2)$ with
$w_t=r_{t+1}$; and
$-\langle\delta_t,w_t-u\rangle=\langle\delta_t,u-r_t\rangle-\langle\delta_t,h_t\rangle$
with $-\langle\delta_t,h_t\rangle\le2\eta_t\|\delta_t\|^2+\|h_t\|^2/(8\eta_t)$.
The coefficient of $\|h_t\|^2$ is
$\frac{\alpha_t}{\eta_t}(-\frac38+\frac{L_f\alpha_t\eta_t}2)\le-\frac{\alpha_t}{4\eta_t}$,
since $\alpha_t\eta_t\le2/\Gamma_{\rm loc}$ and
$L_f\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}/8$. Hence
\begin{align*}
 \mathcal M(z_t,u)\le{}&(1-\alpha_t)\mathcal M(z_{t-1},u)
 +\frac{\alpha_t}{2\eta_t}\bigl(\|r_t-u\|^2-\|r_{t+1}-u\|^2\bigr)
 -\frac{\alpha_t}{4\eta_t}\|h_t\|^2\notag\\
 &+2\alpha_t\eta_t\|\delta_t\|^2
 +\alpha_t\langle\delta_t,u-r_t\rangle
 -\alpha_tD_f(u,y_t)+\alpha_tR_t .
\end{align*}
With $\omega_t=2/(t(t+1))$, dividing by $\omega_t$ and summing as in Step~4
of the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:interp-main},
\begin{align}\label{comp-local:telescope}
 \frac{T(T+1)}2\mathcal M(z_T,u)\le{}&\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}2\|x_0-u\|^2
 +\sum_{t=1}^T\Bigl[-\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}4\|h_t\|^2
 +\frac{2t^2}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}\|\delta_t\|^2
 +t\langle\delta_t,u-r_t\rangle-tD_f(u,y_t)+tR_t\Bigr].
\end{align}

\emph{Noise energy.} Let
$\mathsf R_{\rm wt}=\sum_tt\,\mathbb E R_t\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2$,
$\mathsf B_t=\mathbb E D_f(x_\star,y_t)$,
$V_t=\mathbb E\|\delta_t\|^2$ and
$\mathsf V_{\rm wt}=\sum_tt^2V_t$. By~\eqref{comp-local:variance},
$V_t\le A_\phi\mathsf B_t+\sigma_{\rm bat}^2$ with
$A_\phi=4L_{\max}/b$ and $\sigma_{\rm bat}^2=2\sigma_\star^2/b$, and the
parameters satisfy $\Gamma_{\rm loc}\ge4A_\phi T$ and
$\Gamma_{\rm loc}\ge\sqrt2\,\sigma_{\rm bat}T^{3/2}/R_0$.
Take $u=x_\star$ in~\eqref{comp-local:telescope}:
the left side is nonnegative and the inner products have zero mean, so
\[
 \sum_tt\mathsf B_t\le\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}2R_0^2
 +\frac2{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}\sum_tt^2V_t+\mathsf R_{\rm wt}
 \le\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}2R_0^2
 +\frac{2A_\phi T}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}\sum_tt\mathsf B_t
 +\frac{2\sigma_{\rm bat}^2T^3}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}+\mathsf R_{\rm wt},
\]
and $2A_\phi T/\Gamma_{\rm loc}\le1/2$ gives
$\sum_tt\mathsf B_t\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2+2\mathsf R_{\rm wt}
+4\sigma_{\rm bat}^2T^3/\Gamma_{\rm loc}$.
Therefore
\[
 \mathsf V_{\rm wt}\le A_\phi T\sum_tt\mathsf B_t+\sigma_{\rm bat}^2T^3
 \le\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}^2R_0^2}4
 +\frac{\Gamma_{\rm loc}\mathsf R_{\rm wt}}2+2\sigma_{\rm bat}^2T^3
 \le\frac74\Gamma_{\rm loc}^2R_0^2 .
\]

\emph{The gap.} For $\|u-x_\star\|\le R_0$ we have $\|x_0-u\|\le2R_0$. Split
$\langle\delta_t,u-r_t\rangle=\langle\delta_t,u-x_\star\rangle
+\langle\delta_t,x_\star-r_t\rangle$, drop the nonpositive terms, take the
supremum over $u$ and then the expectation, and use
$\mathbb E\|\sum_tt\delta_t\|\le\sqrt{\mathsf V_{\rm wt}}$:
\[
 \frac{T(T+1)}2\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(z_T)
 \le2\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2
 +\frac{2\mathsf V_{\rm wt}}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}
 +R_0\sqrt{\mathsf V_{\rm wt}}+\mathsf R_{\rm wt}
 \le8\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2 .
\]
Thus $\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(z_T)\le16\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2/(T(T+1))$.
Finally $T\ge N/(2D_{\rm loc})$, $T+1\ge N/D_{\rm loc}$ and
$\vartheta_{\rm loc}D_{\rm loc}\le64J_{\rm loc}/K$; substituting $\Gamma_{\rm loc}$
gives~\eqref{comp-local:near-bound}.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{comp-local:uniform}
If $N\ge D_{\rm loc}$, there is an algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} with
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)=O\!\Biggl(R_0^2\Bigl[
 \frac{D_{\rm loc}^2L_f}{N^2}+\frac{J_{\rm loc}L_H}{KN}
 +\sqrt{\frac{D_{\rm loc}L_{\max}L_f}{mKN}}\Bigr]
 +\sigma_\star R_0\sqrt{\frac{D_{\rm loc}}{mKN}}\Biggr).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
On $\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$,
$D_f(x_\star,y)\le\frac{L_f}2\|y-x_\star\|^2\le\frac92L_fR_0^2$,
so by~\eqref{comp-local:variance} the batch variance is at most
$s_0^2=(18L_{\max}L_fR_0^2+2\sigma_\star^2)/b$. Use the method of
Theorem~\ref{comp-local:near} with
$\Gamma_{\rm loc}=8L_f+2s_0T^{3/2}/R_0+\vartheta_{\rm loc}L_HT$.
If $L_f=L_H=0$, the operator $G$ is
constant with a root, hence zero, and we return $x_0$. Otherwise the
budget calculation is unchanged. Now
$\|c_t-g_\star\|\le\|c_t-\nabla f(y_t)\|+3L_fR_0$, so
\[
 \mathbb E R_t\le4\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2e^{-J_{\rm loc}}
 \Bigl[8+\frac{3L_f}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}
 +\frac{7L_H}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}}+\frac{s_0}{\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0}\Bigr]
 \le4\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2e^{-J_{\rm loc}}(32+6mK+14K),
\]
because $L_f/\Gamma_{\rm loc}\le1/8$,
$L_H/\Gamma_{\rm loc}\le1/(\vartheta_{\rm loc}T)$ and
$s_0/(\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0)\le1/(2T^{3/2})$; hence again
$\mathsf R_{\rm wt}\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2$. The uniform variance bound
gives directly
$\mathsf V_{\rm wt}\le s_0^2T^3\le \Gamma_{\rm loc}^2R_0^2/4$, and the last
step of the proof of Theorem~\ref{comp-local:near} gives
$\frac{T(T+1)}2\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(z_T)
\le4\Gamma_{\rm loc}R_0^2$. Substituting $\Gamma_{\rm loc}$ and the
bounds on $T$, $D_{\rm loc}$ and $\vartheta_{\rm loc}$ proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{comp-pool:theorem}
For every $m,K\ge1$ and $N\ge2$ there is an algorithm of
Definition~\ref{def:ic-main} with
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)\le CR_0^2
 \min\Bigl\{L_f+L_H,\ L_f+\frac{L_H}{KN}
 +\sqrt{\frac{L_{\max}L_f}{mKN}}+\frac{\sigma_\star}{R_0\sqrt{mKN}}\Bigr\},
\end{equation*}
where $C$ is a universal constant.
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
\emph{Linearization at $x_0$.} Let $g_{\rm init}=\nabla f(x_0)$. For
$z,u\in\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$, smoothness and convexity give
$f(z)\le f(x_0)+\langle g_{\rm init},z-x_0\rangle+2L_fR_0^2$ and
$f(u)\ge f(x_0)+\langle g_{\rm init},u-x_0\rangle$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{comp-pool:transfer}
 f(z)-f(u)\le\langle g_{\rm init},z-u\rangle+2L_fR_0^2 .
\end{equation}

\emph{The initial point and small budgets.} The initial point gives
$(L_f/2+L_H)R_0^2$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:composite-schedules-main}). If
$KN<8$, this is at most $8R_0^2(L_f+L_H/(KN))$.

\emph{Pooled gradient.} Let $KN\ge8$. During the first $n_g=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\ge N/3$
rounds all workers sample gradients at $x_0$; denote the average formed
at the end by $g_{\rm pool}$ and set
$Q_{\rm pool}=mKn_g\ge mKN/3$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:composite:variance} and $D_f(x_\star,x_0)\le L_fR_0^2/2$,
\begin{equation}\label{comp-pool:mean-error}
 \mathbb E\|g_{\rm pool}-g_{\rm init}\|
 \le\sqrt{\frac{2L_{\max}L_fR_0^2+2\sigma_\star^2}{Q_{\rm pool}}}.
\end{equation}

\emph{Local solve.} If $L_H>0$, during the remaining $n_h=\lceil N/2\rceil$
rounds one worker runs projected mirror-prox~\citep{nemirovski2004} for
the operator $H+g_{\rm pool}$ on $\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$ from $x_0$,
with step $1/(2L_H)$ and
$T=\lfloor Kn_h/2\rfloor\ge KN/8$ steps of two evaluations of $H$ each.
Its averaged point $z$ satisfies, for all $u\in\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$,
\[
 \langle H(u)+g_{\rm pool},z-u\rangle
 \le\frac{L_H\|x_0-u\|^2}T\le\frac{32L_HR_0^2}{KN}.
\]
If $L_H=0$, one evaluation gives the constant $H\equiv h$, and $z$ is chosen
to minimize $\langle h+g_{\rm pool},z\rangle$ over $\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$,
so that the same
inequality holds with right side $0$.

\emph{The gap.} For $\|u-x_\star\|\le R_0$, both $u$ and $z$ lie in
$\mathcal X_{\rm loc}$ and $\|z-u\|\le4R_0$. By~\eqref{comp-pool:transfer},
\[
 \mathcal M(z,u)\le\langle H(u)+g_{\rm pool},z-u\rangle
 +\langle g_{\rm init}-g_{\rm pool},z-u\rangle+2L_fR_0^2
 \le\frac{32L_HR_0^2}{KN}
 +4R_0\|g_{\rm init}-g_{\rm pool}\|+2L_fR_0^2 .
\]
The right side does not depend on $u$. Taking the expectation and
using~\eqref{comp-pool:mean-error} with $Q_{\rm pool}\ge mKN/3$,
\[
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(z)\le2L_fR_0^2+\frac{32L_HR_0^2}{KN}
 +4\sqrt6\,R_0^2\sqrt{\frac{L_{\max}L_f}{mKN}}
 +\frac{4\sqrt6\,\sigma_\star R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}} .
\]
The algorithm returns the better of $z$ and $x_0$.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
The single-worker entry and the cap $L_f+L_H$ are given by
Proposition~\ref{prop:composite-schedules-main}. For the pooled entry let
$Q_{\rm tot}=mKN$. Then $J_{\rm loc}=O(\log(2Q_{\rm tot}))$ and
$D_{\rm loc}=O(1+\log(2Q_{\rm tot})/K)$; in particular,
$D_{\rm loc}=O(\log(2Q_{\rm tot}))$.

If $N\ge D_{\rm loc}$, the better of Theorem~\ref{comp-local:near} and
Lemma~\ref{comp-local:uniform} gives
\[
 R_0^2\Bigl[\frac{L_f}{N^2}+\frac{L_H}{KN}
 +\min\Bigl\{\frac{L_{\max}}{Q_{\rm tot}},
       \sqrt{\frac{L_{\max}L_f}{Q_{\rm tot}}}\Bigr\}\Bigr]
 +\frac{\sigma_\star R_0}{\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}}
\]
up to powers of $\log(2Q_{\rm tot})$.

If $N<D_{\rm loc}$, then $N^2=O(\log^2(2Q_{\rm tot}))$; consequently,
the $L_f$ fallback is
$O(\log^2(2Q_{\rm tot})\,L_f/N^2)$. Moreover
$\sqrt{L_{\max}L_f/Q_{\rm tot}}
\le L_f+\min\{L_{\max}/Q_{\rm tot},
\sqrt{L_{\max}L_f/Q_{\rm tot}}\}$: if
$L_{\max}/Q_{\rm tot}\le L_f$, the square root is at most $L_f$,
and otherwise it is
the minimum. Hence Lemma~\ref{comp-pool:theorem} gives the same expression
up to powers of $\log(2Q_{\rm tot})$. This holds for every $N\ge2$ and
without any
condition on $L_{\max}/L_f$.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{interp:quadratic-depth}
For integers $m,n_{\rm dep}\ge1$ and $\lambda,R_0>0$ there is a fixed distribution
of convex $\lambda$-smooth quadratics $f\ge0$, each with a unique
minimizer of norm $R_0$, such that every algorithm with $n_{\rm dep}$ batches of
at most $m$ simultaneous exact gradient (and value) queries satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\bigl[f(\widehat v)-\min f\bigr]\ge
 \frac{\lambda R_0^2}{288\,n_{\rm dep}^2}.
\end{equation*}
The dimension is
$d_{\rm ref}(m,2n_{\rm dep})/2\le2048m n_{\rm dep}^2$.
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
Take the distribution of~\eqref{interp:comm-affine-input} with
$B_0=2n_{\rm dep}$
and $\lambda_0=\sqrt\lambda$, and let
$f(v)=\frac12\|M_{\rm quad}v+b_{\rm quad}\|^2$. Its Hessian
$M_{\rm quad}^2$ has norm $\lambda$, and its minimizer
$-M_{\rm quad}^{-1}b_{\rm quad}$ has norm $R_0$. A
batch of gradient queries at points $v_i$ is answered by two batches of
queries to $G_{\rm quad}$: the query $G_{\rm quad}(0,v_i)$ returns
$r_i=M_{\rm quad}v_i+b_{\rm quad}$, hence
$f(v_i)=\|r_i\|^2/2$, and the query $G_{\rm quad}(r_i,0)$ returns
$-M_{\rm quad}r_i=-\nabla f(v_i)$.
After $2n_{\rm dep}$ batches, output $(0,\widehat v)$;
\eqref{interp:comm-affine-input} gives
$\mathbb E\|M_{\rm quad}\widehat v+b_{\rm quad}\|
\ge\sqrt\lambda R_0/(12n_{\rm dep})$, and Jensen's
inequality gives
$\mathbb E[f(\widehat v)-\min f]
=\frac12\mathbb E\|M_{\rm quad}\widehat v+b_{\rm quad}\|^2
\ge\lambda R_0^2/(288n_{\rm dep}^2)$.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
\label{thm:comm-main}\label{interp:communication-lower}
Let $0<\lambda\le L_f\le L_{\max}$, $p=\lambda/L_{\max}$, and
\begin{equation*}
 n_{\rm dep}=\min\bigl\{KN,\ \max\{1,\lceil2N\beta_p\rceil\}\bigr\}.
\end{equation*}
There is a fixed distribution of instances of
Assumption~\ref{ass:interp-main} with $H=0$ and $\sigma_\star=0$, whose
mean $f$ is a convex $\lambda$-smooth quadratic and whose samples are
nonnegative, convex and $L_{\max}$-smooth, such that every algorithm
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)
 \ge\frac{\lambda R_0^2}{576\,n_{\rm dep}^2}
 \ge\frac{\lambda R_0^2}{2304\,(1+N\beta_p)^2}
 \label{interp:comm-clock-lower}
 \ge\frac{\lambda R_0^2}{36864\,[1+ND_{\mathrm{bin}}(m,K,p)]^2},
\end{equation}
where $D_{\mathrm{bin}}(m,K,p)$ is defined in~\eqref{eq:clock:explicit-app}. The dimension is at
most $2048m(KN)^2$, and the bound holds even if the masks and the sample
values are revealed.
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
Draw $f$ from Lemma~\ref{interp:quadratic-depth} with depth $n_{\rm dep}$,
and let
every call use the sample
\begin{equation*}
 f_{\rm samp}(x)=\frac{B_{\rm mask}}p f(x),\qquad
 B_{\rm mask}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\ \text{independent}.
\end{equation*}
Each sample is nonnegative, convex and $\lambda/p=L_{\max}$-smooth, its
mean is $f$, and all samples vanish at the minimizer $x_\star$ of $f$. This
oracle is masked with probability $p$ in the sense of
Section~\ref{sec:relative-minimax}, and calls to $H=0$ give no information.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:masked:simulation}(iii) with
$\ell_{\rm dep}=\lambda R_0^2/(288n_{\rm dep}^2)$, every algorithm has expected
loss at least $\lambda R_0^2/(576n_{\rm dep}^2)$ for the loss
$f(\widehat x)-\min f$, which equals
$\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)$ because $H=0$ and $x_\star$ is an admissible
comparator. Finally $n_{\rm dep}\le2(1+N\beta_p)$ and
$\beta_p\le4D_{\mathrm{bin}}(m,K,p)$
by Theorem~\ref{thm:clock:asymptotic}.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{prop:composite-full-noise-lower}
\label{prop:composite-root-noise}\label{comp-local:noise-lower}
For $\nu\ge0$,
\begin{equation*}
 \mathfrak R_{\rm comp}(\nu)\ge\frac7{2048}
 \min\Bigl\{(L_f+L_H)R_0^2,\ \frac{\nu R_0}{\sqrt{mKN}}\Bigr\}.
\end{equation*}
The instances are one-dimensional and have root noise exactly $\nu^2$.
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
Let $\nu>0$, $Q_{\rm tot}=mKN$, and
$\theta_{\rm test}\in\{-R_0/2,R_0/2\}$. We use two
families, each only when its budget is positive.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,nosep]
\item[(a)] If $L_f>0$:
$\lambda=\min\{L_f,\nu/(4R_0\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}})\}$,
draw $\zeta\sim\mathcal N(\lambda\theta_{\rm test},\nu^2)$, and set
$f_\zeta(x)=\frac\lambda2(x-\zeta/\lambda)^2$ and $H=0$. The samples are
$\lambda$-smooth with $\lambda\le L_f\le L_{\max}$, and
$f(x)=\frac\lambda2(x-\theta_{\rm test})^2+{\rm const}$.
\item[(b)] If $L_H>0$:
$\lambda=\min\{L_H,\nu/(4R_0\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}})\}$,
draw $\zeta\sim\mathcal N(\lambda\theta_{\rm test},\nu^2)$, and set
$f_\zeta(x)=-\zeta x$ and $H(x)=\lambda x$. The samples are affine, so $L_f$ and
$L_{\max}$ may be zero, $H$ is $\lambda$-Lipschitz with $\lambda\le L_H$,
and $f(x)=-\lambda\theta_{\rm test}x$.
\end{itemize}
In both families $G(x)=\lambda(x-\theta_{\rm test})$, the root is $\theta_{\rm test}$,
and
$\nabla f_\zeta(\theta_{\rm test})+H(\theta_{\rm test})
=\lambda\theta_{\rm test}-\zeta$ has variance $\nu^2$.
Write $L_{\rm active}$ for $L_f$ in family (a) and for $L_H$ in family (b).

Every response is a known function of the query and of $\zeta$, so the
algorithm learns at most $Q_{\rm tot}$ independent observations of
$\zeta\sim\mathcal N(\lambda\theta_{\rm test},\nu^2)$. Define the mean
separation $\mu_{\rm obs}=\lambda R_0/2$. Then
$\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}\,\mu_{\rm obs}/\nu\le1/8$, so by
Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-testing} the sign of $\widehat x$ differs from
the sign of $\theta_{\rm test}$ with average probability at least $7/16$;
then $|\widehat x-\theta_{\rm test}|\ge R_0/2$. In (a),
$\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)=\frac\lambda2(\widehat x-\theta_{\rm test})^2
\ge\lambda R_0^2/8$.
In (b), reparametrize the comparator as
$w=u_{\rm cmp}-\theta_{\rm test}$:
\[
 \operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)
 =\sup_{|w|\le R_0}\lambda
   \bigl[w(\widehat x-\theta_{\rm test})-w^2\bigr]
 \ge\lambda\Bigl[\frac{R_0}4|\widehat x-\theta_{\rm test}|
   -\frac{R_0^2}{16}\Bigr]
 \ge\frac{\lambda R_0^2}{16},
\]
taking
$w=\frac{R_0}4\operatorname{sign}(\widehat x-\theta_{\rm test})$.
Hence one sign of $\theta_{\rm test}$ gives
$\mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)\ge\frac7{16}\cdot\frac{\lambda R_0^2}{16}
\ge\frac7{1024}\min\{L_{\rm active}R_0^2,
\nu R_0/\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}\}$ for each family that is available; a family
with $L_{\rm active}=0$ would only give the bound $0$. Finally, with
$R_{\rm noise}=\nu R_0/\sqrt{Q_{\rm tot}}$,
\[
 \max_{L_{\rm active}\in\{L_f,L_H\}}
 \min\{L_{\rm active}R_0^2,R_{\rm noise}\}
 \ge\frac12\min\{(L_f+L_H)R_0^2,R_{\rm noise}\}.
\]
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
\label{comp-proj:lower}
Let $Q_{\rm tot}\ge1$ be an integer, $L_f>0$, $L_H\ge0$ and
$L_{\max}>Q_{\rm tot}L_f$. For every algorithm that makes at most
$Q_{\rm tot}$ stochastic gradient calls, with
arbitrary queries, sequential access and free access to $H$, there is
an instance of Assumption~\ref{ass:interp-main} with $\sigma_\star=0$ in
dimension $d=\lceil8192L_{\max}/L_f\rceil$ (and in every larger dimension)
such that
\begin{equation*}
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Gap}_{R_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}(\widehat x)
 \ge\frac{3}{512\sqrt{8193}}R_0^2
 \min\Bigl\{L_H,\sqrt{\frac{L_{\max}L_f}{Q_{\rm tot}}}\Bigr\}.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
If $L_H=0$ there is nothing to prove. Write
$L_{\rm samp}=L_{\max}$ and let
\[
 d=\Bigl\lceil\frac{8192L_{\rm samp}}{L_f}\Bigr\rceil,\qquad
 \lambda=\frac{4L_{\rm samp}}d\le L_f,\qquad
 \mu_{\rm ex}=\min\Bigl\{L_H,
 \frac{L_{\rm samp}}{32\sqrt{dQ_{\rm tot}}}\Bigr\}>0 .
\]

\emph{The instance.} Let $x_\star$ be uniform on the sphere of radius $R_0$
in $\mathbb R^d$. Every stochastic call draws, independently, the orthogonal
projector $\Pi_{\rm rnd}$ onto a uniformly distributed $4$-dimensional
subspace, and
returns the gradient of
\begin{equation*}
 f_{\Pi_{\rm rnd}}(x)
 =\frac{L_{\rm samp}}2\|\Pi_{\rm rnd}(x-x_\star)\|^2
 -\mu_{\rm ex}\langle x_\star,x\rangle,
 \qquad\text{while}\qquad H(x)=\mu_{\rm ex}x .
\end{equation*}
The samples are convex and $L_{\rm samp}$-smooth. Since
$\mathbb E \Pi_{\rm rnd}=\frac4dI$, the mean is
$f(x)=\frac\lambda2\|x-x_\star\|^2
-\mu_{\rm ex}\langle x_\star,x\rangle$,
which is $\lambda$-smooth, and
$G(x)=(\lambda+\mu_{\rm ex})(x-x_\star)$. Every sample satisfies
$\nabla f_{\Pi_{\rm rnd}}(x_\star)+H(x_\star)=0$, so $\sigma_\star=0$.
The map $H$ is known,
so calls to it carry no information.

\begin{revisionblock}
\begin{lemma}[Spherical posterior under equivariant observations]
\label{comp-proj:posterior}
Let $x_\star$ be uniform on the sphere of radius $R_0$ in $\mathbb R^d$.
Fix $q\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and deterministic scalars $a,b\in\mathbb R$.
Starting with $S=\{0\}$, repeat the following adaptive experiment. Given
the past, choose $x$, replace $S$ by $\operatorname{span}(S,x)$, and reveal
$\Pi_Sx_\star$. Then draw, independently of the past, a uniformly random
rank-$q$ orthogonal projector $P$, observe
$y=aP(x-x_\star)-b x_\star$, replace $S$ by
$\operatorname{span}(S,y)$, and again reveal $\Pi_Sx_\star$.
After either reveal, conditionally on the complete augmented transcript,
$(I-\Pi_S)x_\star$ is uniform on the sphere in $S^\perp$ of radius
$(R_0^2-\|\Pi_Sx_\star\|^2)^{1/2}$. The conclusion is unchanged if the
adaptive choices use independent internal randomness.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Condition on the internal random seed and argue by induction. The claim
is true initially. At a query step, $x$ is fixed by the past. Writing
$v=(I-\Pi_S)x$, revealing the new projection either changes nothing
when $v=0$ or conditions a uniform point of the sphere in $S^\perp$ on
its coordinate along $v$. The remaining component is therefore uniform
on the corresponding sphere in $\operatorname{span}(S,x)^\perp$.

After this enlargement, $x\in S$. Before the response is observed, the
conditional joint law of $(x_\star,P)$ is invariant under
$(x_\star,P)\mapsto(Qx_\star,QPQ^\top)$ for every orthogonal $Q$ fixing
$S$ pointwise, and the response map is equivariant:
$y(Qx_\star,QPQ^\top)=Qy(x_\star,P)$. Put
$S'=\operatorname{span}(S,y)$. After conditioning on $y$ and on the
revealed vector $\Pi_{S'}x_\star$, every orthogonal map fixing $S'$ pointwise
leaves all conditioned data unchanged. Hence the conditional law of
$(I-\Pi_{S'})x_\star$ is invariant under the full orthogonal group of
$S'^\perp$. Its norm is fixed by $\|x_\star\|=R_0$, so uniqueness of the
orthogonally invariant probability measure on a sphere makes this law
uniform. This proves the induction; averaging over the seed gives the
last assertion.
\end{proof}
\end{revisionblock}

\emph{A more informative experiment.} Let $\mathcal S_{\rm obs}$ be the
span of all stochastic queries and responses observed so far, and reveal
$\Pi_{\mathcal S_{\rm obs}}x_\star$ after every change of
$\mathcal S_{\rm obs}$: once when a query $x$ is chosen, and once after
its response
$y=L_{\rm samp}\Pi_{\rm rnd}(x-x_\star)-\mu_{\rm ex}x_\star$.
This can only help the algorithm,
and $\dim\mathcal S_{\rm obs}$ grows by at most two per call, so
$\dim\mathcal S_{\rm obs}\le2Q_{\rm tot}\le d/4096$ and
$d_\perp:=\dim\mathcal S_{\rm obs}^\perp\ge d/2$ throughout.
 
                                                   By Lemma~\ref{comp-proj:posterior}, conditionally on the
augmented history the unrevealed component   
$\Pi_{\mathcal S_{\rm obs}^\perp}x_\star$ is uniform
on the sphere of radius
$r=(R_0^2-\|\Pi_{\mathcal S_{\rm obs}}x_\star\|^2)^{1/2}$ in
$\mathcal S_{\rm obs}^\perp$.

\emph{Information revealed by a query.} The query direction is fixed
given the past, and a uniform point on a sphere of radius $r$ in
dimension $d_\perp$ has second moment $r^2/d_\perp$ in every direction. Hence adding
$x$ to $\mathcal S_{\rm obs}$ reveals in expectation at most
$r^2/d_\perp\le2r^2/d$.

\emph{Information revealed by a response.} After adding $x$, let
$\mathcal V_{\rm hid}=\mathcal S_{\rm obs}^\perp$,
$\Pi_{\mathcal V_{\rm hid}}x_\star=ru_{\rm hid}$ with
$\|u_{\rm hid}\|=1$, and $w=x-x_\star$, so that
$\Pi_{\mathcal V_{\rm hid}}w=-ru_{\rm hid}$ and $\|w\|\ge r$.
A uniform rank-four projector satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 \Pi_{\rm rnd}w=t\,w+\|w\|\sqrt{t(1-t)}\,e_{\rm tan},
\end{equation*}
with independent $t\sim\operatorname{Beta}(2,(d-4)/2)$ and
$e_{\rm tan}$ uniform on
the unit sphere of $w^\perp$. (Rotating $w/\|w\|$ to a coordinate axis,
$t=\|Pw\|^2/\|w\|^2$ is the squared norm of the projection of a uniform
unit vector onto a fixed $4$-dimensional subspace, a ratio of
